get.description:
Returns a list of all user resources.  The results can be
filtered, using the query parameters.

Results are returned in pages.
Each page of results includes the total results found, and
information for requesting the next page of results, using
the `skip` and `limit` query parameters.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter by the user's name

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Filter by the user's username

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Filter by the user's email

parameters.name: groups
parameters.description:
Filter by users in the given group name. Provide multiple groups seperated by comma(",")
to get users in all of those groups.
Using 'nil' as the group name will return users that are not part of any group.

parameters.name: exclude_groups
parameters.description: Users associated with given group will be excluded from the result. Provide multiple groups seperated by comma(",") to exclude multiple groups in the result.

parameters.name: auth_domain_name
parameters.description: Filter by the user's auth domain

parameters.name: account_expired
parameters.description: Filters the list of users whose expiration time has passed.

parameters.name: allowed_auth_methods
parameters.description:
Filter by the login authentication method allowed to the users.  
It is a comma seperated list of values.  
A special value `empty` can be specified to get users to whom no authentication method is allowed.

parameters.name: allowed_client_types
parameters.description:
Filter by the client types that can authenticate the user.
It is a comma separated list of values.

parameters.name: password_policy
parameters.description: Filter the list of users based on assigned password policy.

parameters.name: return_groups
parameters.description: If set to 'True', it returns the group's name in which user is associated along with all users information.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
Currently, sorting on following fields are supported : name,email,user_id,created_at,updated_at,logins_count,last_login,last_failed_login_at. 
For example:
     -name

...will sort the results first by `name`, descending.

allOf.description:
The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

skip.description:
The index of the first record returned.  Equivalent to 'offset' in
SQL.

limit.description: The max number of records returned.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL.

total.description: The total records matching the query.

messages.description: An optional list of warning messages, usually used to note when unsupported query parameters were ignored.

post.description:
Create a new user in a domain(including root), or add an existing domain user to a sub-domain.
Users are always created in the local, internal user database, but might
have references to external identity providers.

The `connection` property is optional. If this property is specified
when creating new users, it can be the name of a connection or
`local_account` for a local user.

The `connection` property is only used in the body of the create-user
request.  It is not present in either request or response bodies of
the other user endpoints.

To create a user -
`username` is mandatory. And
`password` is required in most cases except when certificate authentication is used and certificate subject dn 
is provided.

To enable certificate based authentication for a user,  it is required to set
`certificate_subject_dn` and add "user_certificate" authentication method in `allowed_auth_methods`.
This functionality is available only for local users.

To assign a root domain user to a sub-domain -
the users are added to the domain of the user who is logging in, and the `connection`
property should be left empty.  The `user_id` or `username` fields are
the only ones that are used while adding existing users to sub-domains;
all other fields are ignored.

To enable the two-factor authentication based on username-password and user certificate for a user, it is required to set
"certificate_subject_dn" and add "password_with_user_certificate" authentication method in "allowed_auth_methods". 
For authentication, the user will require both username-password and user certificate. This functionality applies only to local users.

username.description:
The login name of the user. This is the identifier used to login.

This attribute is required to create a user, but is omitted
when getting or listing user resources. It cannot be updated.

This attribute may also be used (instead of the user_id) when
adding an existing root domain user to a different domain.

password.description:
The password used to secure the users account. Allowed
passwords are defined by the password policy.

Password is optional when "certificate_subject_dn" is set and "user_certificate" is in 
allowed_auth_methods.In all other cases, password is required

It is not included in user resource responses.

connection.description:
This attribute is required to create a user, but is not
included in user resource responses. Can be the name of a
connection or "local_account" for a local user, defaults to
"local_account".

certificate_subject_dn.description: The Distinguished Name of the user in certificate

is_domain_user.description: This flag can be used to create the user in a non-root domain where user management is allowed.

enable_cert_auth.description:
**Deprecated**: Use `allowed_auth_methods` instead.  
If both `enable_cert_auth` and `allowed_auth_methods` are provided in the request, `enable_cert_auth` is ignored.  
Enable certificate based authentication flag.
If set to true, the user will be able to login using certificate.

user_metadata.description:
A schema-less object, which can be used by applications
to store information about the resource.
user_metadata is typically used by applications to store information about
the resource which the end-users are allowed to modify, such as
user preferences.

app_metadata.description:
A schema-less object, which can be used by applications to store
information about the resource.
app_metadata is typically used by applications to store information
which the end-users are not themselves allowed to change,
like group membership or security roles.

password_change_required.description:
Password change required flag.
If set to true, user will be required to change their password on next successful login.

user_id.description:
The user_id is the ID of an existing root domain user.
This field is used only when adding an existing root domain user to a different domain.

login_flags.description: Flags for controlling user's login behavior.

prevent_ui_login.description: If true, user is not allowed to login from Web UI. Default - false

allowed_auth_methods.description:
List of login authentication methods allowed to the user.  
Default value - ["password"]  i.e. Password Authentication is allowed by default.  
Setting it to empty, i.e `[]`, means no authentication method is allowed to the user.  
If both `enable_cert_auth` and `allowed_auth_methods` are provided in the request, `enable_cert_auth` is ignored.  
Setting it to ["password_with_user_certificate"], means two-factor authentication is enabled for the user. The
user will require both username-password and user_certificate for authentication.

Valid values in the array are:
- password
- user_certificate
- password_with_user_certificate

This property does not control login behavior for users in admin group.

expires_at.description:
The "expires_at" field is applicable only for local user account. Only members of the 'admin' and 'User Admins' groups can add expiration to an existing local user account or modify the expiration date.
Once the "expires_at" date is reached, the user account gets disabled and the user is not able to perform any actions.
Setting the "expires_at" field to empty, removes the expiration date of the user account.

The supported date-time format is
2025-03-02T06:13:27.71402Z

password_policy.description: The password policy applies only to local user accounts and overrides the global password policy. By default, the global password policy is applied to the users.

allowed_client_types.description:
List of client types that can authenticate using the user's credentials.  
Default value - ["unregistered", "public", "confidential"]  i.e. all clients can authenticate the user using user's credentials.  
Setting it to empty, i.e `[]`, means no client can authenticate this user, which effectively means no one can login into this user.  

Valid values in the array are:
- unregistered
- public
- confidential

This property does not control login behavior for users in admin group.

If the current user is logged into a sub-domain, the user is deleted from that sub-domain.
If the current user is logged into the root domain, the user is deleted from all domains it belongs to.

Change the current user's password. Can only be used to change the password
of the currently authenticated user. The user will not be able to change their password to the same password.

username.description: The login name of the current user.

auth_domain.description: The domain where user needs to be authenticated. This is the domain where user is created. Defaults to the root domain.

204.description: No Content | Successful password change.

parameters.description: An HTTP header carrying the API token. Format: `Bearer {token}`

patch.description: Change the current password policy for all users. Can only be used to by a member of the admin group. Currently, a single policy named 'global' is applied to all users.

inclusive_min_upper_case.description: The minimum number of upper cases

inclusive_min_lower_case.description: The minimum number of lower cases

inclusive_min_other.description: The minimum number of other characters

inclusive_min_total_length.description: The minimum length of the password. Value 0 is ignored.

inclusive_max_total_length.description: Specifies the maximum length of the password. Setting the value to 0 indicates that the property isn't enforced, therefore the password can be of any length.

password_history_threshold.description: Determines the number of past passwords a user cannot reuse. Even with value 0, the user will not be able to change their password to the same password.

password_lifetime.description: The maximum lifetime of the password in days. Value 0 is ignored.

password_change_min_days.description: The minimum period in days between password changes. Value 0 is ignored.

failed_logins_lockout_thresholds.description:
List of lockout durations in minutes for failed login attempts.
For example, with input of [0, 5, 30], the first failed login attempt with duration of zero will not lockout the user account,
the second failed login attempt will lockout the account for 5 minutes,
the third and subsequent failed login attempts will lockout for 30 minutes.
Set an empty array '[]' to disable the user account lockout.

password_expiry_notification_days.description:
Determines number of days before password expiry when notification(s) would be sent to user.  

Login banner would be shown to user on UI if password expiry duration is less than 
`password_expiry_notification_days`.  

If SMTP server is configured, email notification would be sent daily to users notifying need to 
change their password soon.  

Value should be less than password_lifetime.  
Valid values are between 0 and 30. Value of 0 would disable notification. Default value is 14.  

Example:  
If password_lifetime is set to 20 and password_expiry_notification_days is set to 10, 
then user will observe banner on UI about password expiry and receive an email (if configured) 
daily from 10 days before their password expires.

Returns a list of group resources.  Query parameters can be
used to filter the results.  Results are returned in pages.
Each page of results includes the total results found, and
information for requesting the next page of results, using
the `skip` and `limit` query parameters.
Groups can be filtered for user or client membership. Connection
filter applies only to user group membership and NOT to clients.

parameters.description:

parameters.name: connection
parameters.description: Filter by connection name or ID.

parameters.name: clients
parameters.description:

groups with no members.Using '-' at the beginning of client id will 
return groups that the client is not part of.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

allOf.description:
The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

post.description:
This route is for exchanging a credential for
an API authentication token (access token), which can be used to make API calls.
The credential can be a username/password, a refresh token, or a certificate

The username and password or refresh token is passed in the body of the request, and 
the certificate must be presented during SSL negotion, and issued by a CA trusted by the 
web interface.

The response contains the `jwt`, which is the API authentication token (access token),
`duration`, which is the length of time until the token expires, refresh token
that can be used to get a new or additional API authentication token, and the
client id of the refresh token.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description: Current date and time of the client in UTC. ex) 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
The body of the request should contain the username and password
of the user acquiring the token and optionally grant type or the refresh token
with grant type.

grant_type.description:
The authorization grant type. It is optional and valid values are `password`,
`refresh_token`, `user_certificate`, and `client_credential`. 

* Returns only a JWT and not Refresh Token when this parameter is empty or not specified.
* `password`:  Authenticates using a password (which is the default), but returns both a JWT and a refresh token.
If two-factor authentication is enabled for the user, then authenticates using username-password and user certificate. 
The DN of the certificate is matched to the "certificate_subject_dn" of the user and returns both a JWT and a refresh token.
* `refresh_token`: Authenticates using a refresh token. Returns a JWT, and a refresh token if `renew_refresh_token` is set to true.
* `user_certificate`: Authenticate using a client certificate presented during SSL negotiaion.  The DN of the certificate
will be matched to a user's `certificate_subject_dn`.  Returns both a JWT and a refresh token.
* `client_credential`: Authenticates using a client certificate presented during SSL negotiation.  The certifcate will be used to
identify a client and an appropriate token returned. Returns only a JWT.

username.description:
The user's username. Required when the grant_type is not specified or `password`.
You can specify an LDAP user with the format <connection_name>|<username>.
Connection names specified this way override the value specified in the connection field.
Not valid with `refresh_token` grant type.

password.description:
The user's password. Required when the grant_type is not specified or `password`.
Not valid with `refresh_token` grant type.

labels.description: The labels are for tagging. Valid with `password` grant type and optional.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token used to obtain an API authentication token without the user credential.
This refresh token will be revoked if token is requested for a different domain the user belongs to.
Valid with `refresh_token` grant type.

refresh_token_lifetime.description:
Lifetime of a refresh token in minutes. By default, refresh tokens have no expiry.
Valid with `password` grant type.

refresh_token_revoke_unused_in.description:
Refresh token inactivity timeout period in minutes. The refresh token will be revoked if not used
within the specified time to refresh an access token. Each usage resets refresh token lease.
Valid with `password` grant type.

renew_refresh_token.description:
Get a new refresh token along with the API authentication token and invalidate the current
refresh token. Valid with `refresh_token` grant type.

connection.description:
The friendly name of the server you want to authenticate against. If nothing is provided,
it will default to local_account.

domain.description:
The domain name or ID to issue the token for. For grant type of 'password' it defaults to the root domain.
With 'refresh_token' grant type, refresh token used will be revoked if it was not issued for this domain.
Not currently supported for 'client_credential' grant type.

auth_domain.description: The domain where user needs to be authenticated. This is the domain where user is created. Defaults to the root domain.

client_id.description: Client id of the pre-registered clients (nae: c5890024-a6d4-408d-a592-5d4d5807c722, web-ui: 17771cf2-f80b-4eb5-a19b-a2d0032179c3, ksctl: 5ffb6fac-2cb5-4b91-8183-e20ad3b62577, api-playground: 837c840d-75dd-4b4f-a318-79cb16ca248d) and confidential clients.

cookies.description: Any JWT and refresh token will be returned as cookies rather than in the response body.

post.description:
This API can be used to revoke a refresh token.
If the refresh token is associated with an identity provider,
it will log the client out of the identity provider.

A landing page can be supplied. The caller of this API is redirected back
to the landing page.

user_dn_field.description:
LDAP only, Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. If user_dn_field is not provided, an attempt is made to determine default value based on uid_field. If uid_field is provided as sAMAccountName, Active Directory configuration is assumed and 'distingushedName' is used as default for user_dn_field. Otherwise, it will default to  'dn'.

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

flow_type.description:
OpenID Connect only, optional, default value is "implicit".  
Can be an one of "implicit" or "authorization_code".

client_secret.description: secret data stored securely in CipherTrust Manager

authorization_uri.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the authorization endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

client_id.description: OpenID Connect only, required, the public identifier of CipherTrust Manager on the the external identity provider (authorization server). This value is typically generated by and retrieved from the external identity provider.

redirect_uri.description:
(Deprecated) Use redirect URIs instead.

OpenID Connect only, required, URI to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

This URI MUST exactly match one of the Redirection URI values for the Client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

redirect_uris.description:
OpenID Connect only, required, set of allowed URIs to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

These URIs should match the Redirection URIs values for the client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

Typically https://ciphertrust-manager-host/api/v1/auth/oidc-callback where 'ciphertrust-manager-host' should be updated to the hostname of your server.

discovery_uri.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the well-known configuration endpoint of the external identity provider. External ID Provider settings such as authorization URI and public signing keys will be auto-downloaded from this URI.

scope.description:
The scope value should be less than 255 in length and must only contain printable ASCII characters except for spaces, double quotes, and backslashes.
If the scope does not include "openid," the backend will add it to the scope values passed to the OpenID provider.

userinfo_endpoint.description: OIDC server's userinfo_endpoint. It will be used to retrieve group information from OIDC server.

jwks.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, array of JWKS containing the public keys for ID Token validation. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

groups_claim.description: The claim field name to extract group membership from in the OIDC ID Token. Works in conjunction with Group Maps. If unspecified it default to 'groups'.

username_claim.description:
The claim field name to extract username from in the OIDC ID Token. If unspecified it defaults to 'sub'.
The claim field can also be a template to support the nested claims if any in OIDC ID Token.
For instance, for OIDC ID token: 
```
{
 "sub": "111730983950574648607", 
 "email": "test@xyz.com",
 "custom": {       
   "username": "xyz"     
 }
}
```
"email" as string or "{{.custom.username}}" as template can be set as 'username_claim' to set the username of the user on CM after successful authentication on the external identity provider.
It is important that the 'username claim' provided is unique in the external identity provider and it is not modifiable.

token_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the token endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

end_session_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the end session endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

Connection objects still returns the generic `option` attribute in
reponses, for example from create or during list.

LDAP connections also accepts `options` for backwards compatibility but
this attribute is deprecated.

The claim field name to extract username from in the OIDC ID Token. If unspecified it defaults to 'sub'.
The claim field can also be a template to support the nested claims if any in OIDC ID Token.
For instance, for OIDC ID token: 
```
{
 "sub": "111730983950574648607", 
 "email": "test@xyz.com",
 "custom": {       
   "username": "xyz"

}
```

"email" as string or "{{.custom.username}}" as template can be set as 'username_claim' to set the username of the user on CM after successful authentication on the external identity provider.
It is important that the 'username claim' provided is unique in the external identity provider and it is not modifiable.

token_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the token endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

end_session_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the end session endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

patch.description:
Updates a connection's properties.

* These properties are only updated when their value is non-empty:
  * `server_url`
  * `root_dn`
  * `uid_field`

* If `guid_field` is specified as the empty string, then it is set to the value of `uid_field.

Strategies have their own specific "options" attributes, such as
`ldap_options` and `oidc_options` during creation and update.
Connection objects still returns the generic `option` attribute in
reponses, for example from create or during list.

LDAP connections also accepts `options` for backwards compatibility but
this attribute is deprecated.

If not provided, then the server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.

Accepts [PEM encoded certificates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail). Here's an example showing an abbreviated (see `[...]`) list of root CAs.
```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```

insecure_skip_verify.description:
LDAP only, optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

Default value is `false`.

user_dn_field.description:
LDAP only, Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. If user_dn_field is not provided, an attempt is made to determine default value based on uid_field. If uid_field is provided as sAMAccountName, Active Directory configuration is assumed and 'distingushedName' is used as default for user_dn_field. Otherwise, it will default to  'dn'.

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

group_member_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

Can be an one of "implicit" or "authorization_code".

client_id.description: OpenID Connect only, required, the public identifier of CipherTrust Manager on the the external identity provider (authorization server). This value is typically generated by and retrieved from the external identity provider.

redirect_uri.description:
(Deprecated) Use redirect URIs instead.

OpenID Connect only, required, URI to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

This URI MUST exactly match one of the Redirection URI values for the Client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

redirect_uris.description:
OpenID Connect only, required, set of allowed URIs to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

These URIs should match the Redirection URIs values for the client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

Typically https://ciphertrust-manager-host/api/v1/auth/oidc-callback where 'ciphertrust-manager-host' should be updated to the hostname of your server.

discovery_uri.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the well-known configuration endpoint of the external identity provider. External ID Provider settings such as authorization URI and public signing keys will be auto-downloaded from this URI.

scope.description:
The scope value should be less than 255 in length and must only contain printable ASCII characters except for spaces, double quotes, and backslashes.
If the scope does not include "openid," the backend will add it to the scope values passed to the OpenID provider.

userinfo_endpoint.description: OIDC server's userinfo_endpoint. It will be used to retrieve group information from OIDC server.

jwks.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, array of JWKS containing the public keys for ID Token validation. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

groups_claim.description: The claim field name to extract group membership from in the OIDC ID Token. Works in conjunction with Group Maps. If unspecified it default to 'groups'.

username_claim.description:
The claim field name to extract username from in the OIDC ID Token. If unspecified it defaults to 'sub'.
The claim field can also be a template to support the nested claims if any in OIDC ID Token.
For instance, for OIDC ID token: 
```
{
 "sub": "111730983950574648607", 
 "email": "test@xyz.com",
 "custom": {       
   "username": "xyz"     
 }
}
```
"email" as string or "{{.custom.username}}" as template can be set as 'username_claim' to set the username of the user on CM after successful authentication on the external identity provider.
It is important that the 'username claim' provided is unique in the external identity provider and it is not modifiable.

token_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the token endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

end_session_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the end session endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

post.description:
Login initiates an ID Provider login flow. It basically returns a
"login URI" to where the user should perform the login to the external
ID Provider. The connection should contain a redirect URI and the user
should be redirected back after successful login to finish the login
flow and get local credentials, typically an access token and a refresh
token.

Currently it supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) connections using the
implicit flow with form post.

The OpenID Connect implementation is currently limited to:

- `scope=openid email profile`
- `response_type=id_token`
- `response_mode=form_post`

The following standard claims are required to be returned by the external identity provider:

- `sub`: used as the user ID

The following standard claims are optional and will be used if returned by the external identity provider:

- `name`: used as the "name" property of a user, if missing it will fall back to user ID (which effectively means `sub`)
- `email`: used as the "email" property of a user, if missing it will be empty

To read more about standard scopes:

[https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ScopeClaims](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ScopeClaims)

To read more about standard claims:

[https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#StandardClaims](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#StandardClaims)

This API supports both HTML form POST data payload with
"Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" and JSON data payload
with "Content-Type: application/json".

This is an unauthenticated route.

parameters.name: ignore_attribute_mapping
parameters.description:
This attribute is used to handle response. The default value is false.
Only when the "ignore_attribute_mapping" value is set to `false`, the following attributes are displayed:
"uname", "uid", "gname", "gid", "osDomain".
In the case of Open LDAP:
"uname" is mapped to "uid" in User Object, "uid" is mapped to "uidNumber" in User Object, "gid" is mappped to "gidNumber" in User Object, "gname" is mapped to "cn" of a group in the Group Object
And in case of AD:
"uname" is mapped to "UserPrincipalName" by default. But if "UserPrincipalName" is not found then to "sAMAccountName". "osDomain" is mapped to domain provided in UserPrincipalName or sAMAccountName.
Whereas, when the "ignore_attribute_mapping" value is set to `true`, then only "dn" of the User Object is displayed.

parameters.name: hard_limit
parameters.description:
We recommend to use server_max_page_size if ldap server support pagination. This attribute is used to handle the maximum number of entries that can be returned from LDAP in the response. When server_max_page_size is set, then the hard_limit parameter is ignored
Valid value for this field, can be between 0 and 10000. When set to 0, all the users/groups are returned from LDAP server.

group_name_attribute.description: Attribute of the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.

group_id_attribute.description: Attribute of the group object that contains the group identifier (name). This value should be unique.

user_member_field.description:
Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber.
In case, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen.

group_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains the group's distinguished name.
When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber

For example:
- if a groups's LDAP entry has "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`" and the LDAP configuration has "`group_dn_attribute`" set to "`dn`", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`", in order for the user to be considered part of group.

group_member_field.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid
This value can be left empty to disable group membership support for this connection.

user_dn_attribute.description: Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. Example: uid, dn

server_maximum_page_size.description:
This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size. To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0. 
Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

early_listing_stop.description:
This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched. When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user. To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1. When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.

post.description:
Adds a new interface.

An interface is an externally exposed service. This API basically opens
a new port in the system and starts a service to listen on that port.

Currently supported interface types are:
- NAE - "nae"
- KMIP-  "kmip"
- SNMP - "snmp"
- WEB - "web"

NAE by default listens to port 9000, kmip by default listens to port 5696 and web by default listens to port 443. This route offers the capability

tls_groups.description:
TLS Groups contain the list of key exchange algorithms available in the system for the WEB, NAE and KMIP interfaces for TLS handshake.
Classic key exchange algorithms default behaviour:
* Web interface: 'x25519', 'secp256r1', 'x448', 'secp521r1', 'secp384r1', 'ffdhe2048', 'ffdhe3072', 'ffdhe4096', 'ffdhe6144' and 'ffdhe8192' are enabled.
* NAE and KMIP interfaces: 'x25519', 'secp256r1', 'secp521r1' and 'secp384r1' are enabled.

Post Quantum key exchange algorithms default behaviour:
* Web interface: 'X25519MLKEM768', 'SecP256r1MLKEM768', 'MLKEM768', 'MLKEM1024' and 'MLKEM512' are disabled.
* NAE and KMIP interfaces: 'X25519MLKEM768' is disabled.

The entire list of TLS groups is required to enable or disable any specific TLS group.

Behavior of order of TLS Groups:
  * For TLS1.3, despite the server's configured preference order of the groups, currently server will automatically accept the very first key_share that client includes 
    in its ClientHello message, that is also supported by the server.
  * For TLS v1.2, client cannot share its key_share upfront in ClientHello message, thus server will request the client 
    to converge on the most preferred server's group which is also supported by the client. This behavior is aligned with OpenSSL.

However, defining the order still matters. Even if server picks the less preferred (but supported) group, it sends a supported_groups back to the client in its 
ServerHello, so that the client can remember and adjust to send the key_share as per the server's priority for the subsequent requests.

The Akeyless Customer Fragment ID is used to display customer fragments on the Akeyless gateway. If the akeyless-cf-id is not provided, the resource ID will be used instead.

material.description:
Customer fragment secret material is the value of customer fragment which is a base64 encoded string consisting of 88 characters. This field is used to create a customer fragment with user-provided secret material when the user has their own secret material.
In the case of imported customer fragments, material can be obtained from the customer_fragments.json file downloaded from the standalone akeyless gateway.
If the material is not provided, it will be automatically generated on the CipherTrust Manager; however, the material is required when an akeyless_cf_id is provided.

get.description:
This API returns a gzipped tarball (tar.gz) containing the log file(s), certificate and digital signature.
The ca_id(optional parameter) and include_logs(optional parameter) can be passed using the query parameters.
If CA ID is not provided, the default local CA i.e. KeySecure Root CA, signs the log file.

Valid values for include_logs are system, activity and all.
"system" includes the current system logs, "activity" includes the current NAE, KMIP and Web activity logs,
and "all" flag includes both the current and the rotated logs in the CipherTrust Manager.

Multiple values can be mentioned, separated by commas. Default value is "system, activity"

parameters.name: ca_id
parameters.description: Use the provided CA to issue certificate and sign log file

parameters.name: include_logs
parameters.description:
Example
1. "system, all" downloads all the system logs.
2. "activity" only downloads the current activity logs.
3. "system, activity" downloads current system and activity logs.

do_not_modify_subject_dn.description:
Flag to specify if the subject distinguished name (Subject DN) in the presented CSR is allowed to be modified or not.
If this is flag is set to true, then the subject distinguished name must be unique across all the CipherTrust Manager clients,
otherwise the client registration will not be allowed.
This flag is only applied when CSR is provided in the properties.

subject_dn_field_to_modify.description:
This field is used in making the subject distinguished name (Subject DN) unique. This is required when the Subject DN from client's CSR is not unique in itself.
Admins should choose one of the following fields for this purpose. If none is chosen, by default UID is used to modify the Subject DN.
If the admin does not want the Subject DN to be modified, set the do_not_modify_subject_dn flag to true.
If one of these fields (except OU) is chosen, the original field values would be overridden by CipherTrust Manager .
If OU is chosen, the OU would be appended in the Subject DN with other attributes.

cert_duration.description: Duration in days for which the CipherTrust Manager client certificate is valid. The value cannot be negative.

properties.description:
Properties object will contain all profile properties, if CSR is given then no need to provide other csr params. cert_user_field [Specifies how the user name is extracted from the client certificate for kmip app client ]
  csr [CSR for client certificate for kmip app client ]
  csr_cn [CSR common name parameter for client certificate for kmip app client]
  csr_org_name [CSR organization name parameter for client certificate for kmip app client]
  csr_org_unit [CSR organizational unit parameter for client certificate for kmip app client]
  csr_email [CSR email address parameter for client certificate for kmip app client]
  csr_city [CSR city name parameter for client certificate for kmip app client]
  csr_state [CSR state name parameter for client certificate ]
  csr_country [CSR country name parameter for client certificate]
  csr_uid [CSR UID parameter for client certificate].
  csr_sn [ CSR surname parameter for client certificate].
  Fields like csr_org_name, csr_org_unit, csr_email, csr_city, csr_state and csr_country can have multiple values if specified in
  array. Example :- { "csr_org_unit" : ["val1","val2","val3"],"csr_state" : "State" }

device_credential.description:
Device credential object will contains all device credentials related properties, please provide if the credential type is device.
  serial_no [Serial number of the device ]
  password [Password or shared secret of device]
  device_id [Device identifier]
  network_id [Network identifier]
  machine_id [Machine identifier]
  media_id [Media identifier]

post.description:
This performs Format Preserving Encryption (FPE) per the FF3 algorithm.

The key used for encryption can be specified as a HTTP query parameter. 
A 256 bit AES key is created if it does not exist.
A default key is used if the key name is not specified. The name of the default key
is derived using quantities passed in the JWT (the issuer, subject, audience), and can
be considered unique per user. Once created, the same key will be reused for that user
when the key name is not specified.
        
Two modes of input data are supported: batch data and single data.

For single data, the FPE parameters (tweak, etc.) are passed as HTTP query parameters,
and the data is passed as plain text in the body. Set the HTTP "Content Type" header to
"text/plain" for this mode.

The batch data mode allows passing both the FPE parameters and the plain text in the 
body of the HTTP request. Set the HTTP "Content Type" and "Accept" headers to "application/json" for this mode.        
The FPE parameters can be passed both as HTTP query parameters, or in the body. 
Any parameters passed via the body override the parameters passed in the query string.
The data to be encrypted must be passed in the body. Multiple plain text strings can be encrypted 
in a single request, each having their ownset of FPE parameters. The key and the hint
are common to all data sets in the batch request.

The batch mode is recommended because it does not expose any of the FPE parameters via the HTTP query string.
Note that the API playground only works in batch mode. The single data mode is not supported in the API playground.

parameters.name: keyName
parameters.description: This string is used for identifying the cryptographic key that is used for encryption/hmac. An empty string is assumed if this parameter is absent. The tuple containing this keyName string, and the account details in the JWT uniquely identify the cryptographic key.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: This string is used for identifying the version of the cryptographic key that is used for encryption/hmac. The newest version is used if this parameter is omitted. This string is used only when the keyName parameter is also specified. Supported Versions are actual version of the key, Latest version (-1), Latest active version (-2).

parameters.name: hint
parameters.description: This string identifies the type of input. It can be one of following printable strings - 'digit', 'alphabet', 'alphanumeric', 'printable' and 'unicode'. This hint needs to be passed.

parameters.name: charset
parameters.description: This string identifies the charset name or id. It is required when hint is 'unicode'.

parameters.name: tweakAlg
parameters.description: This string specifies the algorithm used for converting the tweak string into the tweak used by the FPE algorithm. Allowed values are "sha1", "sha256", "sha512" and "none". Defaults to "none".

parameters.name: tweak
parameters.description: This string identifies the tweak to be used along with the cryptographic key for hiding/unhiding the data. If tweakAlg is "none", this should be a 8-byte array encoded in hex. Length of encoded string is 16 bytes. It can be any arbitrary string if the tweakAlg is not "none". If provided, it must be the same for both hide and unhide operations for a given data. Tweak is not allowed if tweakAlg is empty.

parameters.name: iv
parameters.description: This string identifies the IV to be used along with the cryptographic key for hiding/unhiding data. It is required only if the input data length is larger than the FPE block length. The block length depends on the hint (digit-56, alphabet,alphanumeric-32, printable-28 bytes). The IV should not be supplied if the data length does not exceed the FPE block length. The characters in the IV should lie in the alphabet specified via the hint. The length of the IV should equal the FPE block size.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
The data to be hidden.
Body can be specified in two ways: plain data for single data mode and JSON data for batch mode.
For plain data, provide data to be hidden in the body and Content-Type header as "text/plain".
For JSON data, provide data in JSON format as specified in the body schema and Content-Type and Accept headers as "application/json".
Only the characters in the data that are within the alphabet type specified by the hint are hidden.
Characters not part of the specified alphabet are returned without modification, at the same location within the string.

schema.description:
Specify the HTTP Content-Type and Accept headers as "application/json" to provide data in JSON format.
Either `"input"` or `"input_base64"` should be specified.

batch_request.description:
Provide single or multiple data.

`"iv"`, `"tweak_alg"` and `"tweak"` can be part of either query parameters or `"batch_request"`.
If specified in query parameters, these will be applicable to every data in the batch.
If specified with a data in the batch, these will be applicable to only that data in the batch.
"iv", "tweak_alg" and tweak", if specified with both "batch_request" and the query parameters,
values within "batch_request" takes precedence.

Response comes in `"batch_response"`. See `"batch_response"` description for more.
Response HTTP status code - 207 indicates failure in batch request.

tweak_alg.description:
This string specifies the algorithm used for converting the tweak string into the tweak used by the FPE algorithm.
Defaults to "none".

tweak.description:
This string identifies the tweak to be used along with the cryptographic key for hiding/unhiding the data.
If tweakAlg is "none", this should be a 8-byte array encoded in hex. Length of encoded string is 16 bytes.
It can be any arbitrary string if the tweakAlg is not "none".

returned only for the data that failed, with `"batch_response"` containing `"error"` for that

post.description:
This operation encrypts data. The key name and the data to encrypt must be supplied. The Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) may be included for AES/GCM operation. Optional information that are passed via query parameters include the key version, crypto mode, crypto padding mode, the Initialization Vector (IV), and the length of the AES-GCM tag. The key version and tag length are pointers, and cannot be used in the API playground. The plaintext and AAD are passed in via a JSON encoded blob. The output is a JSON blob. The JSON blob that is returned can be passed to the decrypt endpoint.
It supports two modes for input data, single data (default) and batch data. To use single data mode, provide data in `"plaintext"`. To use batch mode, refer "`batch_request`" in body schema.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The data to encrypt.

schema.description: The input to an encrypt operation. It is a JSON object that contains the data to be encrypted. For AES-GCM, it also contains the data to be authenticated. Note that both these are byte arrays. JSON encodes byte arrays to base64 strings. Therefore, the JSON object that is input should contain valid base64 data for both the plaintext and AAD.
schema.title: Encryption Input

id.description: The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.

name.description: The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.

type.description: Specify the type of the identifier specified by the 'name' field. Must be one of name, id, uri, or alias.  If not specified, the type of the identifier is inferred.

plaintext.description: Data to Encrypt. This is a byte array. JSON encodes byte arrays to base64 strings. Therefore, the string in the JSON object should be a valid base64 string.

version.description:
Version of the key to use. Supported Versions are
Actual version of the key, Latest Version (-1), Latest Active Version (-2). If no version is specified, the key's latest version (-1) is used by default.

mode.description: This string identifies the cryptographic mode to use for symmetric key operations (i.e algorithm is 'AES' or 'TDES'). Allowed values for AES are 'CBC', 'EBC', 'CTR', and 'GCM' (default is 'GCM'), and the only allowed value for TDES is 'CBC'.

pad.description: This string identifies cryptographic padding algorithm to use. Allowed values depend on the algorithm used. For AES and TDES, allowed values are 'none', 'PKCS5' and 'PKCS7' (default is 'PKCS7'). For asymmetric algorithms the allowed values 'PKCS1', 'OAEP', 'OAEP256', 'OAEP384' and 'OAEP512', defaulting to 'OAEP'. Padding is not applicable for 'CTR' and 'GCM' mode.

aad.description: Data to authenticate. This is a byte array and should be a valid base64 string.

iv.description: The Initialization Vector (IV) is a byte array used with CBC and GCM cryptographic algorithm modes. It appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob. We recommend to omit this field to let the server generate and return a secure IV using its random number generator. Otherwise follow the security guidelines in "NIST SP800-38A" and "NIST SP800-38D" publications to ensure your IV construction is secure.

label.description: A Base64-encoded string containing arbitrary data that will not be encrypted, but gives important context to the message. Used only with asymmetric RSA encryption and supported paddings are OAEP, OAEP256, OAEP384 and OAEP512.

nae_key_version_header.description: This flag requests that the 3-byte NAE key-version header be prepended to the returned ciphertext.

tag_len.description: The byte length of the GCM tag. It can be between 4 and 16, defaults to 16.

batch_request.description:
Single or multiple data to encrypt.

`"iv"`, `"tag_len"`, `"label"` and `"aad"` can be specified explicitly for each data within `"batch_request"` or
for all data in the batch request by making it part of the request body.
If specified at both the places, values inside `"batch_request"` takes precedence.

Response field `"batch_response"` will contain encrypted data. See `"batch_response"` description for more.
Response HTTP status code - 207 indicates failure in batch request.

You must set content type to application/octet-stream for symmetric encryption, and to multipart/form-data for use with AES-GCM operations so both the data to encrypt and the authentication data can be passed in. You must set accept type to multipart/form-data.
The multipart/form-data returned via the body contains (i) the key ID and version used for encryption, (ii) the encrypted data, (iii) the IV that was generated (in case an IV was not passed in via a query parameter).

The IV should not be supplied if the data length does not exceed the FPE block length. The characters in the IV should lie in the alphabet specified via the hint. parameters.name: includeMaterial
parameters.description: Include key bytes in the response. If set to 'false' or not specified, only key meta data is returned.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Type of key to create. By default an AES 256 bit key is created. Other key types are RSA and HMAC. Body itself and all parameters within are optional with the following exception.
By default, users not in the admin group *must* include `{"ownerId" : "local|ab12..."}` in the `meta` property of the post body.  This is because the
default policies state that only the owner of a key may use the key - so we must declare the owner in the metadata.  Policies can be changed by admins if this behavior
is not desired. The key by default enters "Active" state upon creation. For the key to start in "Pre-Active" state as specified in the KMIP spec, set state to "Pre-Active" in the
create request POST body.
An array of aliases can be used to pass in one or more KMIP "Name" attributes associated with the key.

name.description: Optional friendly name, The key name should not contain special characters such as angular brackets (<,>) and backslash (`\`).

usageMask.description:
Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage masks to allow certain usages. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303.
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

algorithm.description: Cryptographic algorithm this key is used with. Defaults to 'aes'. ML-DSA is a post-quantum digital signature algorithm per FIPS 204 (Tech Preview).

xts.description: If set to true, then key created will be XTS/CBC-CS1 Key. Defaults to false. Key algorithm must be 'AES'.

objectType.description:
This specifies the type of object that is being created. Valid values are
'Symmetric Key', 'Public Key', 'Private Key', 'Secret Data', 'Opaque Object',
or 'Certificate'. The object type is inferred for many objects,
but must be supplied for the certificate object.

curveid.description: Cryptographic curve id for elliptic key. Key algorithm must be 'EC'.

parameterSet.description: Specifies the ML-DSA parameter set. Valid values are 'ml-dsa-44', 'ml-dsa-65', and 'ml-dsa-87'. Defaults to 'ml-dsa-65' if not specified.

size.description: Bit length for the key. For ML-DSA, accepts NIST security category values (44, 65, 87) which map to ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87.

macSignBytes.description:
This parameter specifies the MAC/Signature bytes to be used for verification while importing a key. The "wrappingMethod" should be 
"mac/sign" and the required parameters for the verification must be set.

macSignKeyIdentifier.description:
This parameter specifies the identifier of the key to be used for generating MAC or signature of the key material.
The "wrappingMethod" should be "mac/sign" to verify the MAC/signature("macSignBytes") of the key material("material").  
For verifying the MAC, the key has to be a HMAC key.  
For verifying the signature, the key has to be an RSA private or public key.

macSignKeyIdentifierType.description:
This parameter specifies the identifier of the key("macSignKeyIdentifier") used for generating MAC or signature of the key material.
The "wrappingMethod" should be "mac/sign" to verify the mac/signature("macSignBytes") of the key material("material").
Possible values are:
  * name
  * id
  * alias

signingAlgo.description:
This parameter specifies the algorithm to be used for generating the signature for the verification of the "macSignBytes" during import of key material. 
The "wrappingMethod" should be "mac/sign" to verify the signature("macSignBytes") of the key material("material").  
Possible values are:
  * RSA
  * RSA-PSS

wrapPublicKey.description:
If the algorithm is 'aes','tdes','hmac-*', 'seed' or 'aria', this value will be used to encrypt
the returned key material.  This value is ignored for other algorithms.  Value must be an RSA public
key, PEM-encoded public key in either PKCS1 or PKCS8 format, or a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate.
If set, the returned 'material' value will be a Base64 encoded PKCS#1 v1.5 encrypted key. View 
"wrapPublicKey" in export parameters for more information.
Only applicable if 'includeMaterial' is true.

wrapPublicKeyPadding.description:
1. WrapPublicKeyPadding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when importing
the Key using the specified wrapkey.  Accepted values are "pkcs1", "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
and will default to "pkcs1" when 'wrapPublicKeyPadding' is not set and 'WrapPublicKey' is set.

2. While creating a new key, wrapPublicKeyPadding parameter should be specified only if 'includeMaterial' is true.
In this case, key will get created and in response wrapped material using specified wrapPublicKeyPadding and other
wrap parameters will be returned.

wrapKeyName.description:
1. While creating a new key, If 'includeMaterial' is true, then only the key material will be wrapped with material of the specified key name. The response "material"
property will be the base64 encoded ciphertext. For more details, view "wrapKeyName" in export parameters.

2. While importing a key, the key material will be unwrapped with material of the specified key name. The only applicable "wrappingMethod" for the unwrapping is "encrypt" 
and the wrapping key has to be an AES key or an RSA private key.

wrapKeyIDType.description:
IDType specifies how the wrapKeyName should be interpreted.  
Values can be:
  * name
  * id
  * alias

wrappingMethod.description:
This parameter specifies the wrapping method used to wrap/mac/sign the key material.
Valid values:
  * encrypt
  * mac/sign
  * pbe  

In "encrypt", the material of a symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be unwrapped based on
several available parameters.  

For AES Key Wrap with Padding(RFC 5649) or AES Key Wrap(RFC 3394)
algorithms, a wrapped symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be unwrapped using an AES wrapping key. For
unwrapping a symmetric key and importing it, the following parameters are needed:
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo" 
  * "padded"(optional, required if padding not mentioned in "wrappingEncryptionAlgo")
  * "material"  

For unwrapping a wrapped private key, the following parameters are needed:
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(only "aes/aeskeywrappadding" allowed) 
  * "material"  

For unwrapping a wrapped certificate, the following parameters are needed:
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(only "aes/aeskeywrappadding" allowed) 
  * "padded"(only true is valid)  

Additionally "wrapHKDF" parameters can be set in order to derive a wrapping key for the wrapping algorithm(RFC 5649/3394)  

A wrapped symmetric key can be unwrapped with RSA encryption using an RSA private key.  
For this, the following parameters are needed: 
  * "wrapKeyName"(RSA private key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrapPublicKeyPadding"
  * "material"  

For unwrapping a wrapped RSA private key with RSA AES KWP algorithm using an RSA private key, the following parameters are needed:
  * "wrapKeyName"(RSA private key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(set to "rsa/rsaaeskeywrappadding")
  * "wrapRSAAES"
  * "material"  


In "mac/sign", either MAC or signature will be verified based on type of the key in "macSignKeyIdentifier".  
For MAC operation, the hash algorithm will be inferred from the type of key using the "macSignKeyIdentifier" field which has to be an HMAC key. 
The following parameters are needed for this operation:
  * "macSignBytes"
  * "macSignKeyIdentifier"
  * "macSignKeyIdentifierType"(optional) 
  * "material"  

For SIGN operation, the key used to verify the signature("macSignKeyIdentifier") has to be an RSA private or public key. 
The following parameters are needed for this operation:
  * "macSignBytes"
  * "macSignKeyIdentifier"
  * "macSignKeyIdentifierType"(optional)
  * "signingAlgo"
  * "wrappingHashAlgo" 
  * "material"  

For "pbe" (password based encryption) operation, a wrapped symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be 
unwrapped using the following parameters:
  * "padded"(for a symmetric key)
  * "wrapPBE" 
  * "material"  


Additionally, if "includeMaterial" query parameter is true, and the wrapping parameters are set as per 
"wrappingMethod" in export, the wrapped material can be obtained in the "material" field in response.

wrappingEncryptionAlgo.description:
It indicates the Encryption Algorithm information for wrapping the key.
Format is : Algorithm/Mode/Padding. For example : AES/AESKEYWRAP. Here AES is Algorithm, AESKEYWRAP is Mode & Padding is not specified.
AES/AESKEYWRAP is RFC-3394 & AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING is RFC-5649. For wrapping private key, only AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING is allowed.
RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING is used to wrap/unwrap asymmetric keys using RSA AES KWP method. Refer "WrapRSAAES" to provide optional parameters.

wrappingHashAlgo.description:
This parameter specifies the hashing algorithm used if "wrappingMethod" corresponds to "mac/sign".
In case of MAC operation, the hashing algorithm used will be inferred from the type of HMAC key("macSignKeyIdentifier").  
In case of SIGN operation, the possible values are: 
  * sha1
  * sha224
  * sha256
  * sha384
  * sha512

wrapHKDF.description: Information which is used to wrap a Key using HKDF.

hashAlgorithm.description: Hash Algorithm is used for HKDF Wrapping.

salt.description: Salt is an optional hex value for HKDF based derivation.

info.description: Info is an optional hex value for HKDF based derivation.

okmLen.description: The desired output key material length in integer.

wrapPBE.title: Password based encryption parameters for generating password based derived keys.
wrapPBE.description:
WrapPBE derives the key from the password and other parameters such as salt, iteration count, hashing algorithm, and derived key-length. PBE currently supports wrapping of symmetric keys (AES), private keys, and certificates.
WrapPBE is a two-step process to export a key as mentioned below. The key import is similar to the key export but it unwraps the target key in the second step.
Step 1 Use PBKDF2 with the specified parameters (pwd, hash-function, salt, iterations, purpose (opt), KEK length) to derive the KEK. For more details, refer to RFC 2898.
Step 2 Perform AES-KW/KWP to wrap the target key using the KEK derived from Step 1. The AES KEK size is calculated by the KEK length parameter as described in Step 1. For more details, refer to RFC 3394 and 5649.

hashAlgorithm.description: Underlying hashing algorithm that acts as a pseudorandom function to generate derive keys.

password.description:
Base password to generate derive keys. It cannot be used in conjunction with passwordidentifier.
password must be in range of 8 bytes to 128 bytes.

passwordIdentifier.description: Secret password identifier for password. It cannot be used in conjunction with password.

passwordIdentifierType.description: Type of the Passwordidentifier. If not set then default value is name.

salt.description:
A Hex encoded string.
pbeSalt must be in range of 16 bytes to 512 bytes.

purpose.description:
User defined purpose. If specified will be prefixed to pbeSalt.
pbePurpose must not be greater than 128 bytes.

dklen.description:
Intended length in octets of the derived key.
dklen must be in range of 14 bytes to 512 bytes.

iteration.description:
Iteration count increase the cost of producing keys from a password.
Iteration must be in range of 1 to 1,00,00,000.

wrapRSAAES.title: RSA AES KWP parameters
wrapRSAAES.description:
Information which is used to wrap/unwrap asymmetric keys using RSA AES KWP method.
This method internally requires AES key size to generate a temporary AES key and RSA padding.
To use WrapRSAAES, algorithm "RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING" must be specified in WrappingEncryptionAlgo.

aesKeySize.description:
Size of AES key for RSA AES KWP. Accepted value are 128, 192, 256.
Default value is "256".

padding.description:
Padding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when exporting
the Key using RSA AES wrap.  Accepted values are "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
Default value is "oaep256".

padded.description:
This parameter determines the padding for the wrap algorithm while unwrapping a symmetric key,
  * if "wrappingMethod" is "encrypt" and the "wrappingEncryptionAlgo" doesn't have a mode set
  * if "wrappingMethod" is "pbe".  

If true, the RFC 5649(AES Key Wrap with Padding) is followed and if false, RFC 3394(AES Key Wrap) is followed for unwrapping the material for the symmetric key.  

If a certificate is being unwrapped with the "wrappingMethod" set to "encrypt", the "padded" parameter has to be set to true.  
This parameter defaults to false.

format.description:
This parameter is used while importing keys ('material' is not empty), and also when returning
the key material after the key is created ('includeMaterial' is true).

**For Asymmetric keys:**
  When this parameter is not specified, while importing keys, the format of the material is inferred from the material itself.
  When this parameter is specified, while importing keys, the only allowed format is 'pkcs12', and this only applies
  to the 'rsa' algorithm (the 'material' should contain the base64 encoded value of the PFX file in this case).

  For 'ec' algorithm with 'ed25519' curveid, when the format is 'pkcs12', the 'material' should contain the base64 encoded value of the PFX file.

  For ML-DSA keys, only 'pkcs8' format is supported. PKCS#1 and PKCS#12 are not supported for ML-DSA keys.

  When returning the key material, this parameter specifies the format of the returned key material.

*Options:*

- pkcs1
- pkcs8 (default)
- pkcs12

**For Symmetric keys:**
  When importing keys if specified, the value must be given according to the format of the material.

  When returning the key material, this parameter specifies the format of the returned key material.

 *Options:*

- raw  
- opaque

encoding.description:
Specifies the encoding used for the 'material' field. This parameter is used :
 * during importing keys when key material is not empty
 * while returning the key material after the key is created  ('includeMaterial' is true)

For wrapping scenarios and PKCS12 format, the only valid option is base64.
In case of "Symmetric Keys" when 'format' parameter has 'base64' value and 'encoding' parameter also contains some value;
the encoding parameter takes the priority. Following are the options for Symmetric Keys:

material.description:
If set, the value will be imported as the key's material. If not set, new key material will be
generated on the server (certificate objects must always specify the material).
The format of this value depends on the algorithm. If the algorithm is
'aes', 'tdes', 'hmac-*', 'seed' or 'aria', the value should be the hex-encoded bytes of the key material.
If the algorithm is 'rsa' or 'ec' with 'ed25519' curveid, and the format is 'pkcs12', it should be the base64 encoded PFX file.
If the algorithm is 'rsa' or 'ec', and format is not 'pkcs12', the value should be a PEM-encoded private
or public key using PKCS1 or PKCS8 format.
If the algorithm is 'ml-dsa', the value should be a PEM-encoded private or public key in PKCS#8 format.
For a X.509 DER encoded certificate, certType equals 'x509-der' and the material should equal the hex encoded certificate.
The material for a X.509 PEM encoded certificate (certType = 'x509-pem') should equal the certificate itself.
When placing the PEM encoded certificate inside a JSON object (as in the playground), be sure to change
all new line characters in the certificate to the string '\n'.

defaultIV.description: Deprecated. This field was introduced to support specific legacy integrations and applications. New applications are strongly recommended to use a unique IV for each encryption request. Refer to Crypto encrypt endpoint for more details. Must be a 16 byte hex encoded string (32 characters long). If specified, this will be set as the default IV for this key.

parameters correspond to  either of these states - "Deactivated", "Destroyed", "Compromised" and
"Destroyed Compromised". Key in "Destroyed" or "Destroyed Compromised" state would not have key material even
if specified during key creation.

labels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. APIs that list keys can use
labels to filter the set of matching resources.

A label's key has an optional prefix up to 253 characters followed by a
forward slash and a required name up to 63 characters. For example,
`sales.widgets.com/region` is a label key with the prefix
`sales.widgets.com` and the name `region`, while `region` is a label key
without a prefix.

A label's value may be empty and may be up to 63 characters.

Each part of the label (i.e. the prefix, name, and value) must begin
and end with an alphanumeric character (a-zA-Z0-9). Characters
inbetween the beginning and end may contain alphanumeric characters,
dots (.), dashes (-) and underscores (_).

A Label can be a simple tag by specifying a key with no value
(e.g. `{ "critical": "" }`).

Here's a full example showing a name/value pair with prefix, a name/value pair, and a simple tag:
```
    "labels": {
      "sales.widgets.com/region": "noram",
      "team": "sales",
      "critical": ""
    }
```

emptyMaterial.description: If set to `true`, the key material is not created and left empty.

assignSelfAsOwner.description:
If set to `true`, the user who is creating the key is set as the key owner. Specify either `assignSelfAsOwner`
or `ownerId` in the meta, not both. Specifying both in the meta returns an error.

parameters.name: usageMask
parameters.description:
Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage masks to allow certain usages. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303.
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

patch.description:
Updates the key properties.  This can be used to update the key
metadata, change the exportable and deletable properties, activation date,
deactivation date, compromise occurance date and revocation reason for the key.

If you update the `meta` field, and both the current value and the
updated value are JSON objects, the fields of the objects will be
be merged.

This operation can be used to add, delete and modify key aliases.
To add an alias, pass in the alias and alias-type.
To delete an alias, pass the unique index of the alias to be deleted.
To modify an alias, pass the index as well as the new values of the alias and alias-type.

unless format 'base64' is specified, in whcih case the key material is base64-encoded.  If the algorithm is
'rsa' or 'ec', the value should be a PEM-encoded private or public key using PKCS1 or PKCS8 format.
For a X.509 DER encoded certificate, certType equals 'x509-der' and the material should equal the hex encoded certificate.
The material for a X.509 PEM encoded certificate (certType = 'x509-pem') should equal the certificate itself.
When placing the PEM encoded certificate inside a JSON object (as in the playground), be sure to change
all new line characters in the certificate to the string '\n'.

defaultIV.description: Deprecated. This field was introduced to support specific legacy integrations and applications. New applications are strongly recommended to use a unique IV for each encryption request. Refer to Crypto encrypt endpoint for more details. Must be a 16 byte hex encoded string (32 characters long). If specified, this will be set as the default IV for this key.

wrapPublicKey.description:
If the algorithm is 'aes','tdes','hmac-*', 'seed' or 'aria', this value will be used to encrypt
the returned key material.  This value is ignored for other algorithms.  Value must be an RSA public
key, PEM-encoded public key in either PKCS1 or PKCS8 format, or a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate.
If set, the returned 'material' value will be a Base64 encoded PKCS#1 v1.5 encrypted key.
Only applicable if 'includeMaterial' is true.

wrapPublicKeyPadding.description:
1. wrapPublicKeyPadding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when importing
the Key using the specified wrapkey.  Accepted values are "pkcs1", "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
and will default to "pkcs1" when 'wrapPublicKeyPadding' is not set and 'WrapPublicKey' is set.

2. While creating a new version of a key, wrapPublicKeyPadding parameter should be specified only if 'includeMaterial' is true.
In this case, key will get created and in response wrapped material using specified wrapPublicKeyPadding and other
wrap parameters will be returned.

wrapKeyName.description:
1. While creating a new key, If 'includeMaterial' is true, then only the key material will be wrapped with material of the specified key name. The response "material"
property will be the base64 encoded ciphertext. This will follow RFC-3394. Defaults to none. For RSA or EC keys it will follow RFC-5649.

2. While importing a key, the key material will be unwrapped with material of the specified key name.

padded.description:
If set as true, and "wrapKeyName" is specified or "WrappingMethod" is specified as "pbe" will use RFC-5649.
Defaults to false. Applicable for symmetric keys only.

wrapKeyIDType.description:
IDType specifies how the wrapKeyName should be interpreted
Values can be name,id,alias.

encoding.description:
Specifies the encoding used for the 'material' field. This parameter is used:
 * during import of keys when key material is not empty
 * while returning the key material after the key is created  ('includeMaterial' is true)

For wrapping scenarios, the only valid option is base64.
In case of "Symmetric Keys" when 'format' parameter has 'base64' value and 'encoding' parameter also contains some value;
the encoding parameter takes the priority. Following are the options for Symmetric Keys:

format.description:
The format of the returned key material. It is applicable only if 'includeMaterial' is true. If the algorithm is 'rsa' or 'ec', the value
can be 'pkcs1' or 'pkcs8', and defaults to 'pkcs8'. For symmetric keys, the value of 'base64' can be used to indicate the key material
is base64-encoded; without it, the key material defaults to hex-encoded.

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key. 
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
  - Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
  - Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

are 'x509-pem' and 'x509-der'. At present, we only support x.509 certificates.

is infered from the material if it is left blank.

labels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. When labels are provided
they are merged with the key's existing labels.

To remove a label, set the label's value to `null`.
```
    "labels": {

    }
```

To remove all labels, set `labels` to `null`.
```
    "labels": null
```

Refer to the schema under `/v1/vault/keys2 POST` for a full description
of labels.
