post.description: Returns metadata and the material of the latest version of the key matching the given `id` and the JWT's `account` claim.

combineXts.description: If set to true, then full material of XTS/CBC-CS1 key will be exported. Defaults to false.

wrapPublicKeyPadding.description:
wrapPublicKeyPadding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when exporting
the Key using a public wrapping key. Accepted values are "pkcs1", "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
and will default to "pkcs1" when 'wrapPublicKeyPadding' is not set.
(Not used when format is set to "jwe".)

wrapPublicKey.description:
This parameter specifies the public key used to wrap the key material of the key to be exported. The 
response "material" property will be the base64 encoded ciphertext. This parameter is valid if the 
"wrappingMethod" is "encrypt" or "format" is "jwe". This parameter cannot be passed with "wrapKeyName"
parameter for export with wrapping. 

If wrapping of key material with "encrypt" method is desired the key has to be an RSA public key, a 
PEM-encoded public key in either PKCS1 or PKCS8 format, or a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate. If a 
symmetric key is to be wrapped given a valid "wrapPublicKey", the "wrappingMethod" must be "encrypt". 
If a RSA private key is to be wrapped using RSA AES KWP method, a valid "wrapPublicKey" must pe passed,
 the "wrappingMethod" must be "encrypt", the "wrapRSAAES" parameters should be set and the 
"wrappingEncryptionAlgo" should be set to "RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING".

For Wrapping EC Keys "wrappingEncryptionAlgo" should be set to "AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING". EC key wrap with
asymmetric key is not supported.

For export with format 'jwe', if the algorithm is 'aes','tdes','hmac-*', 'seed', 'aria', 'rsa' or 'ec'
, the "wrapPublicKey" value will be used to encrypt the return key material.

wrapKeyName.description:
The key material will be wrapped with material of the specified key name.  The "material" property in 
the response will be base64 encoded ciphertext. If the "wrappingMethod" field is set to "encrypt",
then the wrapping key must be an AES key, RSA private key or RSA public key. For the export of symmetric
keys with the "encrypt" method, the three key types are allowed but for the export of a private key if the
"wrapRSAAES" parameters are not set, the wrapping key has to be an AES key with a size of 256 bits. If
"wrapRSAAES" parameters are set, then the wrapping key has to either be an RSA private or public key. 
You can set either "wrapKeyName" parameter or "wrapPublicKey" at a time. The wrapping key should be 
active with a protect stop date that is not expired.

For Wrapping EC Keys "wrappingEncryptionAlgo" should be set to "AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING". EC key wrap with
asymmetric key is not supported.

For export with format 'jwe',
- One of wrapPublicKey or wrapKeyName is mandatory
- wrapKeyName should be public key name that could be used for generation of 'jwe'

signingAlgo.description:
This parameter specifies the algorithm used for generating a signature in response as "macSignBytes".
The "wrappingMethod" must equal "mac/sign" to generate the signature("macSignBytes") of the key material. 
Possible values are:
  * RSA
  * RSA-PSS

macSignKeyIdentifier.description:
This parameter specifies the identifier of the key used for generating the MAC or signature("macSignBytes") of 
the key whose key material is to be exported.  
The "wrappingMethod" should be "mac/sign" to generate the MAC/signature.  
To generate a MAC, the key should be a HMAC key.  
To generate a signature, the key should be an RSA private key.

macSignKeyIdentifierType.description:
This parameter specifies the identifier of the key used for generating the MAC or signature.
The "wrappingMethod" should be "mac/sign" to generate the mac/signature("macSignBytes") of the key material("material").
Possible values are:
  * name
  * id
  * alias

wrapKeyIDType.description:
IDType specifies how the wrapKeyName should be interpreted.  
Values can be:
  * name
  * id
  * alias

wrappingMethod.description:
This indicates the method used to wrap/mac/sign the key material.
Valid values:
  * encrypt
  * mac/sign
  * pbe  

In "encrypt", the material of a symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be wrapped based on
several available parameters.  
For AES Key Wrap with Padding(RFC 5649) or AES Key Wrap(RFC 3394)
algorithms, a symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be wrapped using an AES wrapping key.  
For wrapping a symmetric key, the following parameters are required: 
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"
  * "padded"(optional, required if padding not mentioned in "wrappingEncryptionAlgo").  

For wrapping a private key, the following parameters are required:
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(only "aes/aeskeywrappadding" allowed)
  * "pemWrap"  

For wrapping a certificate, the following parameters are required:
  * "wrapKeyName"(AES key)
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(only "aes/aeskeywrappadding" allowed)
  * "padded"(only true is valid)  

Additionally "wrapHKDF" parameters can be set in order to derive a wrapping key for the wrapping algorithm.  

A symmetric key can be wrapped with RSA encryption using an RSA public key, private key or a certificate. 
For this, the following parameters are required:
  * either "wrapKeyName" or "wrapPublicKey"
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional) 
  * "wrapPublicKeyPadding"  

For wrapping a RSA private key with RSA AES KWP algorithms using an RSA public key, private key or a certificate,
the following parameters are required:
  * either "wrapKeyName" or "wrapPublicKey"
  * "wrapKeyIDType"(optional)
  * "wrappingEncryptionAlgo"(set to "rsa/rsaaeskeywrappadding")
  * "wrapRSAAES"
  * "pemWrap"  

In "mac/sign", either MAC or signature will be calculated based on type of the key in "macSignKeyIdentifier". 
The key to be exported has to be a symmetric key or a private key.  
For MAC operation, the hash algorithm will be inferred from type of key using the "macSignKeyIdentifier" 
field which has to be an HMAC key. The following parameters are needed for this method:
  * "macSignKeyIdentifier" 
  * "macSignKeyIdentifierType"(optional)  

For SIGN operation, the key used to generate the signature("macSignKeyIdentifier") has to be an RSA 
private key. The following parameters are needed for this method:
  * "macSignKeyIdentifier"
  * "macSignKeyIdentifierType"(optional) 
  * "signingAlgo"
  * "wrappingHashAlgo"  

For "pbe" (password based encryption) operation, a symmetric key, private key or a certificate can be 
wrapped using the following parameters:
  * "padded"(for a symmetric key)
  * "pemWrap"(for a private key)
  * "wrapPBE"

wrappingEncryptionAlgo.description:
It indicates the Encryption Algorithm information for wrapping the key.
Format is : Algorithm/Mode/Padding. For example : AES/AESKEYWRAP. Here AES is Algorithm, AESKEYWRAP is Mode & Padding is not specified.
AES/AESKEYWRAP is RFC-3394 & AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING is RFC-5649. For wrapping private key, only AES/AESKEYWRAPPADDING is allowed.
RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING is used to wrap/unwrap asymmetric keys using RSA AES KWP method. Refer "wrapRSAAES" to provide optional parameters.

wrappingHashAlgo.description:
This parameter specifies the hashing algorithm if "wrappingMethod" corresponds to "mac/sign".
In case of MAC operation, the hash algorithm will be inferred from the type of HMAC key("macSignKeyIdentifier").  
In case of SIGN operation, Possible values are:
  * sha1
  * sha224
  * sha256
  * sha384
  * sha512

pemWrap.description:
If the parameter is set to true, it wraps the PEM encoding of the private key (asymmetric) otherwise, the DER encoding of the key is wrapped.  
Only valid when private keys (asymmetric) and certificates are to be wrapped for "mac/sign" and "encrypt" values for "wrappingMethod" parameter.   
Default value: false.

padded.description:
This parameter determines the padding for the wrap algorithm while exporting a symmetric key, 
  * if "wrappingMethod" parameter is "encrypt" and the "wrappingEncryptionAlgo" doesn't have a mode set
  * if "wrappingMethod" is "pbe".  

If true, the RFC 5649(AES Key Wrap with Padding) is followed and if false, RFC 3394(AES Key Wrap) is followed for wrapping the material for the symmetric key.  

If a certificate is being exported with the "wrappingMethod" set to "encrypt", the "padded" parameter must be set to true.  
This parameter defaults to false.

encoding.description:
Specifies the encoding for the returned key material. 

For wrapping scenarios and PKCS12 format, the only valid option is base64.
In case of "Symmetric Keys" when 'format' parameter has 'base64' value and 'encoding' parameter also contains some value;
then the encoding parameter takes the priority.

For example: When using the "encoding" parameter, keep in mind that PBE wrapping will be skipped. Only "encoding": "base64" will be 
active during export, meaning that the key would be exported exclusively in base64 format. Make sure not to use both options at the same time.

Following are the options for Symmetric Keys:

format.description:
The format of the returned key material. If the algorithm is 'rsa' or 'ec'. The value can be one of these:
'pkcs1', 'pkcs8' , 'pkcs12', or 'jwe'.  The algorithm 'ec' with 'ed25519' curveid, does not support format 'pkcs1' for export. The default value is  'pkcs8'.
For ML-DSA keys, supported formats are 'pkcs8' and 'jwe'. PKCS#1 and PKCS#12 are not supported for ML-DSA keys. Note: the wrapping key used for JWE must be RSA or EC, not ML-DSA.
If algorithm is ‘rsa’  or 'ec' with 'ed25519' curveid and format is 'pkcs12', the key material will contain the base64-encoded value of the PFX file.
The value 'base64' is used for symmetric keys, for which the format of the returned key material is base64-encoded
if wrapping is applied (i.e., either 'wrapKeyName' or 'wrapPublicKey' is specified),otherwise, the format is hex-encoded,
unless 'base64' is given.
If the "format" is 'jwe' then the "material" for the symmetric key, asymmetric key or certificate will be wrapped in JWE format.
"wrapKeyName"(should be a public key) or "wrapPublicKey" and "wrapJWE" parameters are required for 'jwe' format.
The value 'opaque' is supported for symmetric keys with 'opaque' format only.

password.description:
For pkcs12 format, if the pkcs12passwordLink is not present in the Key (RSA keys), specify either password or secretDataLink.
This should be the base64 encoded value of the password.

secretDataLink.description:
For pkcs12 format, if the pkcs12passwordLink is not present in the Key (RSA keys), specify either secretDataLink or password.
The value can be either ID or name of Secret Data.

secretDataEncoding.description:
For pkcs12 format, this field specifies the encoding method used for the secretDataLink material.
Ignore this field if secretData is created from REST and is in plain format.
Specify the value of this field as HEX format if secretData is created from KMIP.

jwtIdentifier.description: JWT identifier (JTI) is unique identifier for the JWT used by SFDC for cache key replay detection.

contentEncryptionAlgorithm.description: Content Encryption Algorithm is symmetric encryption algorithm used to encrypt the data , default is AES_256_GCM.

keyEncryptionAlgorithm.description:
Key Encryption Algorithm is used to encrypt the Content Encryption Key (CEK), default is RSA_OAEP_SHA1.
Algorithm should correspond to type of public key provided for wrapping.

keyIdentifier.description:
Key identifier to be used as "kid" parameter in JWE material and JWE header.
Defaults to key id.

wrapPBE.title: Password based encryption parameters for generating password based derived keys.
wrapPBE.description:
WrapPBE derives the key from the password and other parameters such as salt, iteration count, hashing algorithm, and derived key-length. PBE currently supports wrapping of symmetric keys (AES), private keys, and certificates.
WrapPBE is a two-step process to export a key as mentioned below. The key import is similar to the key export but it unwraps the target key in the second step.
Step 1 Use PBKDF2 with the specified parameters (pwd, hash-function, salt, iterations, purpose (opt), KEK length) to derive the KEK. For more details, refer to RFC 2898.
Step 2 Perform AES-KW/KWP to wrap the target key using the KEK derived from Step 1. The AES KEK size is calculated by the KEK length parameter as described in Step 1. For more details, refer to RFC 3394 and 5649.

hashAlgorithm.description: Underlying hashing algorithm that acts as a pseudorandom function to generate derive keys.

password.description:
Base password to generate derive keys. It cannot be used in conjunction with passwordidentifier.
password must be in range of 8 bytes to 128 bytes.

passwordIdentifier.description: Secret password identifier for password. It cannot be used in conjunction with password.

passwordIdentifierType.description: Type of the Passwordidentifier. If not set then default value is name.

salt.description:
A Hex encoded string.
pbeSalt must be in range of 16 bytes to 512 bytes.

purpose.description:
User defined purpose. If specified will be prefixed to pbeSalt.
pbePurpose must not be greater than 128 bytes.

dklen.description:
Intended length in octets of the derived key.
dklen must be in range of 14 bytes to 512 bytes.

iteration.description:
Iteration count increase the cost of producing keys from a password.
Iteration must be in range of 1 to 1,00,00,000.

wrapRSAAES.title: RSA AES KWP parameters
wrapRSAAES.description:
Information which is used to wrap/unwrap asymmetric keys using RSA AES KWP method.
This method internally requires AES key size to generate a temporary AES key and RSA padding.
To use WrapRSAAES, algorithm "RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING" must be specified in WrappingEncryptionAlgo.

aesKeySize.description:
Size of AES key for RSA AES KWP. Accepted value are 128, 192, 256.
Default value is "256".

padding.description:
Padding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when exporting
the Key using RSA AES wrap.  Accepted values are "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
Default value is "oaep256".

post.description:
It clones the metadata and the material of the given key identified by id or the combination of name and version, and matching the JWT's `account` claim.

The state of the new cloned key would always be active. If version is not specified with the key name, the latest version of the key will be cloned.

XTS Keys will be cloned as a pair of two linked keys.
Private keys will be cloned as private and public key pair, if public Key link is available for the private key.
Links from the key that is being cloned will not be carry forwarded to the cloned key.

While cloning, the key attributes that will be cloned to the new cloned key are :
Material, Algorithm, Usage, Size, Curveid, Unexportable, Undeletable,CertFields, ObjectType, defaultIV, meta.

post.summary: Generates or Returns the value of attribute.
post.description:
When a new key is created, it gets created with certain in-built attributes. If, with a new CipherTrust Manager release, a new attribute gets added to the key, the value of that attribute may not be set for the keys that are pre-existing.
This API allows setting values to the newly supported attributes, for pre-existing keys, where these attributes might not be set already.
If the attribute already has a value, the API will only return the attribute value in the response.

For example- 
If a key get does not show Sha384Fingerprint value, this API will update the key with the Sha384Fingerprint for a particular key.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expression. Multiple
expressions are not supported. For example, to check if a label
`{"region": "noram"}` exists, use `region=noram`. To check if a label
exists with region not equal to noram, use `region!=noram`.
Also to get all labels with a given key `env` just use `env`.

post.description: This operation searches for keys stored on the CipherTrust Manager. The operation is similar to the list operation. The differences are (a) a lot more search parameters can be passed in, and (b) the search parameters are passed in the body of an HTTP POST request instead of being passed as query parameters in a HTTP GET request. Normally, this operation returns a list of keys, secrets, etc., that satisfy the search criteria.  When either the returnOnlyIDs or returnOnlyKeyNames input parameter is specified as `true`, then this operation just returns a list of key IDs or key Names.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The search filter parameters.

schema.title: Search Parameters
schema.description: Information needed to search for a managed object.

skip.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

limit.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL.

returnOnlyIDs.description:
When this is not specified, or set to false, a list of keys is returned.
When this is set to true, a list of key IDs is returned.

returnOnlyKeyNames.description: When this parameter is set to true, a list of key names is returned.

name.description: Filters results to those with matching names.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.

names.description: A set of names of keys that filters results to those with matching names.

id.description: Find the key with a matching ID.

uri.description: Filters results to those with matching uris.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.

version.description:
Deprecated: Use 'versions'. Filters results to those with matching version. If version is specified as -1, only
latest version of the keys is returned. If version is specified as -2, only nae latest active version of the keys will be returned.
All versions are returned when the version is not specified.

versions.description: Filters results to those with matching versions. If versions is specified as [-1], only latest version of the keys are returned.If versions is specified as [-2], only nae latest active version of the keys are returned. All versions are returned when the version is not specified.

algorithm.description: Deprecated: Use 'algorithms'. Filters results to those with matching algorithms.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.

algorithms.description: Filters results to those with matching algorithms.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used if only specifying a single value.

size.description: Deprecated: Use 'sizes'. Filters results to those with matching size.

sizes.description: Filters results to those with a matching size.

curveIDs.description:
Filters results to those with matching elliptic key curve id.  Results will match *any*
of the values.

states.description:
Filters results to those with matching key state. Allowed values are
"Pre-Active", "Active", "Deactivated", "Destroyed", "Compromised" and "Destroyed Compromised".

aliases.description:
Filters results to those with any of the matching aliases. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters
may be used when a single alias is specified.

linkTypes.description:
Filters results to those with any of the matching link types. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters
may be used when a single link type is specified. See the links documentation
for the various link types.

usageMask.description:
Deprecated: Use 'usageMasks'.
Filters results to those with matching Cryptographic usage mask. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303 (all usage masks including Export).
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

usageMasks.description:
Filters results to those with matching any of the Cryptographic usage masks. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303 (all usage masks including Export).
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

metaContains.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only keys whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`
- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`
- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`
- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

objectTypes.description:
Filters results to those with any of the matching KMIP object types. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters
may be used when a single object type is specified. Valid object types are:
"Certificate", "Symmetric Key", "Public Key", "Private Key", "Split Key", "Secret Data", "Opaque Object".

sha1Fingerprint.description:
Deprecated: Use 'sha1Fingerprints'.
Filters results to those with matching SHA1 fingerprints.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.
This fingerprint is truncated and is based on the first 8 bytes of the SHA1 checksum.
To be backward compatible with Classic KeySecure, it is based on ASN.1 representation of PKCS#1 public key.

sha1Fingerprints.description:
Filters results to those with matching one of the SHA1 fingerprints.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used
for singular values. This fingerprint is truncated and is based on the first 8 bytes of the SHA1 checksum.
To be backward compatible with Classic KeySecure, it is based on ASN.1 representation of PKCS#1 public key.

sha256Fingerprint.description:
Deprecated: Use 'sha256Fingerprints'
Filters results to those with matching SHA256 fingerprints. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.

rotationFrequencyDaysBefore.description: Filters results to those with rotation frequencies less than what is specified (in days).

rotationFrequencyDays.description: Filters results to those with matching values of rotation frequencies (in days). The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.

rotationFrequencyDaysAfter.description: Filters results to those with rotation frequencies greater than what is specified (in days).

sha256Fingerprints.description:
Filters results to those with matching SHA256 fingerprints. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used
for a single value.

neverExported.description: Find keys with the specified value of the `neverExported` attribute.

neverExportable.description: Find keys with the specified value of the `neverExportable` attribute (same as the KMIP `Never Extractable` attribute).

unexportable.description: Find keys with the specified value of the `unexportable` attribute (opposite of the KMIP `Extractable` attribute).

revocationReason.description: Deprecated: Use 'revocationReasons'. Find keys having the specified value of the `revocationReason` attribute.

revocationReasons.description: Find keys having one of the specified values of the `revocationReason` attribute.

createdBefore.description:
Find keys created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g.: 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D" will find keys created
before 1 year, 2 months and 5 days ago.

createdAfter.description:

respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D" will find keys created after 1 year, 2 months
and 5 days ago.

createdAt.description:
Find keys created within 0.5 seconds before or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano

labels.description:
Find keys that match label selector expressions. Multiple values are
logically ANDed.

Label selector expressions:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region=noram" ]
  ```
  OR with a double equals:
  ```
  [ "region==noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region!=noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have either `{"region": "noram"}` or `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region in (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have `{"region": "noram"}` nor `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region notin (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have the label key `region` (the value may be anything)
  ```
  [ "region" ]
  ```
- Select keys that not have the label key `region`
  ```
  [ "!region" ]
  ```

Multiple label selector expressions, logically ANDed:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not have
  `{"team": "sales"}`
  ```
  [ "region=noram", "team!=sales" ]

  ```

post.description:
Create a configuration to generate alarms for either audit or client records. 
Alarms are generated with the given name, description and severity whenever the chosen record type matches the
condition, and the number of records hits a threshold within the given time interval in seconds. Conditions are defined in
[Open Policy Agent's query language Rego](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/how-do-i-write-policies/).
Both records and triggered alarms can have one of the following severity levels:

* critical
* error
* warning
* info

When no severity or description is defined in alarm configuration, then triggered alarms inherit them from records.
When threshold and time interval is not defined in alarm configuration, then the default values for both will be 0
and CM will not check for threshold. The interval value should be specified in seconds.

The following example shows an alarm configuration whose condition is satisfied by the provided record and threshold
hits (since it is set to 1) so it generates an alarm.

Alarm configuration:
```
  {
    "name": "RSA key too small",
    "source_type": "server_record",
    "description": "RSA key should be 2048 bits or higher",
    "severity": "critical",
    "condition": "input.success\ninput.message == \"Create Key\"\ninput.details.algorithm == \"RSA\"\ninput.details.size <= 1024",
    "threshold": 1,
    "interval"  : 10
  }
```
* The properties `name`, `source_type`, `description` and `severity` are used to
  populate properties with the same name in the generated alarm.
* To have alarms triggered from the audit records either omit `source_type` or set it to "server_record". To trigger
  an alarm off of a client record then set it to "client_record"
* The `condition` is a set of assertions that must evaluate to true in
  order to generate an alarm. The first assertion `input.success` says
  that given the input document, which is the record, test if the
  record's `success` property is true. See OPA's 
  [input document](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/how-does-opa-work/#the-input-document) for more information.
* The properties `threshold` and `interval` are used to raise alarm if the number of records fetched within a current time interval hits threshold.

    "id": "059015dc-f476-4e56-9b5f-d5e766b5c139",
    "uri": "kylo:kylo:audit:records:059015dc-f476-4e56-9b5f-d5e766b5c139",
    "account": "kylo:kylo:admin:accounts:kylo",

    "createdAt": "2019-08-09T15:23:44.085148Z",
    "message": "Create Key",
    "service": "minerva",
    "requestId": "735625dd-0673-43fd-8d74-aa1269a34420",
    "success": true,
    "username": "admin",
    "details": {
      "id": "9a0c147806055a5ab6be5215e217e934d740ca8d838cfe61fd1a6a07bd1de242",
      "uri": "kylo:kylo:vault:keys:mykey-v0",
      "name": "mykey",
      "size": 1024,
      "ownerId": "local|9e7f69ef-5bb4-4160-a5d1-7ab3fdb605cd",

(e.g. `input.success` or `input.details.size`) because a record
is the input document in OPA's document model.

Example: generate an alarm when a weak RSA key is created. (All double quotes and newlines must be escaped when inserted as a JSON string.)

```
input.success
input.message == "Create Key"
input.details.algorithm == "RSA"
input.details.size <= 1024
```

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description:
If true, the backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition.
Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to include in the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
By default, no filters are applied and the backup includes all keys.
For example, to back up all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

description.description:
User defined description associated with the backup. This is stored along with the backup,
and is returned while retrieving the backup information, or while listing backups.
For example, users can include a backup name or description, or the ID of the HSM the backup is tied to.

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}"}`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to restore from the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
Only keys resource type is supported to filter. By default, no filters are applied and the restore includes all keys with other resources.
For example, to restore all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

post.description:
Migrate a KeySecure Classic or DSM backup file.
This is the main operation associated with this API.
Be sure to upload the appropriate Migration Split Key before migrating a DSM backup file.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Information needed to perform the migration.

password.description:
This field is used only while migrating KeySecure Classic backup files, and is mandatory for those files.
It specifies the password needed to decrypt the KeySecure Classic backup file.

usersType.description:
This field is used only while migrating KeySecure Classic backup files, and is mandatory for those files.
It specifies the type of user accounts being migrated - local or ldap.

ldapConnectionName.description:
This optional field is used only while migrating KeySecure Classic backup files.
It specifies the name for the LDAP connection being migrated.
It is required only if usersType is set to 'ldap'.

privateKey.description:
It specifies the name or id of the CM key.
It is required only for the cckm product.

domains.description:
This optional field is used only while migrating DSM backup files.
It can be used to specify an array of domains.
All the domains are migrated if this is left empty.

containers.description:
This optional field is used only while migrating DSM backup files.
It can be used to specify an array of containers.

groupName.description:
This optional field is used only while migrating DSM backup files.
It can be used to specify the name of a key-sharing group.
This group is created in all the domains that are migrated.
The keys in the migrated domains will be accessible to all the members of this group.

autoCTEGroups.description:
This optional parameter used only while migrating DSM backup files.
It can be used to control how CTE keys get migrated.
On the DSM, if a key has the "Source" field set to "From DSM" or an
empty string, and this flag is set to true, the key is migrated so that
it is fully accessible to members of the "CTE Clients" group.

migrateCCKMSourceKeys.description:
This optional parameter used only while migrating CCKM Enterprise Keys.
If this flag is set to true, the key created in DSM from CCKM enterprise
will be migrated to CipherTrust Manager.

migrateOnlyCCKMSourceKeys.description:
This optional parameter used only while migrating DSM source keys created in CCKM Enterprise.
If this flag is set to true, the key created in DSM from CCKM enterprise
will be migrated to CipherTrust Manager.

migrateCloudKeysWithExternalCm.description:
This optional parameter used only while migrating cloud keys created in CCKM Enterprise.
If this flag is set to true, the cloud key created in CCKM enterprise
will be migrated to CipherTrust Manager if DSM source keys migration done.

migrateDsmKeysToExternalCmFromCm.description:
This optional parameter used only while migrating source keys from DSM to External CipherTrust Manager when the cloud keys from CCKM Enterprise are already migrated to CipherTrust Manager.
If this flag is set to true, the source keys from DSM to External CipherTrust Manager will be migrated.

updateCloudKeysWithExternalCMKeys.description:
This is an optional parameter. Use this flag to update linking of cloud keys with DSM as keysource to External CM.
If this flag is set to true, The source keys of the cloud keys will be updated with the corresponding migrated External CipherTrust Manager key.

externalCMDomainID.description:
This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
It is used to provide the domain which belongs the external CM, where the keys are to be migrated.

externalCMConnection.description:
This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
It is used to provide the connection of the external CM from which the keys are to be migrated.

migrateDKESourceKeys.description:
This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
It is used to execute CCKM DKE Keys migration.

keyOwners.description:
This optional parameter is a JSON object used only while migrating data from DSM to the CipherTrust Manager.
This parameter contains the key-value pairs. 
The key corresponds to the domain in the DSM backup and the value is the user id of an existing user in the root domain of the CipherTrust Manager. 
After migration, this value (user id) will be assigned to the corresponding new domain and will be the owner of all keys in that domain.
If no key owner is provided during migration, then the default owner will be the migration user.
For example: {domain1 : local|f224bced-800b-4103-9d94-5e5a6034706f}
Here domain1 is the domain name which will be migrated from the DSM and local|f224bced-800b-4103-9d94-5e5a6034706f
is the id of the user created on the CipherTrust Manager.

private key. This API does not store any state on the server as
everything is returned back in the result. This means that both the CSR
and the private key must be stored securely on the client side.

The private key can optionally be encrypted with a password. It is
strongly recommended to encrypt the private key.

post.description:
Performs the initial setup of the system to use HSM.

A `reset` operation is required. This means that all existing data in
the system will be wiped and CipherTrust Manager will be started from a clean
slate.

Note:
  This is a long running operation and could take some time, the
  browser might timeout before the operation completes. If you get a
  timeout error then the operation started successfully and you will
  need to `list` to determine if it has completed

Note:
  It is important that time is in sync when using HSM. Please ensure
  the system time is correct before.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: HSM setup parameters

type.description: Type of HSM server to setup, supported types are "luna", "lunapci", "lunatct", "protectserver", "aws", "dpod", "gcp", "nshield" and "ibmhpcs". "luna" refers to the Luna Network HSM version 5, 6, or 7, "lunapci" refers to the embedded Luna PCIe HSM, "lunatct" refers to the Luna T-Series HSMs, "protectserver" refers to ProtectServer HSM, "aws" refers to AWS CloudHSM, "dpod" refers to Thales Data Protection on Demand's HSM on Demand service, "gcp" refers to Google Cloud HSM, "nshield" refers to Entrust nShield Connect HSM, and "ibmhpcs" refers to IBM HPCS HSM.

connInfo.description:
Connection information for initial HSM to setup in JSON document format. The expected content of this parameter depends on the specific HSM type used.

For Luna Network HSM (including TCT) and Luna PCIe, the required attributes are:

- "partition_name"  
  The name of the HSM partition to use.

- "partition_password"  
  The password of the initial partition to use. This will be the Crypto Officer role password or challenge secret. Luna documentation describes in detail how to set up a password for an application to access a partition.  
  If you plan to use multiple Luna HSMs operating in high-availability (HA) mode, all HSMs must have the same password.

For ProtectServer HSM, the required attributes are:

- "token_serial"  
  The serial number of the slot.

- "token_password"  
  The password of the slot.

For AWS Cloud HSM (Cavium), the required attributes are:

- "partition_name"
  This must have the value "cavium".

- "partition_password"
  The credentials of a cryptouser in the form of "username:password"

For DPoD HSM on Demand Service, the required attributes are:

- "partition_name"
  The name of the the partition configured during partition initialization

- "partition_password"
  The password of the Crypto Officer

For Google Cloud HSM, the required attributes are:

- "type"
  The type of the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account. The value must be `service_account`. The service account must be granted a role or roles with the following IAM permissions: `cloudkms.keyRings.get` in the location, `cloudkms.locations.generateRandomBytes` in the location, `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.list`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.list`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.manageRawAesCbcKeys`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToVerify`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.create` and `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.destroy` in the keyring.

- "project_id"
  The project ID of the GCP service account.

- "private_key_id"
  The private key ID of the GCP service account.

- "private_key"
  The private key of the GCP service account.

- "client_email"
  The client email of the GCP service account.

- "client_id"
  The client ID of the GCP service account.

- "auth_uri"
  The auth URI of the GCP service account.

- "token_uri"
  The token URI of the GCP service account.

- "auth_provider_x509_cert_url"
  The auth provider X509 cert URL of the GCP service account.

- "client_x509_cert_url"
  The client X509 cert URL of the GCP service account.

For Entrust nShield Connect HSM, the required parameters are:

- "softcard_name"  
  The name of the softcard to use to protect the keys.

- "softcard_password"  
  The password of the softcard.

For IBM HPCS HSM the required parameter is:

- "api_key"  
    The api key for the Normal User with Key operator privileges.

Luna Network/PCIe HSM (including TCT) example:  
`"{\"partition_name\": \"kylo-partition\", \"partition_password\": \"sOmeP@ssword\"}"`

ProtectServer example:  
`"{\"token_serial\": \"123456:54321\", \"token_password\": \"sOmeP@ssword\"}"`

AWS CloudHSM (Cavium) example:  
`"{\"partition_name\": \"cavium\", \"partition_password\": \"hsmuser:sOmeP@ssword\"}"`

DPoD example:  
`"{\"partition_name\": \"partition-name\", \"partition_password\": \"sOmeP@ssword\"}"`

initialConfig.description:
A free form JSON opaque blob. The expected content of this parameter depends on the specific HSM type used.

For Luna Network HSM (including TCT) the required attributes are:
- "host"
  IP or hostname
- "serial"
  Serial number of the partition to use
- "server-cert"
  Server certificate in PEM format. Line breaks in PEM string must be replaced with "\n".
  For externally signed server certs (not supported on TCT), append all certificates in the signing chain.
- "client-cert"
  Client certificate in PEM format. Line breaks in PEM string must be replaced with "\n".
- "client-cert-key"
  Client private key in PEM format. Line breaks in PEM string must be replaced with "\n".

For Luna Network HSM using the STC protocol, the required attributes are:
- "host"
  IP or hostname
- "serial"
  Serial number of the partition to use
- "server-cert"
  Server certificate in PEM format. Line breaks in PEM string must be replaced with "\n".
- "stc-par-identity"
  STC partition identity encoded as a base64 string without line breaks (base64 -w0 1234567890123.pid)
Note that this instance's STC client identity (see /system/hsm/clients/stcidentity) must be registered externally prior to invoking this API.

Luna PCIe HSM (including TCT) does not require any attribute. initialConfig shall be omitted.

For ProtectServer HSM, the attributes are:
- "host"
  IP or hostname of the ProtectServer HSM (required)
- "port"
  Port number of the ProtectServer HSM. (optional, defaults to 12396)
- "server_cert"
  The HSM server certificate of the ProtectServer HSM (required)

For AWS CloudHSM (Cavium) the required attributes are:
- "host"
  ENI IP Address of cloudhsm cluster.
- "server-cert"
  CloudHSM cluster certificate in PEM format. Line breaks in PEM string must be replaced with "\n".

For Google Cloud HSM the required attributes are:
- "location"
  Google Cloud Location of the key ring. It should match location specified in GCP Project for Google Cloud HSM.
- "key_ring"
  Name of key ring that contains the Cloud HSM key. This key ring must exist on specified Google Cloud Location.

For Google Cloud HSM the optional attribute is:
- "project_id"
  ID of the GCP project where the key ring is in. If not specified, default to the ID of the project the service account belongs to.

For Entrust nShield Connect HSM the required attributes are:
- "host"
  IP Address of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.
- "serial"
  Electronic Serial Number (ESN) of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.
- "hkneti"
  Hash of the KNETI key (HKNETI) of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.
- "rfs_host"
  IP Address of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM's Remote File System (RFS).

For Entrust nShield Connect HSM the optional attributes are:
- "port"
  Port number of the nShield Connect HSM. If not specified, default to 9004.
- "rfs_port"
  Port number of the nShield Connect HSM's RFS. If not specified, default to 9004.

For IBM HPCS HSM the required attributes are:
- "host"
  Host name or IP Address of cloudhsm server.
- "port"
  Port number of cloudhsm server .
- "instance_id"
  Instance ID of IBM HPCS instance.
- "token_space_id"
  IBM HPCS token space ID.

Luna Network HSM (including TCT) example:

    {
      "host": "172.20.32.11",
      "serial": "1234",
      "server-cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "client-cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "client-cert-key": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n...\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
    }

ProtectServer HSM example:

    {
      "host": "172.20.32.11",
      "port": "12396",
      "server_cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }

AWS CloudHSM example:

    {
      "host": "172.20.32.11",
      "server-cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }

DPoD example:

    Cloud HSMoD (DPoD) client:

    {
      "server_cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "partition_ca_cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "partition_cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
      "cv_partition_data": "Chrystoki-conf-PartitionData00",
      "auth_token_config_uri": "Chrystoki-conf-AuthTokenConfigURI",
      "auth_token_client_id": "Chrystoki-conf-AuthTokenClientId",
      "auth_token_client_secret": "Chrystoki-conf-AuthTokenClientSecret"
    }

GCP Cloud HSM example:

    {
      "location": "us-east1",
      "key_ring": "my-keyring"
    }

Entrust nShield Connect HSM example:

    {
      "host": "10.194.173.39",
      "serial": "AB03-02E0-D947",
      "hkneti": "4a7b4d770abc415654cd2b50a25dd38aafce8d60",
      "rfs_host": "10.194.173.70"
    }

IBM HPCS HSM example:


    {
      "host": "ep11.us-south.hs-crypto.cloud.ibm.com"
      "port": "9253",
      "instance_id": "4ec51d44-d94d-4200-bc2c-fcfb04b1287c`"
      "token_space_id": "12c2c67d-9bfe-4e73-a97f-9902913daf6f"
    }

Note: JSON does not allow line-breaks, it needs to be replaced with \n. Use "sed -z 's/\n/\\n/g' cert-file.pem" command to format the certificate.

post.description:
Adds a new HSM server for high-availability (HA) and load balancing. Only supported for Luna Network HSM (including TCT), AWS cloud HSM, and Entrust nShield Connect HSM.

Luna Network HSM (including TCT) specific notes:
- The partition password as provided during HSM setup must be the same for all servers in the same HA group
- The call will fail if the partition on the joining node contains objects. It must be manually cleared using the Luna toolset, or either one of the forceClear or forceCopy optional attributes specified for this operation to succeed. Refer to CipherTrust Manager Administration Guide for more details.

AWS cloud HSM notes:
- The AWS cloud HSM being added must belong to the same AWS cloud HSM cluster.

Entrust nShield Connect HSM specific note:
- The new HSM server being added must belong to the same Security World as existing setup or added HSM server(s).

Note:
  This is a long running operation and could take some time, the
  browser might timeout before the operation completes. If you get a
  timeout error then the operation started successfully and you will
  need to `list` to determine if it has completed

parameters.description: HSM servers parameters

config.description:
Connection information for the HSM to add as a free form JSON opaque blob. The expected content of this parameter depends on the specific HSM type being added.

For Luna Network HSM (including TCT) the required attributes are:
- "host"
  IP or hostname
- "server-cert"
  Server certificate in PEM format
- "serial"
  Serial number of the partition to use, this is used to ensure the correct partition is added to the HA group

For Luna Network HSM (including TCT) the optional attributes are:
- "forceClear"
  When set to "true", forcefully clears all existing data on the partition of the joining node before adding it to the HA group. Use with caution. Refer to CipherTrust Manager Administration Guide for more details.
- "forceCopy"
  When set to "true", all existing objects on the joining partition are retained and propagated within the HA group. Use with caution. Refer to CipherTrust Manager Administration Guide for more details.
- "stc-par-identity"
  Specify this parameter to use the STC protocol to the Luna Network HSM partition. The STC partition identity must encoded as a base64 string without line breaks (base64 -w0 1234567890123.pid)
  Note that this instance's STC client identity (see /system/hsm/clients/stcidentity) must be registered externally prior to invoking this API.

For Entrust nShield Connect HSM the required attributes are:
- "host"
  IP Address of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.
- "serial"
  Electronic Serial Number (ESN) of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.
- "hkneti"
  Hash of the KNETI key (HKNETI) of the Entrust nShield Connect HSM.

For Entrust nShield Connect HSM the optional attribute is:
- "port"
  Port number of the nShield Connect HSM. If not specified, default to 9004.

For AWS cloud HSM, the required attribute is:
- "host"
  IP Address of the AWS cloud HSM

patch.description:
Modify the network interface configuration asynchronously. Since the final result is not known, GET with the same path can be used periodically to check if the change is applied successfully.
When inet or inet6 has existing values and the request method is 'static' then any property absent from the request inherits the existing value.  For example, if the interface is configured to use DHCP and the modify request only contains 'ip' and 'dns', then the existing values for netmask and gateway are applied as part of the static configuration.
If 'bond' is provided then it is ignored. These values can only be modified via the console or ssh using 'nmcli'.
Please note there is a risk that modifying a network interface remotely using this API may make communication with the node impossible without console access.

post.description:
Adds a new CipherTrust Manager client on the CipherTrust Manager. Specify the following details.
- Name for the CipherTrust Manager client (optional).
- Client Registration Token.
- Client Type (optional).
 
- Specify any one of the following fields
  - Certificate signing request.
  - CSR params.
  - Client Certificate in case when clients bring their own certs.
- If cert_duration is present in both Client Profile and Registration Token then the preference will be given to the cert_duration present in client profile. If cert_duration is neither provided in Client Profile nor in Client Registration Tokens then server will use 730 days by default during registration.
- If ca_id is present in both Client Profile and Registration Token then the preference will be given to the ca_id present in registration token.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: CipherTrust Manager client parameters

name.description: Name for the CipherTrust Manager client to display on CipherTrust Manager.

csr.description: Certificate signing request to be signed by CipherTrust Manager.

subject_dn_field_to_modify.description:
This field makes the Subject Distinguished Name (Subject DN) unique. It is required when the Subject DN from client's CSR is not unique.
By default, the `UID` is used to modify the Subject DN. However, Subject DN can be modified based on the following fields.
If one of these fields (except OU) is chosen, the original field values is overridden by the CipherTrust Manager.
If OU is chosen, the OU gets appended in the Subject DN with other attributes.
To prevent Subject DN from being modified, set the `do_not_modify_subject_dn` flag to `true`.

do_not_modify_subject_dn.description:
Specifies if Subject DN in the CSR is allowed to be modified or not.
If this flag is set to true, then Subject DN must be unique across all the CipherTrust Manager clients, otherwise registration will not be allowed.
This flag is applicable if client is registered using a presented CSR.

algorithm.description:
RSA or ECDSA (default) algorithms are supported. Signature algorithm (SHA512WithRSA, SHA384WithRSA,
SHA256WithRSA, SHA1WithRSA, ECDSAWithSHA512, ECDSAWithSHA384, ECDSAWithSHA256) is selected
based on the algorithm and size.

names.description:
Name fields are "O=organization, OU=organizational unit, L=location, ST=state/province, C=country".

Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

name.description: Name to uniquely identify the client. This name will be visible on the CipherTrust Manager.

communication_enabled.description: Whether communication with the client is enabled. The default value is `false`. Can be set to `true` only if `registration_allowed` is `true`.

client_locked.description: Whether the CTE client is locked. The default value is `false`. Enable this option to lock the configuration of the CTE Agent on the client. Set to `true` to lock the configuration, set to `false` to unlock. Locking the Agent configuration prevents updates to any policies on the client.

system_locked.description: Whether the system is locked. The default value is false. Enable this option to lock the important operating system files of the client. When enabled, patches to the operating system of the client will fail due to the protection of these files.

client_type.description: Type of CTE Client. The default value is FS. Valid values are CTE-U and FS.

    "labels": {
      "key1": "value1",
      "key2": "value2"
    }

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

`DOCKER` - Docker Support. Avaiable on RedHat and CentOS Linux only.

`IDT` - Inplace Data Transformation capable.

`COS` - Cloud Storage Protection. Available for S3 only.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection capable.

`CLOG` - Concise Logging.

`RESIGN` - Re-Sign Client Settings.

`EA` - Secure Start GuardPoint. Available on Windows only.

`CBCCS1` - CBC-CS1 encryption mode capable.

`XTS` - XTS encryption mode capable.

`QOS` - LDT rekey quality of service capable.

`XRULE` - LDT key rule exclusion capable.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

Notifies the CipherTrust Manager to delete multiple clients. Both the *del_client* and *force_del_client* options are mutually exclusive.

password.description:
Password for the client if password_creation_method is manual. Agents use this password to encrypt the data encryption key (DEK).
The password MUST be minimum 8 characters and MUST contain one alphabet, one number, and one of the !@#$%^&*(){}[] special characters.

- A CTE agent encrypts the DEK when it passes between the client and the CipherTrust Manager.
- A VDE agent encrypts the DEK saved on the disk.
This password is used for the challenge and response to unlock the agent when the client and the CipherTrust Manager are unreachable

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password for the client, GENERATE or MANUAL. The default method is GENERATE.

GENERATE – Client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager administrator each time a client password is required.
When GENERATE is specified, the Regenerate Password option is displayed on the GUI. Use this option to generate a new random
password and download it to the client. This new password is used to wrap the DEK.
MANUAL – Specify password for unlocking a GuardPoint when the CipherTrust Manager is unreachable. The Password and Confirm Password options are
displayed on the GUI to re-enter the password.

system_locked.description: Whether the system is locked. The default value is false. Enable this option to lock the important operating system files of the client. When enabled, patches to the operating system of the client will fail due to the protection of these files.

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

get.description: Returns the list of CTE profiles. The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter result using the profile name.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

get.description: Returns the list of policies added to the CipherTrust Manager. The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: never_deny
parameters.description: Filters results to those learn mode enabled or disabled.

parameters.name: never_deny_enabled_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those learn mode enabled at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter result using the policy name.

parameters.name: policy_type
parameters.description: Filter policies by policy type.Valid values are STANDARD, LDT, IDT, CLOUD_OBJECT_STORAGE and CSI.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

allOf.description:
The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

skip.description:
The index of the first record returned.  Equivalent to 'offset' in
SQL.

limit.description: The max number of records returned.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL.

Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

`COS` - Cloud Storage Protection. Available for S3 only.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection capable.

`CLOG` - Concise Logging.

`RESIGN` - Re-Sign Client Settings.

`EA` - Secure Start GuardPoint. Available on Windows only.

`CBCCS1` - CBC-CS1 encryption mode capable.

`XTS` - XTS encryption mode capable.

`QOS` - LDT rekey quality of service capable.

server_host_name.description: Host name or IP address of the key server.

client_locked.description: Whether to lock the client. Use this tag to lock/unlock the configuration of the File System Agent on the client. Locking the configuration prevents updates to policies on the client. The default value is false.

system_locked.description: Whether the system is locked. The default value is false. Enable this option to lock the important operating system files of the client. When enabled, patches to the operating system of the client will fail due to the protection of these files.

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

capabilities.description:
Comma-separated agent capabilities.  Available options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation. Implies `QOS` and `XRULE`.              

`DOCKER` - Docker Support. Avaiable on RedHat and CentOS Linux only.

`IDT` - Inplace Data Transformation capable.

`COS` - Cloud Storage Protection. Available for S3 only.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection capable.

`CLOG` - Concise Logging.

`RESIGN` - Re-Sign Client Settings.

`EA` - Secure Start GuardPoint. Available on Windows only.

`CBCCS1` - CBC-CS1 encryption mode capable.

`XTS` - XTS encryption mode capable.

`QOS` - LDT rekey quality of service capable.

`XRULE` - LDT key rule exclusion capable.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

enabled_capabilities.description:
Enable disabled feature(s). Separate multiple features by commas. The options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

disable_capability.description:

client_locked.description: Whether to lock the client. Use this tag to lock/unlock the configuration of the File System Agent on the client. Locking the configuration prevents updates to policies on the client. The default value is false.

system_locked.description: Whether the system is locked. The default value is false. Enable this option to lock the important operating system files of the client. When enabled, patches to the operating system of the client will fail due to the protection of these files.

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

capabilities.description:
Comma-separated agent capabilities.  Available options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation. Implies `QOS` and `XRULE`.              

`DOCKER` - Docker Support. Avaiable on RedHat and CentOS Linux only.

`IDT` - Inplace Data Transformation capable.

`COS` - Cloud Storage Protection. Available for S3 only.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection capable.

`CLOG` - Concise Logging.

`RESIGN` - Re-Sign Client Settings.

`EA` - Secure Start GuardPoint. Available on Windows only.

`CBCCS1` - CBC-CS1 encryption mode capable.

`XTS` - XTS encryption mode capable.

`QOS` - LDT rekey quality of service capable.

`XRULE` - LDT key rule exclusion capable.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

enabled_capabilities.description:
Enable disabled feature(s). Separate multiple features by commas. The options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

parameters.name: domain_name
parameters.description:
Filter reports by domain name.
To filter reports by multiple domains, provide comma-delimited list of domains.
For example: domain1,domain2

parameters.name: client_name
parameters.description: Filter report by Client name.

parameters.name: client_type
parameters.description: Filter clients by Client type. Valid values are FS, CSI, CTE-U.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter clients by client health status. Valid values are UNREGISTERED, ERROR, WARNING, HEALTHY, EXPUNGED, WAITING FOR CONNECTION, NOT CONNECTED.
To filter clients by multiple status provide comma-delimited list of status.
For example: HEALTHY,WARNING
...will filter clients which have HEALTHY or WARNING client health status.

parameters.name: os_type
parameters.description: Filter clients by os type of client.Valid values are LINUX, WINDOWS, AIX, FREEBSD and UNKNOWN. To filter clients by multiple os provide comma-delimited list of os.

parameters.name: using_hwsig
parameters.description: Filter clients by hardware association enablement status. Valid values are YES, NO and N/A (not applicable).

parameters.name: exclude_domain_sharing_data
parameters.description: Whether to exclude domain sharing data in reports or not. Valid values are true/false.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed. 

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not 
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
Valid values are client_name,status,os_type,total_gp,enabled_gp.
For example:

     client_name,-status

...will sort the results first by `client_name`, ascending, then by `status`, descending.

client_locked.description: Whether to lock the client. Use this tag to lock/unlock the configuration of the File System Agent on the client. Locking the configuration prevents updates to policies on the client. The default value is false.

system_locked.description: Whether the system is locked. The default value is false. Enable this option to lock the important operating system files of the client. When enabled, patches to the operating system of the client will fail due to the protection of these files.

password_creation_method.description:
Method to create password (GENERATE, MANUAL). Default value is `GENERATE`.
The client uses this password as a wrapper to encrypt the data encryption key when it passes between the
client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v in the case of a CTE agent client, or saved to disk in the case of a VDE agent. This same
password is used for the challenge and response, to unlock the agent when there is no network connection
between the client and the CipherTrust Manager k170v.

`GENERATE` - When `GENERATE` is selected, the client user must request a new password from a CipherTrust Manager k170v
administrator each time a client password is required. If GENERATE is selected, the Regenerate Password
option is displayed, select to download a new randomly generated password to the client. This new password
will be used to wrap the data encryption key.

`MANUAL` - Enter the password for unlocking a GuardPoint when there is no server connection.
Password / Confirm Password, displayed when Password Creation Method is set to MANUAL, re-enter the
password.

capabilities.description:
Comma-separated agent capabilities.  Available options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation. Implies `QOS` and `XRULE`.              

`DOCKER` - Docker Support. Avaiable on RedHat and CentOS Linux only.

`IDT` - Inplace Data Transformation capable.

`COS` - Cloud Storage Protection. Available for S3 only.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection capable.

`CLOG` - Concise Logging.

`RESIGN` - Re-Sign Client Settings.

`EA` - Secure Start GuardPoint. Available on Windows only.

`CBCCS1` - CBC-CS1 encryption mode capable.

`XTS` - XTS encryption mode capable.

`QOS` - LDT rekey quality of service capable.

`XRULE` - LDT key rule exclusion capable.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

enabled_capabilities.description:
Enable disabled feature(s). Separate multiple features by commas. The options are:

`LDT` - Live Data Transformation.

`EKP` - Encryption Key Protection.

`LDT_P` - Live Data Transformation Passive.

disable_capability.description:
