CCKM Synchronization operation specific arguments. Should be JSON-serializable
"key_rotation_params", "database_backup_params" and "cckm_synchronization_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
Required only for "cckm_synchronization" operations. Not allowed for other operations.
cckm_synchronization_params.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Synchronization Parameters

cloud_name.description: Name of the cloud in which the Synchronize operation will be triggered. The possible values are "aws", "hsm-luna", "dsm" , "oci", "sfdc", "gcp", "sap", "external-cm" and "AzureCloud".

kms.description: IDs or names of kms resource from which Aws keys will be synchronized. Kms is used for aws cloud. At least one kms is required for aws synchronization operation.

key_vaults.description: IDs or name of vault from which azure keys will be synchronized. Vaults are used for azure cloud. At least one vault is required for azure synchronization operation.

sync_item.description: Items which need to be synchronized. At least one of the values from below is required for azure synchronization operation.

partitions.description: IDs of partition from which keys will be synchronized. Partitions are used for HSM. At least one partition is required for HSM synchronization operation.

domains.description: IDs of domains from which keys will be synchronized. Domains are used for DSM. At least one domain is required for DSM synchronization operation.

key_rings.description: IDs or name of key ring from which google cryptographic keys will be synchronized. Key Rings are used for google cloud. At least one key ring is required for google synchronization operation.

organizations.description: Organization ID from which tenant secrets will be synchronized. Provide CCKM organization ID. At least one organization ID is required for sfdc synchronization operation.

groups.description: Group ID from which sap key will be synchronized. Provide CCKM group ID. At least one group ID is required for sap synchronization operation.

oci_vaults.description: Vault ID from which oci key will be synchronized. Provide CCKM OCI vault ID. At least one vault ID is required for oci synchronization operation.

external_cm_domains.description: IDs of external cm domains from which keys will be synchronized. At least one external cm domain is required for external CM synchronization operation.

synchronize_all.description: Set true to synchronize all keys from all vaults or kms. synchronize_all, key_vaults and kms are mutually exclusive. Specify either the synchronize_all or key_vaults or kms.

take_cloud_key_backup.description: Set true to take cloud key backup of all keys of the vaults. Only applicable for Azure.

cloud_name.description: Name of the cloud for which the operation will be triggered. Supported values are "gcp" , "aws" & "AzureCloud".

connection.description: Resource ID of the connection for which the containers need to be fetched.

permit.description: Whether to permit users to perform specific operations. Set true to permit or false to deny.

enable_success_audit_event.description:
Enable or disable audit recording of successful operations within an external key store. Default value is false.
Recommended value is false as enabling it can affect performance. Applicable for 'gcp' cloud only.

discover_only.description:
Whether to only discover the KMS containers. Set to `false` to discover the containers and add them to CCKM.

aws_params.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Add Container AWS Parameters

auto_archive.description: Whether to set not-found KMSes, as ARCHIVED.

filter.description:
Filter to be applied on discovered accounts, before adding to CCKM. Each filter will be of key-value pair type and multiple filters can be specified in the string, separated by the ampersand (&) operator. 
Filters will also support wildcard matching using '?' and '\*' to allow customers to filter based on sub-string, starts with or ends with. Filtering will be supported based on 'Root'{Arn, Id, Name, Tag}, 'OrganizationalUnit'{Arn, Id, Name, Tag} and 'Account'{Arn, Email, Id, Name, Tag} resource attributes.
Example : Account.Name=Demo&Account.Id=1243545
Account.Name=Demo&OrganizationalUnit.Name=DemoOrg\*
OrganizationalUnit.Tag=department:eng?neering&Root.Id=r-cuc9

"cckm_key_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
cckm_synchronization_params.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Synchronization Parameters

cloud_name.description: Name of the cloud in which the Synchronize operation will be triggered. The possible values are "aws", "hsm-luna", "dsm" , "oci", "sfdc", "gcp", "sap", "external-cm" and "AzureCloud".

kms.description: IDs or names of kms resource from which Aws keys will be synchronized. Kms is used for aws cloud. At least one kms is required for aws synchronization operation.

key_vaults.description: IDs or name of vault from which azure keys will be synchronized. Vaults are used for azure cloud. At least one vault is required for azure synchronization operation.

sync_item.description: Items which need to be synchronized. At least one of the values from below is required for azure synchronization operation.

partitions.description: IDs of partition from which keys will be synchronized. Partitions are used for HSM. At least one partition is required for HSM synchronization operation.

domains.description: IDs of domains from which keys will be synchronized. Domains are used for DSM. At least one domain is required for DSM synchronization operation.

key_rings.description: IDs or name of key ring from which google cryptographic keys will be synchronized. Key Rings are used for google cloud. At least one key ring is required for google synchronization operation.

organizations.description: Organization ID from which tenant secrets will be synchronized. Provide CCKM organization ID. At least one organization ID is required for sfdc synchronization operation.

groups.description: Group ID from which sap key will be synchronized. Provide CCKM group ID. At least one group ID is required for sap synchronization operation.

oci_vaults.description: Vault ID from which oci key will be synchronized. Provide CCKM OCI vault ID. At least one vault ID is required for oci synchronization operation.

external_cm_domains.description: IDs of external cm domains from which keys will be synchronized. At least one external cm domain is required for external CM synchronization operation.

synchronize_all.description: Set true to synchronize all keys from all vaults or kms. synchronize_all, key_vaults and kms are mutually exclusive. Specify either the synchronize_all or key_vaults or kms.

take_cloud_key_backup.description: Set true to take cloud key backup of all keys of the vaults. Only applicable for Azure.

cckm_key_rotation_params.description:
CCKM Key Rotation operation specific arguments. The "key_rotation_params","database_backup_params",
"cckm_synchronization_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
cckm_key_rotation_params.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Synchronization Parameters

cloud_name.description: Name of the cloud in which the Rotation operation will be triggered. The possible values are "aws", "gcp", "oci" , "sfdc", "sap", "sap-ekm", "microsoft-dke" and "AzureCloud".

expiration.description: Expiration time of the new key that will be created through scheduled rotation. If not specified, the new key material never expires. For example, if you set `expiration` to `6h`, the key material of the new key will expire in 6 hours.

expire_in.description: Period during which certain keys are going to expire. When the scheduler is run, it rotates the keys that are expiring in this period. If not specified, the scheduler rotates all the keys. For example, if you want the scheduler to rotate the keys that are expiring within six hours of the schedule run, set `expire_in` to `6h`. This parameter is not valid for cloud_name `gcp`.

aws_param.description: AWS param specifies whether to retain alias with timestamp on archieved key after rotation.
aws_param.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Synchronization Parameters

retain_alias.description: Whether to retain alias with timestamp on archieved key after rotation.

rotate_material.description: Whether to rotate material. When set to true, key material of the key will be rotated. Set to false, will create a new key and move the alias as part of rotation.

sfdc_param.description: SFDC param specifies oraganization_id and key_type for which keys will be rotated.
sfdc_param.title: CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager Synchronization Parameters

organization_id.description: Organization ID to which this key type belongs.

key_type.description: Type of tenant secret requested for which sfdc keys will be rotated and can have the following values.

key_source.description: Source of the key material. Options are `native`, `hsm-luna`, `dsm`, 'external-cm` and `ciphertrust`.

certificate_id.description: (Mandatorily required for SFDC cloud) Certificate ID, whose public key to be used to encrypt tenant secret.

key_derivation_mode.description: (Mandatorily required for SFDC cloud) Values are PBKDF2 or NONE.

domain_id.description: Domain ID where key will be created to upload on sfdc.

partition_id.description: Partition ID where key will be created to upload on sfdc.

external_cm_domain_id.description: External CM Domain ID where key will be created to upload on sfdc.

rotation_after.description: Number of days after which the keys will be rotated. Specify `Xd` for `x` days. The first key rotation will happen after `x` days of key creation. Subsequent key rotations will happen after every `x` days of the last rotation date. For example, if you set `rotation_after` to `6d`, the first key rotation will happen after six days of key creation. Subsequently, the keys will be rotated after every six days.

user_password_expiry_notification_params.description:
User password expiry notification operation specific arguments. 
This operation is applicable only for password based auth users whose notification is enabled in policy. 
There is default job created by system to check and send email notification for all users whose 
password is about to expire as defined in password policy (if email is configured).
*NOTE*: This job can only be in root domain and there can be only one such job in CM.

parameters.description: The ID of the object.

get.description: Returns information about the requested job configuration.

id.description: The unique identifier of the resource

uri.description: A human readable unique identifier of the resource

account.description: The account which owns this resource.

application.description: The application this resource belongs to.

devAccount.description: The developer account which owns this resource's application.

operation.description: Type of operation to configure. Possible values are "Key Rotation", "Database Backup", "Sync CRL", "CCKM Synchronization" and "CCKM XKS Credential Rotation".

run_at.description:
Described using the cron expression format : "* * * * *"
These five values indicate when the job should be executed. They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.
Valid values are 0-59 (minutes), 0-23 (hours), 1-31 (day of month), 1-12 or jan-dec (month), and 0-6 or sun-sat (day of week). Names are case insensitive. For use of special characters, consult the Time Specification description at the top of this page.

For example:
* To run every min: "* * * * *"
* To run on Saturday at 23:45(11:45 PM): "45 23 * * 6"
* To run on Monday at 09:00: "0 9 * * 1"

run_on.description:
Optional flag. Default is 'any'.
* Use 'any' to run the config on any node in the cluster.
* Use '<specific node id>' to run the config on that node.

disabled.description: By default, the job configuration starts in an active state. True disables the job configuration.

start_date.description:
Date the job configuration becomes active. RFC3339 format.
For example, 2018-10-02T14:24:37.436073Z

end_date.description:
Date the job configuration becomes inactive. RFC3339 format.
For example, 2018-10-02T14:24:37.436073Z

key_rotation_params.description:
Key rotation operation specific arguments. The "key_rotation_params","database_backup_params",
"cckm_synchronization_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
key_rotation_params.title: Key Rotation Parameters

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

query.description:
Use this object to specify the keys that need to be rotated.
All keys are rotated when this object is not specified.
This object is the same as the one used for POST request to the /v1/vault/query-keys endpoint.
Refer to the documentation in that endpoint for further details on formulating the query.

meta.description:
Use this object to modify the metadata on a key that is replaced by the key rotation procedure.
This object should be a JSON serialized object. The metadata on the replaced key (which is
also a JSON object) is merged with this JSON object.

database_backup_params.description:
Database backup operation specific arguments. Should be JSON-serializable
"key_rotation_params", "cckm_synchronization_params", "cckm_key_rotation_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_rotation_params" fields are mutually
exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
database_backup_params.title: Database Backup Parameters

scope.description: Scope of the backup to be taken - system (default) or domain.

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description: If true, the system backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition. Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to include in the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
By default, no filters are applied and the backup includes all keys.
For example, to back up all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

retentionCount.description: Number of backups saved for this job config. Default is an unlimited quantity.

description.description: User defined description associated with the backup. This is stored along with the backup, and is returned while retrieving the backup information, or while listing backups. Users may find it useful to store various types of information here: a backup name or description, ID of the HSM the backup is tied to, etc.

do_scp.description: If true, the system backup will also be transferred to the external server via SCP.

connection.description: Name or ID of the SCP connection which stores the details for SCP server.

expiration.description: Expiration time of the new key that will be created through scheduled rotation. If not specified, the new key material never expires. For example, if you set `expiration` to `6h`, the key material of the new key will expire in 6 hours.

expire_in.description: Period during which certain keys are going to expire. When the scheduler is run, it rotates the keys that are expiring in this period. If not specified, the scheduler rotates all the keys. For example, if you want the scheduler to rotate the keys that are expiring within six hours of the schedule run, set `expire_in` to `6h`. This parameter is not valid for cloud_name "gcp".

rotation_after.description:
Number of days after which the keys will be rotated. Specify `Xd` for `x` days. The first key rotation will happen after `x` days of key creation. Subsequent key rotations will happen after every `x` days of the last rotation date.
For example, if you set `rotation_after` to `6d`, the first key rotation will happen after six days of key creation. Subsequently, the keys will be rotated after every six days.

Filters will also support wildcard matching using '?' and '\*' to allow customers to filter based on sub-string, starts with or ends with. run_at.description:
Described using the cron expression format : "* * * * *"
These five values indicate when the job should be executed. They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.
Valid values are 0-59 (minutes), 0-23 (hours), 1-31 (day of month), 1-12 or jan-dec (month), and 0-6 or sun-sat (day of week). Names are case insensitive. For use of special characters, consult the Time Specification description at the top of this page.

For example:
* To run every min: "* * * * *"
* To run on Saturday at 23:45(11:45 PM): "45 23 * * 6"
* To run on Monday at 09:00: "0 9 * * 1"

run_on.description:
Optional flag. Default is 'any'.
* Use 'any' to run the config on any node in the cluster.
* Use '<specific node id>' to run the config on that node.

"cckm_synchronization_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
key_rotation_params.title: Key Rotation Parameters

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

scope.description: Scope of the backup to be taken - system (default) or domain.

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description: If true, the system backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition. Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to include in the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
By default, no filters are applied and the backup includes all keys.
For example, to back up all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

retentionCount.description: Number of backups saved for this job config. Default is an unlimited quantity.

description.description: User defined description associated with the backup. This is stored along with the backup, and is returned while retrieving the backup information, or while listing backups. Users may find it useful to store various types of information here: a backup name or description, ID of the HSM the backup is tied to, etc.

do_scp.description: If true, the system backup will also be transferred to the external server via SCP.

connection.description: Name or ID of the SCP connection which stores the details for SCP server.

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

client_configuration_id.description:
Client configuration identifier.

**Note:**
Use either client_configuration_id to link this profile to an existing configuration,
or provide inline configuration fields such as configurations, nae_iface_port, policy_id, enable_client_autorenewal, or jwt_verification_key.
Do not specify both at the same time.

configurations.description:
Parameters required to initialize connector.
- symmetric_key_cache_enabled: Whether the symmetric key cache is enabled.
  Options.
  - true (Default)
  - false
- symmetric_key_cache_expiry: Time after which the symmetric key cache will expire. Default: 43200
- size_of_connection_pool: The maximum number of connections that can persist in connection pool. Default: 300
- load_balancing_algorithm: Determines how the client selects a Key Manager from a load balancing group.
  Options.
  - round-robin (Default)
  - random
- connection_idle_timeout: The time a connection is allowed to be idle in the connection pool before it gets automatically closed. Default: 600000
- connection_retry_interval: The amount of time to wait before trying to reconnect to a disabled server. Default: 600000
- log_level: The level of logging to determine verbosity of clients logs.
  Options.
  - ERROR
  - WARN (Default)
  - INFO
  - DEBUG
- log_rotation: Specifies how frequently the log file is rotated.
  Options.
  - None
  - Daily (Default)
  - Weekly
  - Monthly
  - Size
- log_size_limit: The maximum size of  log file. Default: 100K
- log_gmt: This value specifies if timestamp in logs should be formatted in GMT or not. Default disabled
- log_type: Type of the log.
  Options.
  - Console (Default)
  - File
  - Multi
- log_file_path: This value specifies the path where log file will be created
- connection_timeout: Connection timeout value for clients. Default: 60000
- connection_read_timeout: Read timeout value for clients. Default: 7000
- heartbeat_interval: Frequency interval for sending heartbeat by connectors. Default: 300
- heartbeat_timeout_count: heartbeat timeout missed communication counts with CM for connectors to decide on cleanup profile cache. Default: -1
- tls_to_appserver
- dial_timeout: Specifies the maximum duration (in seconds) the DPG server will wait for a connection with the Application Server to succeed.
- dial_keep_alive: Specifies the interval (in seconds) between keep-alive probes for an active network connection.
- auth_method_used the parameter is used to define how and from where to validate the application user
  - scheme_name: the type of authentication scheme to be used to fetch the suer
    Options.
    - Basic (Default)
    - Bearer
  - token_field: the json field which have the user information. Required when scheme_name is Bearer.
- jwt_details: Information about the the JWT validation.  **Note:** Use either `jwt_details` or `jwt_verification_configurations`. These fields are mutually exclusive. `jwt_verification_configurations` enables multiple JWT verification sources.
  - issuer: A string that identifies the principal that issued the JWT. If left empty, the iss (issuer) field in the JWT will not be validated.
  - jwks_url: A string that provides the JWKs URL from which JSON Web Keys (JWKs) are retrieved to validate the JWT.
  - jwks_refresh_duration: The duration (in days) after which the JWKs will be refreshed. The value must be specified as integer.
  - jwt_username_field: Specifies the location of the username in the JWT. Access policy will be applied based on the username present in this location. The value must be a string.
  - enable_dpop: A boolean flag to enable DPoP verification. To enable DPoP verification JWT verification must be turned on either using public key or JWKS URL.

- jwt_verification_configurations: Array of JWT verification configurations to support multiple JWT verification sources.
  Each configuration defines how the JWT should be validated.
  - jwt_verification_method (string, required): Specifies how the JWT should be verified. Valid values: `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - issuer (string): Identifies the entity that issued the JWT. If not provided, the iss (issuer) claim in the JWT will be ignored during validation.
  - jwks_url (string, conditional): JWKs endpoint URL used for token verification. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwks_refresh_duration (integer, conditional): Number of days after which the JWKs will be refreshed. **Applicable only if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwt_username_field (string, optional): Specifies the claim in the JWT that contains the username. Access policy is applied based on the username value in this field.
  - enable_dpop (boolean, optional): Enables DPoP verification. DPoP verification requires JWT verification via either `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - jwt_verification_key (string, conditional): Public key used to validate JWT signatures. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwt_verification_key`.

- enable_performance_metrics:  Flag used to enable performance metrics.
  Options.
  - true (Default)
  - false

- kms_cluster_configuration: Optional. Enables clients to connect to KMS in cluster mode.
  A maximum of 3 tiers are supported. Each tier accepts a list of IP strings. All tiers are optional.
  - tier1 (array of strings): Primary KMS node IPs.
  - tier2 (array of strings): Secondary KMS node IPs. Requires tier1 to be set.
  - tier3 (array of strings): Tertiary KMS node IPs. Requires tier2 to be set.

  - jwks_refresh_duration: The duration (in days) after which the JWKs will be refreshed. The value must be specified as integer.
  - jwt_username_field: Specifies the location of the username in the JWT. Access policy will be applied based on the username present in this location. The value must be a string.
  - enable_dpop: A boolean flag to enable DPoP verification. To enable DPoP verification JWT verification must be turned on either using public key or JWKS URL.

- jwt_verification_configurations: Array of JWT verification configurations to support multiple JWT verification sources.
  Each configuration defines how the JWT should be validated.
  - jwt_verification_method (string, required): Specifies how the JWT should be verified. Valid values: `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - issuer (string): Identifies the entity that issued the JWT. If not provided, the iss (issuer) claim in the JWT will be ignored during validation.
  - jwks_url (string, conditional): JWKs endpoint URL used for token verification. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwks_refresh_duration (integer, conditional): Number of days after which the JWKs will be refreshed. **Applicable only if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwt_username_field (string, optional): Specifies the claim in the JWT that contains the username. Access policy is applied based on the username value in this field.
  - enable_dpop (boolean, optional): Enables DPoP verification. DPoP verification requires JWT verification via either `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - jwt_verification_key (string, conditional): Public key used to validate JWT signatures. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwt_verification_key`.

- enable_performance_metrics:  Flag used to enable performance metrics.
  Options.
  - true (default) 
  - false

- kms_cluster_configuration: Optional. Enables clients to connect to KMS in cluster mode.
  A maximum of 3 tiers are supported. Each tier accepts a list of IP strings. All tiers are optional.
  - tier1 (array of strings): Primary KMS node IPs.
  - tier2 (array of strings): Secondary KMS node IPs. Requires tier1 to be set.
  - tier3 (array of strings): Tertiary KMS node IPs. Requires tier2 to be set.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

allOf.description:
The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

skip.description:
The index of the first record returned.  Equivalent to 'offset' in

limit.description: The max number of records returned.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL.

total.description: The total records matching the query.

get.description:
Returns a list of all connections.
The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on fields associated with the connections and return the field attribute in the response.
Currently, only "meta" is supported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP , Luna connections , "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Filter the result based on the external services associated with the connections. (e.g. aws, azure, gcp, hadoop-knox, luna network).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter the result based on category.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed.

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

aws_sts_regional_endpoints.description:
By default, AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) is available as a global service, and all AWS STS requests
go to a single endpoint at https://sts.amazonaws.com. Global requests map to the US East (N. Virginia) Region.
AWS recommends using Regional AWS STS endpoints instead of the global endpoint to reduce latency,
build in redundancy, and increase session token validity.
valid values are:
- legacy (default): Uses the global AWS STS endpoint, sts.amazonaws.com
- regional: The SDK or tool always uses the AWS STS endpoint for the currently configured Region.

To know more about AWS STS please go through the following link
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_enable-regions.html

aws_region.description:
AWS region. only used when aws_sts_regional_endpoints is equal to regional otherwise, it takes default values
according to Cloud Name given. Default values are:
- for aws, default region will be "us-east-1"
- for aws-us-gov, default region will be "us-gov-east-1"
- for aws-cn, default region will be "cn-north-1"

Labels are key/value pairs used to group resources. They are based on Kubernetes Labels, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/.

To add a label, set the label's value as follows.
```
    "labels": {
      "key1": "value1",
      "key2": "value2"
    }
```
To remove a key/value pair, pass value null to the particular key
```
    "labels": {
      "key1": null
    }
```

get.description:
Returns a list of Azure connections.
The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on fields associated with the connections and return the field attribute in the response.
Currently, only "meta" is supported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP , Luna connections , "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: cloud_name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on cloud name.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: external_certificate_used
parameters.description: Filter the result based on if external certificate is used for connection.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed.

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

allOf.description:
The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

skip.description:
The index of the first record returned.  Equivalent to 'offset' in

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter

format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed.

For example, to select resources that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not
have `{"team": "sales"}` use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

To select resources whose labels contain the key called region, use `region`.

To select resources whose labels do not contain the key called region, use `!region`.

To select resources in the sales and engineering teams, use `team in (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, or do not have a key called `team`, use `team notin (sales,engineering)`.

To select resources that are not in the sales and engineering teams, and have a key called `team`, use `team,team notin (sales,engineering)`.

password.description:
Password for the Salesforce account. This a mandatory parameter for a connection
with Client Credential Authentication method. This parameter is not needed for
Certificate Authentication or when using domain name.
“Allow OAuth Username-Password Flows” must be enabled under
Setup -> Settings -> Identity -> OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings
in your salesforce account to use password for authentication.

client_secret.description:
Consumer Secret for the Salesforce application. This a mandatory parameter for a connection
with Client Credential Authentication method. This parameter is not needed for
Certificate Authentication.

tls_client_private_key_password.description:
Password/passphrase for TLS Client Private key. Provide value if private key is encrypted with
password/passphrase.

client_id.description: Unique Identifier (client ID/consumer key) for the Salesforce Application.

username.description: Username of the Salesforce account. Not required when using domain name.

domain_name.description:
The domain_name represents My Domain that could be found in your salesforce account. This My Domain acts
as a subdomain in framing URL https://MyDomain.my.salesforce.com which is eventually used to establish a
connection to salesforce account. The client_credentials grant uses this URL to make a request when
usernmame and password are not provided.
You can refer to Salesforce documentation in order to learn more about My Domain.
This parameter cannot be used if hostname is specified.

hostname.description:
The hostname of the salesforce instance to connect to. Example: test-site-aesf24.sf-onp-dc-test-02.ml.
When hostname is specified, domain name parameter cannot be used.

audience.description:
The audience identifies the authorization server as an intended audience.
Use the authorization server’s URL for the audience value for salesforce.com cloud:
https://login.salesforce.com, https://test.salesforce.com
This variable is supported with certificate authentication only.

allOf.description: Sensitive parameters specific to a Salesforce connection.

enable_mutual_tls.description:
Setting it to true will enforce SSL or TLS mutual authentication for Salesforce API calls.
Default is false.

tls_client_certificate_with_private_key.description:
TLS client certificate along with private key to be used as client side certificate
to support Salesforce Mutual Authentication Certificate option. Provide certificate chain as a single
PEM-encoded CA-signed certificate representing the concatenated chain of certificates.
The uploaded certificate chain must include the intermediate certificates and private key.
Certificate order should be client certificate and then add its signing certificate, intermediate certificates
if any followed by private key of Client certificate. If Private key is encrypted then specify
password/passphrase used to encrypt Private key in tls_client_private_key_password param.

tls_client_private_key_password.description:
Password/passphrase for TLS Client Private key. Provide value if private key is encrypted with
password/passphrase.

is_certificate_used.description:
User has the option to choose the Certificate Authentication method instead of Client Credentials (password and client_secret)
Authentication for Salesforce Cloud connection. In order to use the Certificate, set this field to true.
Once the connection is created, in the response user will get a certificate.

cert_duration.description: Duration in days for which the salesforce server certificate is valid, default (730 i.e. 2 Years).

certificate.description: User has the option to upload external certificate for Salesforce Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option is_certificate_used and client_secret. User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 1024, 2048 or 4096. User can also update the new external certificate in the existing connection in Update (PATCH) API call. Any unused certificate will automatically deleted in 24 hours.

parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after

get.description:
Returns a list of OCI connections.
The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP , Luna connections , "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

post.description:
Creates a new Akeyless connection.
Each Akeyless connection has an access ID, access key  and an optional parameter akeyless url.
These credentials can be used to connect to the Akeyless server in the cloud
via the Akeyless gateway that runs on the CM.
The access key is a secret and is protected by the CM.
For Single Tenant infrastructures, akeyless_url parameter is the URL used by the gateway to connect to the Akeyless server.

get.description:
Returns a list of Akeyless connections.
The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on fields associated with the connections and return the field attribute in the response.
Currently, only "meta" is supported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP , Luna connections , "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

SHA256WithRSA, SHA1WithRSA, ECDSAWithSHA512, ECDSAWithSHA384, ECDSAWithSHA256) is selected
based on the algorithm and size.

names.description:
Name fields are "O=organization, OU=organizational unit, L=location, ST=state/province, C=country".
Fields can be duplicated if present in different objects.

Example: [{"O": "Thales Group", "OU": "CPS", "C": "US", "ST": "MD", "L": "Belcamp"}, {"OU": "Thales Group Inc."}]

encryptionAlgo.description: Private key encryption algorithm. AES256 (default), AES192, AES128, TDES

privateKeyBytes.description: Private Key bytes of the key which is to be used while creating CSR(Algorithm and size should be according to this key). If not given will generate key internally as per algorithm and size.

key_mgmt_mode.description:
The mode is only valid for product CCKM. For handling private keys, individual partition can be configured by using one of the supported modes. 
It is required that all the partitions should be in the same mode.The key_mgmt_mode parameter is applicable only when is_ha_enabled is set to true.
If no value or empty string ("") is provided, then a connection will be created without any key_mgmt_mode.
For creating partition and handling keys in a specific mode in HSM, please refer HSM Docs as the valid values correspond to key export and clone mode mentioned in HSM Docs.
Valid values are:
- keyExport:
  - CCKM supports the replication of private asymmetric keys within the partition's HA group
- clone:
  - all keys/objects in CCKM are replicated automatically within the partition's HA group

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: skip

parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP, Luna connections, "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:

format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:

format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after

format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

insecure_skip_verify.description:
Optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

root_cas.description:
Optional list of CA certificates that are used to determine if the LDAP server certificate is trusted. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

If not provided, the server's certificate is verified using the operating system's default CAs.

Accepts [PEM encoded certificates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail). Here's an example showing an abbreviated (see `[...]`) list of root CAs.
```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```

bind_dn.description: Object which has permission to search under the root DN for users.

base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for users.

search_filter.description: LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in.

user_login_attribute.description: Attribute inside the user object which contains the username used to login with.

group_base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_filter.description: Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_name_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.

user_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. Example: uid, dn

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

group_id_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value should be unique and can be left empty to disable group support for this connection. If group_id_attribute is not provided, it will default to  'group_name_attribute'.

group_member_field.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid
This value can be left empty to disable group membership support for this connection.

user_member_field.description:
Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber.
In case, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen.

group_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains the group's distinguished name.
When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber

For example:
- if a groups's LDAP entry has "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`" and the LDAP configuration has "`group_dn_attribute`" set to "`dn`", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`", in order for the user to be considered part of group.

server_maximum_page_size.description:
This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
By default 'server_maximum_page_size' is set to 1000, and therefore entries are retrieved from LDAP server through pagination. We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size.
To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0. Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

early_listing_stop.description:
This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched. When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user. To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1. When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.

parameters.name: sort

The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

insecure_skip_verify.description:
Optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

Default value is `false`.

root_cas.description:

```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```
