bind_dn.description: Object which has permission to search under the root DN for users.

base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for users.

search_filter.description: LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in.

user_login_attribute.description: Attribute inside the user object which contains the username used to login with.

group_base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_filter.description: Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_name_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.

user_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. Example: uid, dn

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

group_id_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value should be unique and can be left empty to disable group support for this connection. If group_id_attribute is not provided, it will default to  'group_name_attribute'.

group_member_field.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid
This value can be left empty to disable group membership support for this connection.

user_member_field.description:
Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber.
In case, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen.

group_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains the group's distinguished name.
When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber

For example:
- if a groups's LDAP entry has "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`" and the LDAP configuration has "`group_dn_attribute`" set to "`dn`", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`", in order for the user to be considered part of group.

server_maximum_page_size.description:
This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
By default 'server_maximum_page_size' is set to 1000, and therefore entries are retrieved from LDAP server through pagination. We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size.
To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0. Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

early_listing_stop.description:
This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched. When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user. To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1. When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.

user_login_attribute.description: Attribute inside the user object which contains the username used to login with.

group_base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_filter.description: Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_name_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.

user_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. Example: uid, dn

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

group_id_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value should be unique and can be left empty to disable group support for this connection. If group_id_attribute is not provided, it will default to  'group_name_attribute'.

group_member_field.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid
This value can be left empty to disable group membership support for this connection.

user_member_field.description:
Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber.
In case, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen.

group_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains the group's distinguished name.
When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber

For example:
- if a groups's LDAP entry has "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`" and the LDAP configuration has "`group_dn_attribute`" set to "`dn`", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`", in order for the user to be considered part of group.

server_maximum_page_size.description:
This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
By default 'server_maximum_page_size' is set to 1000, and therefore entries are retrieved from LDAP server through pagination. We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size.
To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0. Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

early_listing_stop.description:
This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched. When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user. To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1. When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.

```

]
```

get.description:
Returns a list of Hadoop connections.
The results can be filtered using the query parameters.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The index of the first resource to return.  Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The max number of resources to return.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. The returned resources may be truncated to less than the requested limit in some cases (endpoint dependent).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The fields to sort results by.  This should be a comma-delimited list of properties.
Multiple properties will result in a multi-column sort.  Sort order is ascending by default.
To have a descending sort for a field, precede the field name with a minus sign ("-").
For example:

     name,-createdAt

...will sort the results first by `name`, ascending, then by `createdAt`, descending.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Filter the result based on the external services associated with the connections. (e.g. aws, azure, gcp, hadoop-knox, luna network).

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on fields associated with the connections and return the field attribute in the response.
Currently, only "meta" is supported.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection's ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter the result based on connection name.

parameters.name: products
parameters.description:
Filter the result based on the CipherTrust Manager products associated with the connections.
   Valid values are "cckm" for AWS, Azure, GCP, Luna connections, "cte", "ddc", "data discovery" for Hadoop connections
    and "cte" for SMB connections

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_ok
parameters.description: Filter the result based on last_connection_ok result.

parameters.name: last_connection_before
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or before the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

parameters.name: last_connection_after
parameters.description:
Filters results to those created at or after the specified timestamp. Timestamp should be in RFC3339Nano
format, e.g. 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z, or a relative timestamp where valid units are 'Y', 'M', 'D' representing
years, months, and days respectively. Negative values are permitted. e.g. "-1Y-2M-5D".

DeleteCSIStorageGroupCTE (for deleting CTE CSI storage group)
UpdateCSIStorageGroupCTE (for updating CTE CSI storage group)
DeleteGoogleWorkspaceCSEEndpoint (for deleting Google Worspace CSE endpoint)

schema.description:
Policies are access control rules.  They declare a set of
actions, applied to a set of resources, under an optional set of
conditions, which are either allowed or not allowed.

Policies, like other resources, share common properties like `id`,
`uri`, `name`, etc.

`actions` is a list of permissions.

TBD: link to
canonical dictionary of permissions.  Operations will require some
set of the these permissions

`resources` is a list of URI patterns.

id.description: The unique identifier of the resource

uri.description: A human readable unique identifier of the resource

account.description: The account which owns this resource.

application.description: The application this resource belongs to.

devAccount.description: The developer account which owns this resource's application.

effect.description:
The effect describes the effect of the policy. There are 4 possible values.
With effect, the allow flag gets deprecated. Please use one of the two and
use allow only if it is needed, instead use effect.

path.format: A JSON path, with template variables.
path.description: A JSON path which resolves to a value in the operation

op.description:
The comparison operator used to compare the operation value
to the conditions values.

values.description:
The value or values to compare with the operation value.
Can be either a single value, or an array.  If an
array, each of the items in the array is compared to
the operation value, and if any match, the condition is
met.  In other words, the items are logically OR'd.

includeDescendantAccounts.description:
When this is false, only the resources in the principal's account can be accessed if the policy allows it.
When this is true, the resources the principal's account as well as all child accounts associated with the
principal's account, can be accessed if the policy allows it.
For example, sub-domains will be included while listing domains when this parameter is true.

post.description: Create a password policy. Can only be used by a member of the admin or user admin group. Currently, be default 'global' policy is applied to all users. To apply the policy, you need to assign it to a user.

inclusive_min_upper_case.description: The minimum number of upper cases

inclusive_min_lower_case.description: The minimum number of lower cases

inclusive_min_other.description: The minimum number of other characters

inclusive_min_total_length.description: The minimum length of the password. Value 0 is ignored.

inclusive_max_total_length.description: Specifies the maximum length of the password. Setting the value to 0 indicates that the property isn't enforced, therefore the password can be of any length.

password_history_threshold.description: Determines the number of past passwords a user cannot reuse. Even with value 0, the user will not be able to change their password to the same password.

password_lifetime.description: The maximum lifetime of the password in days. Value 0 is ignored.

password_change_min_days.description: The minimum period in days between password changes. Value 0 is ignored.

failed_logins_lockout_thresholds.description:
List of lockout durations in minutes for failed login attempts.
For example, with input of [0, 5, 30], the first failed login attempt with duration of zero will not lockout the user account,
the second failed login attempt will lockout the account for 5 minutes,
the third and subsequent failed login attempts will lockout for 30 minutes.
Set an empty array '[]' to disable the user account lockout.

password_expiry_notification_days.description:
Determines number of days before password expiry when notification(s) would be sent to user.  

Login banner would be shown to user on UI if password expiry duration is less than 
`password_expiry_notification_days`.  

If SMTP server is configured, email notification would be sent daily to users notifying need to 
change their password soon.  

Value should be less than password_lifetime.  
Valid values are between 0 and 30. Value of 0 would disable notification. Default value is 14.    

Example:  
If password_lifetime is set to 20 and password_expiry_notification_days is set to 10, 
then user will observe banner on UI about password expiry and receive an email (if configured) 
daily from 10 days before their password expires.

parameters.description: Filters results to those with matching IDs. May be specified more than once. Results will match *any* of the values.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
Filters results that match label selector expressions. Multiple
values are logically ANDed. For example, to select templates that have
the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not have `{"team": "sales"}`
use `region=noram,team!=sales`.

parameters.name: meta_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only templates whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:
- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`
- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`
- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`
- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

parameters.name: key_attributes_contains
parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only templates whose 'key_attributes' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"Algorithm":"RSA"}` contains `{"Algorithm":"RSA"}`
- Values contain subsets: `{"Algorithm":"RSA", "size":2048}` contains `{"Algorithm":"RSA"}` and `{"size":1024}`, but not `{"size":2048}`
- Contained values can be nested: `{"meta":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"meta":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

usageMask.description:
Filters results based on matching Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage mask values to allow the usages. 
The associated values are - Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4), Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512), 
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384), Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), 
Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144), Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). To set all usage mask bits, 
use 4194303 (all usage masks including Export). Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728), 'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 
'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

curveid.description: The Cryptographic curve id of a template is used for the elliptic key. This is a mandatory parameter for 'EC' algorithm.

parameterSet.description: Specifies the ML-DSA parameter set. Valid values are 'ml-dsa-44', 'ml-dsa-65', and 'ml-dsa-87'. Defaults to 'ml-dsa-65' if not specified.

size.description: The Bit length of the key using this template.The Size is mandatory for all supported algorithms except for algorithms 'ec' and 'ml-dsa'.

unexportable.description: The key created using this template will not be exportable. The default value is false.

undeletable.description: The key created using this template will not be deleted. The default value is false.

-pkcs1

-pkcs12
For ML-DSA keys, only 'pkcs8' format is supported. PKCS#1 and PKCS#12 are not supported for ML-DSA keys.

For Symmetric Keys the valid options are
-raw
-opaque

  For Deactived State deactivationDate is required. Deactivation Date must not be before Activation Date or ProtectStopDate.

 - HMAC

     name,-createdAt

parameters.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only resources whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Values contain subsets: `{"color":"red", "size":"big"}` contains `{"color":"red"}` and `{"size":"big"}`, but not `{"size":"small"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`

- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

post.description:
Create a DKE endpoint for the Microsoft Double Key Encryption service.
You can create a new KEK or specify an existing KEK for getkey and decrypt operations. 
Existing KEK is applicable for migrating DKE integration from another CipherTrust Manager deployment. Specify the following required details:
- Unique name for the endpoint.
- Base hostname for the Key URI.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Endpoint parameters

source_key_tier.description: Source key tier. Options are local and external-cm. Default is local.

key_type.description: DKE key type. Only the key type of asymmetric is currently supported.

algorithm.description: DKE key algorithm. Only the RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256 algorithm is currently supported, which is the default value.

key_uri_hostname.description:
Base URL hostname for KeyURI.

If you have changed the CipherTrust Manager web interface port from its default of 443 to a different port, you must include that new port number when specifying the URL hostname, e.g. example.com:8443.

meta.description: Additional information associated with this endpoint.

enabled.description: Flag to denote whether endpoint is enabled. Default value is true.

enable_success_audit_event.description: Flag to denote whether audit recording of successful operations for the DKE endpoint is enabled or disabled. Default value is true.

existing_key_id.description:
If source_key_tier is local, Identifier is to be used to find the latest version of an existing CipherTrust Manager key. This identifier can be the
ID of any version or the name of a CipherTrust Manager key.  If the identifier is not supplied, a new CipherTrust Manager key will be created. 
This identifier is applicable to the migration of a DKE endpoint from one CipherTrust Manager deployment to another. When creating a new DKE 
endpoint using an existing CipherTrust Manager key in the new deployment, CCKM uses this identifier to associate all of the existing versions 
of a CipherTrust Manager key to the new endpoint.

If source_key_tier is external-cm, Identifier should be of the external CipherTrust Manager(required).

Source key must be an asymmetric key type, having Sign and Verify usage masks. In addition, this key must not be exportable or deletable. 
A DKE endpoint will be created using the latest version of this key.

User.description:
A User represents a unique, actual person or system.

Users and their credentials currently reside in an internal user database.
Support will be added in the future for users residing in external
authentication services as well.

Users must be created explicitly through the API.

user_id.description: A unique identifier for API call usage.

username.description:
The login name of the user. This is the identifier used to login.

This attribute is required to create a user, but is omitted
when getting or listing user resources. It cannot be updated.

password.description:
The password used to secure the users account.  There are currently
no restrictions around the type or length of password that is required.
This attribute is required to create a user, but is not included
in user resource responses.

connection.description:
This attribute is required to create a user, but is not included
in user resource responses. Can be the name of a connection or
"local_account" for a local user, defaults to "local_account".

**Deprecated**: Use `allowed_auth_methods` instead.

If set to true, the user will be able to login using certificate.

ConnectionLDAPOptions.description: Options for connecting to an LDAP server.

server_url.description: LDAP only, LDAP URL for your server. (e.g. ldap://172.16.2.2:3268)

root_dn.description: LDAP only, Starting point to use when searching for users

uid_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the user object which contains the user id

bind_dn.description: LDAP only, Object which has permission to search under the root DN for users. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

bind_password.description: LDAP only, Password for the Bind DN object. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

user_dn_field.description:
LDAP only, Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. If user_dn_field is not provided, an attempt is made to determine default value based on uid_field. If uid_field is provided as sAMAccountName, Active Directory configuration is assumed and 'distingushedName' is used as default for user_dn_field. Otherwise, it will default to  'dn'.

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

search_filter.description: LDAP only, LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in

guid_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains the globally unique identifier of the group. On bind, if guid_field is not provided, it will default to whatever is in uid_field. However, on uid_field update, guid_field will not update automatically.

group_base_dn.description: LDAP only, Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection

group_filter.description: LDAP only, Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_id_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_member_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

root_cas.description:
LDAP only, optional list of certificates that are used to determine if the server is trusted. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

If not provided, then the server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.

Accepts [PEM encoded certificates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail). Here's an example showing an abbreviated (see `[...]`) list of root CAs.
```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```

insecure_skip_verify.description:
LDAP only, optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

Default value is `false`.

ConnectionOIDCOptions.description: Options for connecting to an external OpenID Connect server

flow_type.description:
OpenID Connect only, optional, default value is "implicit".  
Can be an one of "implicit" or "authorization_code".

client_secret.description: secret data stored securely in CipherTrust Manager

authorization_uri.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the authorization endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

client_id.description: OpenID Connect only, required, the public identifier of CipherTrust Manager on the the external identity provider (authorization server). This value is typically generated by and retrieved from the external identity provider.

redirect_uri.description:
(Deprecated) Use redirect URIs instead.

OpenID Connect only, required, URI to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

This URI MUST exactly match one of the Redirection URI values for the Client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

redirect_uris.description:
OpenID Connect only, required, set of allowed URIs to redirect to after finished authentication to the external identity provider (authorization server).

These URIs should match the Redirection URIs values for the client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider. The Redirection URI MUST NOT use the `http` scheme.

Typically https://ciphertrust-manager-host/api/v1/auth/oidc-callback where 'ciphertrust-manager-host' should be updated to the hostname of your server.

discovery_uri.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the well-known configuration endpoint of the external identity provider. External ID Provider settings such as authorization URI and public signing keys will be auto-downloaded from this URI.

scope.description:
The scope value should be less than 255 in length and must only contain printable ASCII characters except for spaces, double quotes, and backslashes.
If the scope does not include "openid," the backend will add it to the scope values passed to the OpenID provider.

userinfo_endpoint.description: OIDC server's userinfo_endpoint. It will be used to retrieve group information from OIDC server.

jwks.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, array of JWKS containing the public keys for ID Token validation. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

groups_claim.description: The claim field name to extract group membership from in the OIDC ID Token. Works in conjunction with Group Maps. If unspecified it default to 'groups'.

username_claim.description:
The claim field name to extract username from in the OIDC ID Token. If unspecified it defaults to 'sub'.
The claim field can also be a template to support the nested claims if any in OIDC ID Token.
For instance, for OIDC ID token: 
```
{
 "sub": "111730983950574648607", 
 "email": "test@xyz.com",
 "custom": {       
   "username": "xyz"     
 }
}
```
"email" as string or "{{.custom.username}}" as template can be set as 'username_claim' to set the username of the user on CM after successful authentication on the external identity provider.
It is important that the 'username claim' provided is unique in the external identity provider and it is not modifiable.

token_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the token endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

end_session_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the end session endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

If uid_field is provided as sAMAccountName, Active Directory configuration is assumed and 'distingushedName' is used as default for user_dn_field. Otherwise, it will default to  'dn'.

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_field`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

search_filter.description: LDAP only, LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in

guid_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains the globally unique identifier of the group. On bind, if guid_field is not provided, it will default to whatever is in uid_field. However, on uid_field update, guid_field will not update automatically.

group_base_dn.description: LDAP only, Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection

group_filter.description: LDAP only, Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_id_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_member_field.description: LDAP only, Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

root_cas.description:
LDAP only, optional list of certificates that are used to determine if the server is trusted. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

If not provided, then the server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.

Accepts [PEM encoded certificates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail). Here's an example showing an abbreviated (see `[...]`) list of root CAs.
```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```

insecure_skip_verify.description:
LDAP only, optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

Default value is `false`.

flow_type.description:

client_secret.description: secret data stored securely in CipherTrust Manager

client_id.description: OpenID Connect only, required, the public identifier of CipherTrust Manager on the the external identity provider (authorization server). This value is typically generated by and retrieved from the external identity provider.

username_claim.description:
The claim field name to extract username from in the OIDC ID Token. If unspecified it defaults to 'sub'.
The claim field can also be a template to support the nested claims if any in OIDC ID Token.
For instance, for OIDC ID token: 
```
{
 "sub": "111730983950574648607", 
 "email": "test@xyz.com",
 "custom": {       
   "username": "xyz"     
 }
}
```
"email" as string or "{{.custom.username}}" as template can be set as 'username_claim' to set the username of the user on CM after successful authentication on the external identity provider.
It is important that the 'username claim' provided is unique in the external identity provider and it is not modifiable.

end_session_endpoint.description: OpenID Connect only, optional, URI to the end session endpoint of the external identity provider. Intended for test and not recommended for use in production, see discovery URI.

Configuration.description: Configuration is the set of editable options for how an interface operates.

mode.description: The interface mode can be one of the following: no-tls-pw-opt, no-tls-pw-req, unauth-tls-pw-opt, tls-cert-opt-pw-opt, tls-pw-opt, tls-pw-req, tls-cert-pw-opt, or tls-cert-and-pw. Default mode is no-tls-pw-opt. Refer to the top level discussion of the Interface section for further details.

cert_user_field.description: Specifies how the user name is extracted from the client certificate. Allowed values are: CN, SN, E, E_ND, UID and OU. Refer to the top level discussion of the Interfaces section for more details.

auto_gen_ca_id.description: Auto-generate a new server certificate on server startup using the identifier (URI) of a Local CA resource if the current server certificate is issued by a different Local CA. This is especially useful when a new node joins the cluster. In this case, the existing data of the joining node is overwritten by the data in the cluster. A new server certificate is generated on the joining node using the existing Local CA of the cluster. Auto-generation of the server certificate can be disabled by setting `auto_gen_ca_id` to an empty string ("") to allow full control over the server certificate.

trusted_cas.title: Trusted CAs

local.description: A list of Local CA IDs

external.description: A list of External CA IDs

default_connection.description: The default connection may be "local_account" for local authentication or the LDAP domain for LDAP authentication. This value is applied when the username does not embed the connection name (e.g. "jdoe" effectively becomes "local_account|jdoe"). This value only applies to NAE only and is ignored if set for web and KMIP interfaces.

port.description:
The interface will listen on the specified port.
The port number should not be negative, 0 or the one already in-use.

kmip_enable_hard_delete.description: Enables hard delete of keys on KMIP Destroy operation, that is both meta-data and material will be removed from CipherTrust Manager for the key being deleted. By default, only key material is removed and meta-data is preserved with the updated key state. This setting applies only to KMIP interface. Should be set to 1 for enabling the feature or 0 for returning to default behavior.

auto_registration.description: Set auto registration to allow auto registration of kmip and nae clients.

registration_token.description: Registration token in case auto registration is true.

minimum_tls_version.description:
Minimum TLS version to be configured for NAE or KMIP or Web interface, default is v1.2 (tls_1_2).
Web interface tls version cannot go below v1.2.

Currently supported:
  - `tls_1_0`
  - `tls_1_1`
  - `tls_1_2`
  - `tls_1_3`

maximum_tls_version.description:
Maximum TLS version to be configured for NAE or KMIP or Web interface, default is latest maximum supported protocol.
Web interface tls version cannot go below v1.2.

Currently supported:
  - `tls_1_0`
  - `tls_1_1`
  - `tls_1_2`
  - `tls_1_3`

custom_uid_size.description: This flag is used to define the custom uid size of managed object over the KMIP interface.

custom_uid_v2.description: This flag specifies which version of custom uid feature is to be used for KMIP interface. If it is set to true, new implementation i.e. Custom uid version 2 will be used.

local_auto_gen_attributes.description: Local CSR parameters for interface's certificate. These are for the local node itself, and they do not affect other nodes in the cluster. This gives user a convenient way to supply custom fields for automatic interface certification generation. Without them, the system defaults are used.

names.description:
Name fields are "O=organization, OU=organizational unit, L=location, ST=state/province, C=country".
Example: [{"O": "Thales Group", "OU": "CPL", "C": "US", "ST": "MD", "L": "Belcamp"}, {"OU": "Thales Group Inc."}]

tls_groups.description:
TLS Groups contain the list of key exchange algorithms available in the system for the WEB, NAE and KMIP interfaces for TLS handshake.
Classic key exchange algorithms default behaviour:
* Web interface: 'x25519', 'secp256r1', 'x448', 'secp521r1', 'secp384r1', 'ffdhe2048', 'ffdhe3072', 'ffdhe4096', 'ffdhe6144' and 'ffdhe8192' are enabled.
* NAE and KMIP interfaces: 'x25519', 'secp256r1', 'secp521r1' and 'secp384r1' are enabled.

Post Quantum key exchange algorithms default behaviour:
* Web interface: 'X25519MLKEM768', 'SecP256r1MLKEM768', 'MLKEM768', 'MLKEM1024' and 'MLKEM512' are disabled.
* NAE and KMIP interfaces: 'X25519MLKEM768' is disabled.

The entire list of TLS groups is required to enable or disable any specific TLS group.

Behavior of order of TLS Groups:
  * For TLS1.3, despite the server's configured preference order of the groups, currently server will automatically accept the very first key_share that client includes 
    in its ClientHello message, that is also supported by the server.
  * For TLS v1.2, client cannot share its key_share upfront in ClientHello message, thus server will request the client 
    to converge on the most preferred server's group which is also supported by the client. This behavior is aligned with OpenSSL.

However, defining the order still matters. Even if server picks the less preferred (but supported) group, it sends a supported_groups back to the client in its 
ServerHello, so that the client can remember and adjust to send the key_share as per the server's priority for the subsequent requests.

tag.description: The AEAD tag is a byte array, and appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob.

iv.description: The IV is a byte array, and appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob.

aad.description: Data to authenticate. This is a byte array and should be a valid base64 string.

label.description: A Base64-encoded string containing arbitrary data that will not be encrypted, but gives important context to the message. Used only with asymmetric RSA decryption and supported paddings are OAEP, OAEP256, OAEP384 and OAEP512. The value must be equal to the value used when encrypting.

DecryptedBlob.description: The output of an decrypt operation. It is a JSON object that contains the plaintext.
DecryptedBlob.title: Decrypted Blob

plaintext.description: The plain text is a byte array, and appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob.

batch_response.description:
Contains decrypted data.
Returned only when `"batch_request"` is provided in request (i.e if data is sent in batch mode).

If error occurs while processing any data in a batch, Response HTTP status code will be 207 and error will be
returned only for the data that failed, with `"batch_response"` containing `"error"` for that
index; rest all indexes will be successfully decrypted.

plaintext.description: The plain text is a byte array, and appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob.

error.description:
Returned only for the index that failed.
Either `"error"` or `"plaintext"` will be returned.

ReencryptInput.description:
The input for a re-encrypt operation. It is a JSON object that contains encryption and decryption parameters.
The decryption parameters contain the encrypted data and the parameters required to decrypt the data.
For Encryption parameters, in case of AES-GCM, it contains the data to be authenticated. Note that this is byte array. JSON encodes byte arrays to base64 strings. Therefore, the JSON object should contain valid base64 data for AAD.
Note: The Plaintext parameter is not required.
ReencryptInput.title: ReencryptInput

encrypt.description: The input of Encrypt operation, In case of AES-GCM, it contains the data to be authenticated. Note that this is byte array. JSON encodes byte arrays to base64 strings.

id.description: The name, ID, or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.

name.description: The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.

type.description: Type of the identifier specified in the 'name' parameter. The Type of the identifier is derived from name, ID, URI, or alias. If not specified, the type of the identifier is automatically inferred.

version.description:
Version of the key to use. Supported Versions are
Actual version of the key, Latest Version (-1), Latest Active Version (-2). If no version is specified, the key's latest version (-1) is used by default.

mode.description: Identifies the cryptographic mode to use for the symmetric key operations. The allowed values depend on the algorithm used. Allowed values for AES are 'CBC', 'EBC', 'CTR', and 'GCM' (default is 'GCM'). The only allowed value for TDES is 'CBC'.

pad.description: This string identifies the cryptographic padding algorithm to use. The allowed values depend on the algorithm used. For AES and TDES, the allowed values are 'none', 'PKCS5', and 'PKCS7' (default is 'PKCS7'). For asymmetric algorithms, the allowed values are 'PKCS1', 'OAEP', 'OAEP256', 'OAEP384', and 'OAEP512' (default is 'OAEP').

aad.description: Data to authenticate. This is a byte array and should be a valid base64 string.

iv.description: The Initialization Vector (IV) is a byte array used with CBC and GCM cryptographic algorithm modes. It appears as a base64 encoded string in the JSON blob. We recommend to omit this field to let the server generate and return a secure IV using its random number generator. Otherwise follow the security guidelines in "NIST SP800-38A" and "NIST SP800-38D" publications to ensure your IV construction is secure.

nae_key_version_header.description: This flag requests that the 3-byte NAE key-version header be prepended to the returned ciphertext.

tag_len.description: The byte length of the GCM tag. It can be between 4 and 16, defaults to 16.

usageMask.description:
Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage masks to allow certain usages. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303.
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

algorithm.description: Cryptographic algorithm this key is used with. Defaults to 'aes'

objectType.description:
This specifies the type of object that is being created. Valid values are
'Symmetric Key', 'Public Key', 'Private Key', 'Secret Data', 'Opaque Object',
or 'Certificate'. The object type is inferred for many objects,
but must be supplied for the certificate object.

curveid.description:
Cryptographic curve id for elliptic key. Key algorithm must be 'EC'. Values:
  * secp224k1
  * secp224r1
  * secp256k1
  * secp384r1
  * secp521r1
  * prime256v1
  * brainpoolP224r1
  * brainpoolP224t1
  * brainpoolP256r1
  * brainpoolP256t1
  * brainpoolP384r1
  * brainpoolP384t1
  * brainpoolP512r1
  * brainpoolP512t1

undeletable.description: Key is not deletable. Defaults to false.

labels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. When labels are provided
they are merged with the key's existing labels.

To add a label, set the label's value as follows.
```
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    }
```

unexportable.description: Key is not exportable.

undeletable.description: Key is not deletable.

rotationFrequencyDays.description:
Number of days from current date to rotate the key. It should be greater than or equal to 0. Default is an empty string.
If set to 0, rotationFrequencyDays set to an empty string and auto rotation of key will be disabled.

revocationReason.description:
Revocation Reason Code for revoking the object. Required in conjunction with compromiseOccurrenceDate.
It is one of 'Key Compromise', 'CA Compromise', 'Unspecified', 'Affiliation Changed',
'Superseded', 'Cessation of Operation' or 'Privilege Withdrawn'

revocationMessage.description: Revocation message. Optionally used in conjunction with revocationReason.

cryptographically protected information (e.g., decryption or unwrapping)

protectStopDate.description:
Date/time after which a Managed Symmetric Key Object SHALL NOT be used for
applying cryptographic protection (e.g., encryption or wrapping)

aliases.description:
Information needed for adding, modifying or deleting key aliases.
To delete a key, just specify its index. To add a key, do not specify the index.
To modify a key, specify its index, and the new values of the alias and type.

allVersions.description:
To update the group permissions/custom attribute or both in metadata of all versions of the key.
This parameter also updates the usageMask, undeletable, and unexportable properties of all versions of a key at once.
By default it is set to false.
Set to true, only when to update the group/custom attribute or both permissions of all versions of the key.
If this parameter is set to true, use the key name as the identifier.

labels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. When labels are provided
they are merged with the key's existing labels.

To remove a label, set the label's value to `null`.
```
    "labels": {
      "critical": null
    }
```

To remove all labels, set `labels` to `null`.
```
    "labels": null
```

Refer to the schema under `/v1/vault/keys2 POST` for a full description
of labels.

metaContains.description:
A valid JSON value.  Only keys whose 'meta' attribute contains the JSON value will be
returned.  Examples of JSON containment:

- Values contain themselves: `{"color":"red"}` contains `{"color":"red"}`

- Contained values can be nested: `{"info":{"size":"big","color":"red"}}` contains `{"info":{"color":"red"}}`, but not `{"color":"red"}`
- Array containment: `["east","west","north"]` contains `["east"]` and `["east","north"]`, but not `["south"]` or `["east","south"]`

labels.description:
Find keys that match label selector expressions. Multiple values are
logically ANDed.

Label selector expressions:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region=noram" ]
  ```
  OR with a double equals:
  ```
  [ "region==noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region!=noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have either `{"region": "noram"}` or `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region in (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have `{"region": "noram"}` nor `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region notin (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have the label key `region` (the value may be anything)
  ```
  [ "region" ]
  ```
- Select keys that not have the label key `region`
  ```
  [ "!region" ]
  ```

Multiple label selector expressions, logically ANDed:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not have
  `{"team": "sales"}`
  ```
  [ "region=noram", "team!=sales" ]

  ```

permissions.description:
The filter returns only those keys on which the user performing the query has the same permissions as given
in the query. The permissions are given to a group in the key meta and the group must have the `ReadKey`
permission. The user performing the query must be a member of the group having those permissions.
Allowed values are "EncryptWithKey", "DecryptWithKey", "MACWithKey", "MACVerifyWithKey", "SignWithKey",

WrapPBE.title: Password based encryption parameters for generating password based derived keys.
WrapPBE.description:
WrapPBE derives the key from the password and other parameters such as salt, iteration count, hashing algorithm, and derived key-length. PBE currently supports wrapping of symmetric keys (AES), private keys, and certificates.
WrapPBE is a two-step process to export a key as mentioned below. The key import is similar to the key export but it unwraps the target key in the second step.
Step 1 Use PBKDF2 with the specified parameters (pwd, hash-function, salt, iterations, purpose (opt), KEK length) to derive the KEK. For more details, refer to RFC 2898.
Step 2 Perform AES-KW/KWP to wrap the target key using the KEK derived from Step 1. The AES KEK size is calculated by the KEK length parameter as described in Step 1. For more details, refer to RFC 3394 and 5649.

hashAlgorithm.description: Underlying hashing algorithm that acts as a pseudorandom function to generate derive keys.

Base password to generate derive keys. It cannot be used in conjunction with passwordidentifier.
password must be in range of 8 bytes to 128 bytes.

pbeSalt must be in range of 16 bytes to 512 bytes.

User defined purpose. If specified will be prefixed to pbeSalt.
pbePurpose must not be greater than 128 bytes.

dklen.description:
Intended length in octets of the derived key.
dklen must be in range of 14 bytes to 512 bytes.

iteration.description:
Iteration count increase the cost of producing keys from a password.
Iteration must be in range of 1 to 1,00,00,000.

WrapRSAAES.description:
Information which is used to wrap/unwrap asymmetric keys using RSA AES KWP method.
This method internally requires AES key size to generate a temporary AES key and RSA padding.
To use WrapRSAAES, algorithm "RSA/RSAAESKEYWRAPPADDING" must be specified in WrappingEncryptionAlgo.

aesKeySize.description:
Size of AES key for RSA AES KWP. Accepted value are 128, 192, 256.
Default value is "256".

padding.description:
Padding specifies the type of padding scheme that needs to be set when exporting
the Key using RSA AES wrap.  Accepted values are "oaep", "oaep256", "oaep384", "oaep512",
Default value is "oaep256".

BasicLabels.description: Optional key/value pairs used to group keys.

AddLabels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. APIs that list keys can use
labels to filter the set of matching resources.

A label's key has an optional prefix up to 253 characters followed by a
forward slash and a required name up to 63 characters. For example,
`sales.widgets.com/region` is a label key with the prefix
`sales.widgets.com` and the name `region`, while `region` is a label key
without a prefix.

A label's value may be empty and may be up to 63 characters.

Each part of the label (i.e. the prefix, name, and value) must begin
and end with an alphanumeric character (a-zA-Z0-9). Characters
inbetween the beginning and end may contain alphanumeric characters,
dots (.), dashes (-) and underscores (_).

A Label can be a simple tag by specifying a key with no value
(e.g. `{ "critical": "" }`).

Here's a full example showing a name/value pair with prefix, a name/value pair, and a simple tag:
```
    "labels": {
      "sales.widgets.com/region": "noram",
      "team": "sales",
      "critical": ""
    }
```

UpdateLabels.description:
Optional key/value pairs used to group keys. When labels are provided
they are merged with the key's existing labels.

To remove a label, set the label's value to `null`.
```
    "labels": {
      "critical": null
    }
```

To remove all labels, set `labels` to `null`.
```
    "labels": null
```

Refer to the schema under `/v1/vault/keys2 POST` for a full description
of labels.

QueryLabels.description:
Find keys that match label selector expressions. Multiple values are
logically ANDed.

Label selector expressions:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region=noram" ]
  ```
  OR with a double equals:
  ```
  [ "region==noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have the label `{"region": "noram"}`:
  ```
  [ "region!=noram" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have either `{"region": "noram"}` or `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region in (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that do not have `{"region": "noram"}` nor `{"region": "emea"}`
  ```
  [ "region notin (noram,emea)" ]
  ```
- Select keys that have the label key `region` (the value may be anything)
  ```
  [ "region" ]
  ```
- Select keys that not have the label key `region`
  ```
  [ "!region" ]
  ```

Multiple label selector expressions, logically ANDed:
- Select keys that have the label `{"region": "noram"}` but do not have
  `{"team": "sales"}`
  ```
  [ "region=noram", "team!=sales" ]

  ```

usageMask.description:
Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage masks to allow certain usages. Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4),
Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512),
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384),
Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144),
Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). Add the usage mask values to allow
the usages. To set all usage mask bits, use 4194303.
Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728),
'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12),
'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

Defaults to 12 (Encrypt, Decrypt).

Not applicable to the following:
  * blob

If the data cannot be set as a JSON string, such as arbitrary binary data, then the caller should encode the data first (e.g. using base64). This field is optional only for dataType "password" as material will be system generated for the authorized users.

unexportable.description: Material is not exportable. Defaults to false.

undeletable.description: Object is not deletable. Defaults to false.

Policy.description:
Policies are access control rules.  They declare a set of
actions, applied to a set of resources, under an optional set of
conditions, which are either allowed or not allowed.

Policies, like other resources, share common properties like `id`,
`uri`, `name`, etc.

`actions` is a list of permissions.

TBD: link to
canonical dictionary of permissions.  Operations will require some
set of the these permissions

`resources` is a list of URI patterns.

effect.description:
The effect describes the effect of the policy. There are 4 possible values.
With effect, the allow flag gets deprecated. Please use one of the two and
use allow only if it is needed, instead use effect.

path.description: A JSON path which resolves to a value in the operation

The comparison operator used to compare the operation value
to the conditions values.

values.description:
The value or values to compare with the operation value.
Can be either a single value, or an array.  If an
array, each of the items in the array is compared to
the operation value, and if any match, the condition is
met.  In other words, the items are logically OR'd.

The description of this config which will also be used as the `description` property of the generated alarms when it is set.
If it not set, `message` property of the `records` will be used as alarms `description`.

condition.description:
The condition is a set of assertions that must evaluate to true
in order to generate an alarm. It is defined using
[Open Policy Agent's query language Rego](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/how-do-i-write-policies/)
which let's you compose complex rules to evaluate against an
audit record.

Note: all record properties must be prefixed with `input`
(e.g. `input.success` or `input.details.size`) because a record
is the input document in OPA's document model.

Example: generate an alarm when a weak RSA key is created. (All double quotes and newlines must be escaped when inserted as a JSON string.)

```
input.success
input.message == "Create Key"
input.details.algorithm == "RSA"
input.details.size <= 1024
```

threshold.description:
The threshold is an integer value which defines the limit for raising alarm by observing the number of records fetched in given time interval.
If it is not set then the default value will be 0 and it will not be used for raising alarm.

interval.description: The interval is an integer value which defines the time interval in seconds and it is used for raising alarms if a threshold hits within this time interval.

This optional parameter used only while migrating DSM backup files.
It can be used to control how CTE keys get migrated.
On the DSM, if a key has the "Source" field set to "From DSM" or an

it is fully accessible to members of the "CTE Clients" group.

If this flag is set to true, the key created in DSM from CCKM enterprise

This optional parameter used only while migrating cloud keys created in CCKM Enterprise.

keyOwners.description:
This optional parameter is a JSON object used only while migrating data from DSM to the CipherTrust Manager.
This parameter contains the key-value pairs. 
The key corresponds to the domain in the DSM backup and the value is the user id of an existing user in the root domain of the CipherTrust Manager. 
After migration, this value (user id) will be assigned to the corresponding new domain and will be the owner of all keys in that domain.
If no key owner is provided during migration, then the default owner will be the migration user.
For example: {domain1 : local|f224bced-800b-4103-9d94-5e5a6034706f}
Here domain1 is the domain name which will be migrated from the DSM and local|f224bced-800b-4103-9d94-5e5a6034706f
is the id of the user created on the CipherTrust Manager.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

Key rotation operation specific arguments. The
"key_rotation_params" and "database_backup_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
key_rotation_params.title: Key Rotation Parameters

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

database_backup_params.description:
Database backup operation specific arguments. Should be JSON-serializable
"key_rotation_params" and "database_backup_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
database_backup_params.title: Database Backup Parameters

scope.description: Scope of the backup to be taken - system (default) or domain.

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description: If true, the system backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition. Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to include in the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
By default, no filters are applied and the backup includes all keys.
For example, to back up all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

retentionCount.description: Number of backups saved for this job config. Default is an unlimited quantity.

description.description: User defined description associated with the backup. This is stored along with the backup, and is returned while retrieving the backup information, or while listing backups. Users may find it useful to store various types of information here: a backup name or description, ID of the HSM the backup is tied to, etc.

do_scp.description: If true, the system backup will also be transferred to the external server via SCP.

connection.description: Name or ID of the SCP connection which stores the details for SCP server.

expiration.description: Expiration time of the new key that will be created through scheduled rotation. If not specified, the new key material never expires. For example, if you set `expiration` to `6h`, the key material of the new key will expire in 6 hours.

If not specified, the scheduler rotates all the keys. For example, if you want the scheduler to rotate the keys that are expiring within six hours of the schedule run, set `expire_in` to `6h`. This parameter is not valid for cloud_name `gcp`.

expression.description:
Custom info type expression. The expression is a combination of the following commands.
- WORD '{FREE TEXT}'
- RANGE {TYPE} TIMES {FROM}-{TO}
- REFER '{PREFIX}_{KEYNAME}'
The different options for the {TYPE} are SPACE, HSPACE, VSPACE, BYTE, ALNUM, LETTER, DIGIT, PRINTABLE,
PRINTABLEASCII, PRINTABLENONALPHA, PRINTABLENONALNUM, GRAPHIC, SAMELINE, NONALNUM, NONALPHA and NONDIGIT
The {PREFIX}_{KEYNAME} is the Key field of the Infotype. The chosen infotype needs to be a built-in info type.
For each {PREFIX} used in the REFER section we need to add a INCLUDE 'DEFINE_{PREFIX}' at the start of the expression.
The commands are combined using the THEN clause.
Example:
  INCLUDE 'DEFINE_BANK'
  INCLUDE 'DEFINE_CHD'
  REFER 'CHD_AMERICANEXPRESS'
  THEN WORD 'Hello world'
  THEN RANGE ALNUM TIMES 0-1
  THEN REFER 'BANK_AUSTRALIA_ABN_STRICT'
  THEN REFER 'CHD_MASTERCARD'

region.description: Region of the info type. Possible values - Global, Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania

family.description:
Info type family. Possible values - Passport Number, License Number, Date Of Birth, Gender,
Telephone Number, Phone Number, Card Number, Patient Health Data, Email addresses, Login credentials,
IP Address, Ethnicity, Roll Number, Credit/Debit Cards, Bank Account Info, Personal Identification,
Mailing Address, Name, Religion, MAC Address

riskWeight.description:
Defines the value each match of the info type adds to the risk score.
This particular section of the risk score works like this: 
(It1Matches * It1Weight + It2Matches * It2Weight + ...) * 0.1

* exclude_prefix - requires expression field
* exclude_max_size - requires size field
* include_recent - requires days field

* include_date_range - requires fromDate and toDate fields
* exclude_suffix - requires expression field

type_url.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized potocol buffer message. The last segment of the URL's path must represent the fully qualified name of the type (as in `path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form (e.g., leading "." is not accepted). In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows: * If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed. * An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)
Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with type.googleapis.com. Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be used with implementation specific semantics.

Policy parameters (applicable only to encrypt and decrypt data plane API's for AWS XKS Key).
XKS Key usage would be allowed only if attribute values specifed in policy here would match the 
request data  received in encrypt/decrypt API request against value specified here).

aws_principal_arn.description:
ARN of the principal that invoked KMS Encrypt, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlainText 
or ReEncrypt API. Default value is '*' where all values of aws_principal_arn would be allowed.

aws_source_vpc.description:
AWS Source VPC indicates the VPC where request originated from. 
It is present only if the KMS API request was made against a VPC endpoint.

AWS Source VPC indicates the VPC endpoint where request originated from.

ARN of the KMS Key on which the Encrypt, ReEncrypt, GenerateDataKey or 
GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlainText API was invoked. Default value is '*' where all values of kms_key_arn
would be allowed.

kms_operation.description:
Indicates KMS API call that resulted in the XKS Proxy API request, 
eg any one of the four KMS API's (Encrypt, ReEncrypt, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext) 
can result in Encrypt call. Default value is '*' where all values of kms_operation would be allowed.
enum: Encrypt                         (applicable only for Encrypt API requests)
ReEncrypt                       (applicable for Encrypt as well as Decrypt API requests)
GenerateDataKey                 (applicable only for Encrypt API requests)
GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext (applicable only for Encrypt API requests)
