deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

query.description:
Use this object to specify the keys that need to be rotated.
All keys are rotated when this object is not specified.
This object is the same as the one used for POST request to the /v1/vault/query-keys endpoint.
Refer to the documentation in that endpoint for further details on formulating the query.

meta.description:
Use this object to modify the metadata on a key that is replaced by the key rotation procedure.
This object should be a JSON serialized object. The metadata on the replaced key (which is
also a JSON object) is merged with this JSON object.

scope.description: Scope of the backup to be taken - system (default) or domain.

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description: If true, the system backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition. Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.

These five values indicate when the job should be executed. They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.
Valid values are 0-59 (minutes), 0-23 (hours), 1-31 (day of month), 1-12 or jan-dec (month), and 0-6 or sun-sat (day of week). Names are case insensitive. For use of special characters, consult the Time Specification description at the top of this page.

For example:
* To run every min: "* * * * *"
* To run on Saturday at 23:45(11:45 PM): "45 23 * * 6"
* To run on Monday at 09:00: "0 9 * * 1"

key_rotation_params.title: Key Rotation Parameters

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

The result of a query on the resource collection endpoints.
Collection endpoints (e.g. '/widgets/') return a set of resources
wrapped in this envelope. The envelope structure contains meta data
about the list of results, to assist in paging.

skip.description:
The index of the first record returned.  Equivalent to 'offset' in
SQL.

limit.description: The max number of records returned.  Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL.

total.description: The total records matching the query.

uri.description: A human readable unique identifier of the resource

account.description: The account which owns this resource.

operation.description: Type of operation to configure. Possible values are "Key Rotation", "Database Backup", "Sync CRL", "CCKM Synchronization" and "CCKM XKS Credential Rotation".

run_at.description:
Described using the cron expression format : "* * * * *"
These five values indicate when the job should be executed. They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.
Valid values are 0-59 (minutes), 0-23 (hours), 1-31 (day of month), 1-12 or jan-dec (month), and 0-6 or sun-sat (day of week). Names are case insensitive. For use of special characters, consult the Time Specification description at the top of this page.

For example:
* To run every min: "* * * * *"
* To run on Saturday at 23:45(11:45 PM): "45 23 * * 6"
* To run on Monday at 09:00: "0 9 * * 1"

run_on.description:
Optional flag. Default is 'any'.
* Use 'any' to run the config on any node in the cluster.
* Use '<specific node id>' to run the config on that node.

end_date.description:

Key rotation operation specific arguments. The "key_rotation_params","database_backup_params",
"cckm_synchronization_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_params" fields are mutually exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
key_rotation_params.title: Key Rotation Parameters

deactivate_replaced_key.description:
**Deprecated**: It is recommended to use "replaced_key_state" and "change_state_after_time" fields.
It is an optional integer that can be used to deactivate the keys that are replaced by the key rotation procedure.
When "deactivate_replaced_key" is not specified, the state of the replaced key remains the same.
This field represents the time ( number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key is deactivated.

replaced_key_state.description:
An optional string to set the state of the previous key version to "Deactivated" or "ProtectStop" after key rotation.  
This parameter should only be used with the "change_state_after_time" parameter.  
Also, ensure not to use "replaced_key_state" parameter when "deactivate_replaced_key" is used.

change_state_after_time.description:
Optional integer to be used with "replaced_key_state". 
It is the time (number of seconds >= 0) after which the replaced key will change its state to the value defined in "replaced_key_state".

offset.description:
Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
Activation Date of the replacement key.
- If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
existing key. 
- If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
- Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
- Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this 
key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the
Replacement Key's Activation Date will be:
14:33:26 + 00:10:00 = 2024-01-11T14:43:26.

database_backup_params.description:
Database backup operation specific arguments. Should be JSON-serializable
"key_rotation_params", "cckm_synchronization_params", "cckm_key_rotation_params" and "cckm_xks_credential_rotation_params" fields are mutually
exclusive (cannot be set simultaneously).
database_backup_params.title: Database Backup Parameters

scope.description: Scope of the backup to be taken - system (default) or domain.

backupKey.description: ID of backup key used for encrypting the backup. The default backup key is used if this is not specified.

tiedToHSM.description: If true, the system backup can only be restored to instances that use the same HSM partition. Valid only with the system scoped backup.

resourceType.description: Type of resources to be backed up. Valid values are "Keys", "cte_policies", "customer_fragments" and, "users_groups".

resourceQuery.description:
A JSON object containing resource attributes and attribute values to be queried.
The resources returned in the query are backed up. If empty, all the resources of the specified resourceType will be backed up.
For Keys, valid resourceQuery paramater values are the same as the body of the 'vault/query-keys' POST endpoint described on the Keys page.
If multiple parameters of 'vault/query-keys' are provided then the result will be AND of all.
To back up AES keys with a meta parameter value containing `{"info":{"color":"red"}}}`, use
`{"algorithm":"AES", "metaContains": "{"info":{"color":"red"}}}"`. To backup specific keys using names, use {"names":["key1", "key2"]}.

For CTE policies, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/transparent-encryption/policies' endpoint described in the CTE > Policies section.
For example, to back up LDT policies only, use `{"policy_type":"LDT"}`. Similarly, to back up policies with learn mode enabled, use `{"never_deny": true}`.
For users, the valid resourceQuery parameter values are the same as query parameters of the list '/v1/usermgmt/users' endpoint as described in the “Users” page.
For example, to back up all users with name  "frank" and email id "frank@local", use {"name":"frank","email": "frank@local"}.

For Customer fragments, valid `resourceQuery` parameter values are 'ids' and 'names' of Customer fragments. To backup specific customer fragments using ids, use {"ids":["370c4373-2675-4aa1-8cc7-07a9f95a5861", "4e1b9dec-2e38-40d7-b4d6-244043200546"]}. To backup specific customer fragments using names, use {"names":["customerFragment1", "customerFragment2"]}.

filters.description:
A set of selection criteria to specify what resources to include in the backup. Only applicable to domain-scoped backups.
By default, no filters are applied and the backup includes all keys.
For example, to back up all keys with a name containing 'enc-key', set the filters to `[{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery":{"name":"*enc-key*"}}]`.

retentionCount.description: Number of backups saved for this job config. Default is an unlimited quantity.

description.description: User defined description associated with the backup. This is stored along with the backup, and is returned while retrieving the backup information, or while listing backups. Users may find it useful to store various types of information here: a backup name or description, ID of the HSM the backup is tied to, etc.

do_scp.description: If true, the system backup will also be transferred to the external server via SCP.

connection.description: Name or ID of the SCP connection which stores the details for SCP server.

client_configuration_id.description:
Client configuration identifier.

**Note:**
Use either client_configuration_id to link this profile to an existing configuration,

configurations.description:
Parameters required to initialize connector.
- symmetric_key_cache_enabled: Whether the symmetric key cache is enabled.
  Options.
  - true (Default)
  - false
- symmetric_key_cache_expiry: Time after which the symmetric key cache will expire. Default: 43200
- size_of_connection_pool: The maximum number of connections that can persist in connection pool. Default: 300
- load_balancing_algorithm: Determines how the client selects a Key Manager from a load balancing group.
  Options.
  - round-robin (Default)
  - random
- connection_idle_timeout: The time a connection is allowed to be idle in the connection pool before it gets automatically closed. Default: 600000
- connection_retry_interval: The amount of time to wait before trying to reconnect to a disabled server. Default: 600000
- log_level: The level of logging to determine verbosity of clients logs.
  Options.
  - ERROR
  - WARN (Default)
  - INFO
  - DEBUG
- log_rotation: Specifies how frequently the log file is rotated.
  Options.
  - None
  - Daily (Default)
  - Weekly
  - Monthly
  - Size
- log_size_limit: The maximum size of  log file. Default: 100K
- log_gmt: This value specifies if timestamp in logs should be formatted in GMT or not. Default disabled
- log_type: Type of the log.
  Options.
  - Console (Default)
  - File
  - Multi
- log_file_path: This value specifies the path where log file will be created
- connection_timeout: Connection timeout value for clients. Default: 60000
- connection_read_timeout: Read timeout value for clients. Default: 7000
- heartbeat_interval: Frequency interval for sending heartbeat by connectors. Default: 300
- heartbeat_timeout_count: heartbeat timeout missed communication counts with CM for connectors to decide on cleanup profile cache. Default: -1
- tls_to_appserver
- dial_timeout: Specifies the maximum duration (in seconds) the DPG server will wait for a connection with the Application Server to succeed.
- dial_keep_alive: Specifies the interval (in seconds) between keep-alive probes for an active network connection.
- auth_method_used the parameter is used to define how and from where to validate the application user
  - scheme_name: the type of authentication scheme to be used to fetch the suer
    Options.
    - Basic (Default)
    - Bearer
  - token_field: the json field which have the user information. Required when scheme_name is Bearer.
- jwt_details: Information about the the JWT validation.  **Note:** Use either `jwt_details` or `jwt_verification_configurations`. These fields are mutually exclusive. `jwt_verification_configurations` enables multiple JWT verification sources.
  - issuer: A string that identifies the principal that issued the JWT. If left empty, the iss (issuer) field in the JWT will not be validated.
  - jwks_url: A string that provides the JWKs URL from which JSON Web Keys (JWKs) are retrieved to validate the JWT.
  - jwks_refresh_duration: The duration (in days) after which the JWKs will be refreshed. The value must be specified as integer.
  - jwt_username_field: Specifies the location of the username in the JWT. Access policy will be applied based on the username present in this location. The value must be a string.
  - enable_dpop: A boolean flag to enable DPoP verification. To enable DPoP verification JWT verification must be turned on either using public key or JWKS URL.

- jwt_verification_configurations: Array of JWT verification configurations to support multiple JWT verification sources.
  Each configuration defines how the JWT should be validated.
  - jwt_verification_method (string, required): Specifies how the JWT should be verified. Valid values: `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - issuer (string): Identifies the entity that issued the JWT. If not provided, the iss (issuer) claim in the JWT will be ignored during validation.
  - jwks_url (string, conditional): JWKs endpoint URL used for token verification. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwks_refresh_duration (integer, conditional): Number of days after which the JWKs will be refreshed. **Applicable only if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwks_url`.
  - jwt_username_field (string, optional): Specifies the claim in the JWT that contains the username. Access policy is applied based on the username value in this field.
  - enable_dpop (boolean, optional): Enables DPoP verification. DPoP verification requires JWT verification via either `jwks_url` or `jwt_verification_key`.
  - jwt_verification_key (string, conditional): Public key used to validate JWT signatures. **Required if** `jwt_verification_method` is `jwt_verification_key`.

- enable_performance_metrics:  Flag used to enable performance metrics.
  Options.
  - true (Default)
  - false

- kms_cluster_configuration: Optional. Enables clients to connect to KMS in cluster mode.
  A maximum of 3 tiers are supported. Each tier accepts a list of IP strings. All tiers are optional.
  - tier1 (array of strings): Primary KMS node IPs.
  - tier2 (array of strings): Secondary KMS node IPs. Requires tier1 to be set.
  - tier3 (array of strings): Tertiary KMS node IPs. Requires tier2 to be set.

A maximum of 3 tiers are supported. Each tier accepts a list of IP strings. All tiers are optional.
- tier1 (array of strings): Primary KMS node IPs.
- tier2 (array of strings): Secondary KMS node IPs. Requires tier1 to be set.
- tier3 (array of strings): Tertiary KMS node IPs. Requires tier2 to be set.

PEM encoded PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 public key used to validate a JWT.

version.description: The version of the protection policy.

iv.description:
IV to be used during crypto operations.
IV can be provided only for the following algorithms:
- AES/CBC/NoPadding
- AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
 - AES/CTR


 - ECIESwithSHA224/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA256/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA384/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA512/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA224/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA256/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA384/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA512/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- FPE/AES/UNICODE

tweak_algorithm.description:
Tweak algorithm to be used during crypto operations.
Options:
- SHA1
- SHA256
- None

algorithm.description:
Algorithm to be used during crypto operations.
Supported algorithms are:
- AES/CBC/NoPadding
- AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- AES/ECB/NoPadding
- AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding
- AES/GCM
 - AES/CTR


 - Random2
- FPE/AES/UNICODE
- FPE/FF1v2/UNICODE
- FPE/FF3/UNICODE
- FPE/FF3-1/UNICODE
- DATEv3
 - RSA/PKCS1Padding
- RSA/PKCS1OAEPPadding
- RSA/PKCS1OAEPPaddingSHA256
- RSA/PKCS1OAEPPaddingSHA384
- RSA/PKCS1OAEPPaddingSHA512
 - ECIESwithSHA224/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA256/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA384/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA512/AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- ECIESwithSHA224/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA256/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA384/AES/CBC/NoPadding
- ECIESwithSHA512/AES/CBC/NoPadding

tag_length.description: Tag length required for AES/GCM algorithm. Valid values are 32 - 128 in multiples of 8, i.e 32,40,48,56, ... 128

aad.description: Additional authenticated data for AES/GCM algorithm. This is an optional field

random_nonce.description:
parameter to enable the random nonce. The random nonce parameter can be: internal or external
- For the following algorithms an IV is not required as it will be generated randomly:
  - AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
  - AES/CBC/NoPadding
  - AES/GCM
   - AES/CTR


 - For the following algorithms a tweak is not required as it will be generated randomly:
    - FPE/AES/UNICODE
    - FPE/FF1v2/UNICODE
    - FPE/FF3/UNICODE
    - FPE/FF3-1/UNICODE
 - Irreversible Token can not be set to true if Random Nonce is selected.

use_external_versioning.description: If set to true, external versioning is enabled for the protection policy. The version details are stored in a separate external parameter. The default value is false.

disable_versioning.description: If set to true, versioning is not maintained for the protection policies. The default value is false.

access_policy_name.description: Access Policy associated with the protection policy.

prefix.description: A static string to be added to the tokens. Maximum value of prefix can be 7.

data_format.description:
The format in which the data to be protected will be provided.
Options:
- luhn

allow_small_input.description: Allow small input in protection policy. This parameter is only supported for FPE and RANDOM2 algorithms. By default, its value is true.

irreversible_token.description:
This parameter generates ciphertext that cannot be reversed. By default, its value is set to false.
IV is not supported with AES algorithms, Tweak is not supported with FPE algorithms, and Random Nonce can not be set to true when Irreversible Token is set to true.
Algorithms that support irreversible token are:
- AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding
- AES/CBC/NoPadding
- AES/GCM
 - AES/CTR
- FPE/AES/UNICODE
- FPE/FF1v2/UNICODE
- FPE/FF3/UNICODE
- FPE/FF3-1/UNICODE

date_format.description:
Format of the date. Supported formats are:
- YYMMDD
- MMDDYY
- DDMMYY
- MMYY
- MMMDDYY
- DDMMMYY
- YYYYMMDD
- MMDDYYYY
- DDMMYYYY
- MMYYYY
- DDMMMYYYY
- MMMDDYYYY
- DDMMMMYYYY
- MMMMDDYYYY

start_year.description: Start year defines the beginning of the supported range. Its value must be between 1000 and 9999.  The start year must always be less than or equal to the end year. If the date format uses two-digit years (YY), both the start year and end year must fall within the same century.  Otherwise, the difference between the start year and end year can be up to 999 years.

end_year.description: End year defines the last year in the supported range. Its value must be between 1000 and 9999. If the date format uses two-digit years (YY), both the start year and end year must fall within the same century.  Otherwise, the difference between start and end years can be up to 999 years.

case_sensitive.description:
Options:
- true: If set to true, all the database objects mentioned in the policy file will be processed in the same case as input.
- false: If set to false, all the database objects mentioned in the policy file will be automatically converted to CAPITAL case.

in_place_update.description: If enabled, BDT transform data in-place within the database, rather than the default behavior that creates a new destination table containing the transformed data.

unprocessed_record_file.description: The file path where all the failed files would be saved (having .failed extension)

source_table.description: Name of the source table. It is applicable only for DB-to-DB Transformation.

source_schema.description: Name of the source table schema. It is applicable only for DB-to-DB Transformation.

destination_table.description: Name of the destination table. It is applicable only for DB-to-DB Transformation.

destination_schema.description: Name of the destination table schema. It is applicable only for DB-to-DB Transformation.

create_destination_table.description: If set to true, a table will be created in the destination database. It is applicable only for DB-to-DB Transformation.

subset.description: Table-specific data filter criteria. Filter input data based on these criteria.  Not supported for file transformation.

offset.description: It indicated start of record index.

limit.description: Maximum number of records/rows to transform, starting from offset.

recurrency.description: Select every Nth record. By default, select every record.

order_by.description: Sort input data based on the column specified. By default, first column will be used.

order.description: Order in which output data will be sorted. ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending) record order is supported.

filters.description: It filters the input data with specific criteria using selector, operator and expresion.

labels.description:
Labels are key/value pairs used to group resources. They are based on Kubernetes Labels, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/.

To add a label, set the label's value as follows.
```
    "labels": {
      "key1": "value1",
      "key2": "value2"
    }
```
To remove a key/value pair, pass value null to the particular key
```
    "labels": {
      "key1": null
    }
```

aws_sts_regional_endpoints.description:
By default, AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) is available as a global service, and all AWS STS requests
go to a single endpoint at https://sts.amazonaws.com. Global requests map to the US East (N. Virginia) Region.
AWS recommends using Regional AWS STS endpoints instead of the global endpoint to reduce latency,
build in redundancy, and increase session token validity.
valid values are:
- legacy (default): Uses the global AWS STS endpoint, sts.amazonaws.com
- regional: The SDK or tool always uses the AWS STS endpoint for the currently configured Region.

To know more about AWS STS please go through the following link
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_enable-regions.html

aws_region.description:
AWS region. only used when aws_sts_regional_endpoints is equal to regional otherwise, it takes default values
according to Cloud Name given. Default values are:
- for aws, default region will be "us-east-1"
- for aws-us-gov, default region will be "us-gov-east-1"
- for aws-cn, default region will be "cn-north-1"

is_certificate_used.description:
User has the option to choose the Certificate Authentication method instead of Client Secret for Azure Cloud connection. In order to use the Certificate, set it to true. Once the connection is created, in the response user will get a certificate.
By default, the certificate is valid for 2 Years. User can update the certificate in the existing connection by setting it to true in Update (PATCH) API call.

certificate.description: User has the option to upload external certificate for Azure Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option cert_bundle, is_certificate_used and client_secret.User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 2048 or 4096. User can also update the new external certificate in the existing connection in Update (PATCH) API call. Any unused certificate will automatically deleted in 24 hours.

cert_duration.description: Duration in days for which the azure certificate is valid, default (730 i.e. 2 Years).

external_certificate_used.description: true if the certificate associated with the connection is generated externally, false otherwise.

cloud_name.description: Name of the cloud.

certificate.description: User has the option to upload external certificate for Azure Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option cert_bundle, is_certificate_used and client_secret. User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 2048 or 4096.

cert_bundle.description: User has the option to upload external certificate and key for Azure Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option certificate, is_certificate_used and client_secret.

data.description:
Data can be Certificate-Key pair generated externally, in PEM or PKCS12 format or only Certificate in PEM format, for Certificate the user first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 2048 or 4096.
Only one of Certificate, Client Secret, or Cert Bundle is allowed.
For PKCS12 and encrypted key, password is mandatory. The PKCS12 data must be in base64 encoding, it should contain both private key and certificate.

format.description: Format of uploaded Certificate-Key, can be PEM(default) or PKCS12. Ensure to provide format for PKCS12 data.

password.description: It specifies the password required for decrypting PKCS12 or encrypted PEM data.

active_directory_endpoint.description: Azure stack active directory authority URL

salesforce_mtls_params.description: Sensitive parameters specific to a Salesforce connection.

enable_mutual_tls.description:
Setting it to true will enforce SSL or TLS mutual authentication for Salesforce API calls.
Default is false.

tls_client_certificate_with_private_key.description:
TLS client certificate along with private key to be used as client side certificate
to support Salesforce Mutual Authentication Certificate option. Provide certificate chain as a single
PEM-encoded CA-signed certificate representing the concatenated chain of certificates.
The uploaded certificate chain must include the intermediate certificates and private key.
Certificate order should be client certificate and then add its signing certificate, intermediate certificates
if any followed by private key of Client certificate. If Private key is encrypted then specify
password/passphrase used to encrypt Private key in tls_client_private_key_password param.

tls_client_private_key_password.description:
Password/passphrase for TLS Client Private key. Provide value if private key is encrypted with
password/passphrase.

salesforce_connection_credentials.description: Sensitive parameters specific to a Salesforce connection.

password.description:
Password for the Salesforce account. This a mandatory parameter for a connection
with Client Credential Authentication method. This parameter is not needed for
Certificate Authentication or when using domain name.
“Allow OAuth Username-Password Flows” must be enabled under
Setup -> Settings -> Identity -> OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings
in your salesforce account to use password for authentication.

client_secret.description:
Consumer Secret for the Salesforce application. This a mandatory parameter for a connection
with Client Credential Authentication method. This parameter is not needed for
Certificate Authentication.

tls_client_private_key_password.description:
Password/passphrase for TLS Client Private key. Provide value if private key is encrypted with
password/passphrase.

cloud_name.description: Name or Type of the Salesforce cloud. Supported cloud options are listed below:

client_id.description: Unique Identifier (client ID/consumer key) for the Salesforce Application.

username.description: Username of the Salesforce account. Not required when using domain name.

domain_name.description:
The domain_name represents My Domain that could be found in your salesforce account. This My Domain acts
as a subdomain in framing URL https://MyDomain.my.salesforce.com which is eventually used to establish a
connection to salesforce account. The client_credentials grant uses this URL to make a request when
usernmame and password are not provided.
You can refer to Salesforce documentation in order to learn more about My Domain.
This parameter cannot be used if hostname is specified.

hostname.description:
The hostname of the salesforce instance to connect to. Example: test-site-aesf24.sf-onp-dc-test-02.ml.
When hostname is specified, domain name parameter cannot be used.

audience.description:
The audience identifies the authorization server as an intended audience.
Use the authorization server’s URL for the audience value for salesforce.com cloud:
https://login.salesforce.com, https://test.salesforce.com
This variable is supported with certificate authentication only.

certificate.description: Salesforce server certificate.

external_certificate_used.description: true if the certificate associated with the connection is generated externally, false otherwise.

is_certificate_used.description:
User has the option to choose the Certificate Authentication method instead of Client Credentials (password and client_secret)
Authentication for Salesforce Cloud connection. In order to use the Certificate, set this field to true.
Once the connection is created, in the response user will get a certificate.

cert_duration.description: Duration in days for which the salesforce server certificate is valid, default (730 i.e. 2 Years).

certificate.description: User has the option to upload external certificate for Salesforce Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option is_certificate_used and client_secret. User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 1024, 2048 or 4096. User can also update the new external certificate in the existing connection in Update (PATCH) API call. Any unused certificate will automatically deleted in 24 hours.

regenerate_certificate.description: To update the certificate, set the regenerate_certificate to true. This will update the certificate, corresponding private key and certificate subject.

PEM-encoded CA-signed certificate representing the concatenated chain of certificates.
The uploaded certificate chain must include the intermediate certificates and private key.
Certificate order should be client certificate and then add its signing certificate, intermediate certificates
if any followed by private key of Client certificate. If Private key is encrypted then specify
password/passphrase used to encrypt Private key in tls_client_private_key_password param.

User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) in POST /v1/connectionmgmt/connections/csr. The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 1024, 2048 or 4096. User can also update the new external certificate in the existing connection in Update (PATCH) API call. Any unused certificate will automatically deleted in 24 hours.

insecure_skip_verify.description:
Optional flag to disable verifying the server's certficate. It ignores both the operating system's CAs and `root_cas` if provided. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

Default value is `false`.

root_cas.description:
Optional list of CA certificates that are used to determine if the LDAP server certificate is trusted. Only applies if the `server_url` scheme is `ldaps`.

If not provided, the server's certificate is verified using the operating system's default CAs.

Accepts [PEM encoded certificates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail). Here's an example showing an abbreviated (see `[...]`) list of root CAs.
```
"root_cas": [
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEiTCCA3GgAwIBAgIQEtTWutN7HdEKAAAAAOthCDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBG[...]rVtyMKdOXGZl1gR22A==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIHCjCCBfKgAwIBAgIQDhZMtvVrLG4NDkY/70TmRDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADBw[...]lYgbVhEaSeWnKcSG/4OJDLgbJL1cQa5BQUjWiZo7\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
]
```

bind_dn.description: Object which has permission to search under the root DN for users.

base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for users.

search_filter.description: LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in.

user_login_attribute.description: Attribute inside the user object which contains the username used to login with.

group_base_dn.description: Starting point to use when searching for groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_filter.description: Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups. This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.

group_name_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.

user_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. Example: uid, dn

When this property is set it uses the specified attribute to test for user equality. This primarily affects LDAP group maps. For example:
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`cn: John Doe`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`cn`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`John Doe`", not "`cn=John Doe`", in order for the user to be considered part of the group.
- If a user's LDAP entry has "`customDN: cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" and the LDAP configuration has "`user_dn_attribute`" set to "`customDN`", then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly "`cn=John Doe,ou=Users`" in order for the user to be considered part of the group.

group_id_attribute.description: Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name). This value should be unique and can be left empty to disable group support for this connection. If group_id_attribute is not provided, it will default to  'group_name_attribute'.

group_member_field.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid
This value can be left empty to disable group membership support for this connection.

user_member_field.description:
Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber.
In case, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen.

group_dn_attribute.description:
Attribute inside the group object which contains the group's distinguished name.
When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber

For example:
- if a groups's LDAP entry has "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`" and the LDAP configuration has "`group_dn_attribute`" set to "`dn`", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "`cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com`", in order for the user to be considered part of group.

server_maximum_page_size.description:
This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
By default 'server_maximum_page_size' is set to 1000, and therefore entries are retrieved from LDAP server through pagination. We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size.
To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0. Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

early_listing_stop.description:
This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched. When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user. To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1. When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.

usageMask.description:
Filters results based on matching Cryptographic usage mask. Add the usage mask values to allow the usages. 
The associated values are - Sign (1), Verify (2), Encrypt (4), Decrypt (8), Wrap Key (16), Unwrap Key (32), Export (64), MAC Generate (128), MAC Verify (256), Derive Key (512), 
Content Commitment (1024), Key Agreement (2048), Certificate Sign (4096), CRL Sign (8192), Generate Cryptogram (16384), Validate Cryptogram (32768), Translate Encrypt (65536), 
Translate Decrypt (131072), Translate Wrap (262144), Translate Unwrap (524288), FPE Encrypt (1048576), FPE Decrypt (2097152). To set all usage mask bits, 
use 4194303 (all usage masks including Export). Equivalent usageMask values for deprecated usages 'fpe' (FPE Encrypt + FPE Decrypt = 3145728), 'blob' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 
'hmac' (MAC Generate + MAC Verify = 384), 'encrypt' (Encrypt + Decrypt = 12), 'sign' (Sign + Verify = 3), 'any' (4194303 - all usage masks).

algorithm.description: The Cryptographic algorithm of the template that is used to create the specific key. ML-DSA is a post-quantum digital signature algorithm per FIPS 204 (Tech Preview).

curveid.description: The Cryptographic curve id of a template is used for the elliptic key. This is a mandatory parameter for 'EC' algorithm.

parameterSet.description: Specifies the ML-DSA parameter set. Valid values are 'ml-dsa-44', 'ml-dsa-65', and 'ml-dsa-87'. Defaults to 'ml-dsa-65' if not specified.

size.description: The Bit length of the key using this template.The Size is mandatory for all supported algorithms except for algorithms 'ec' and 'ml-dsa'.

unexportable.description: The key created using this template will not be exportable. The default value is false.

undeletable.description: The key created using this template will not be deleted. The default value is false.

format.description:

For Asymmetric Keys the valid options are
-pkcs1
-pkcs8
-pkcs12
For ML-DSA keys, only 'pkcs8' format is supported. PKCS#1 and PKCS#12 are not supported for ML-DSA keys.

For Symmetric Keys the valid options are
-raw
-opaque

state.description:
This specified the valid key state for creation of Key using Template
Options:
- Pre-Active
- Active
  For Active State activation Date is required. Activation Date must not be a future Date.
- Deactived
  For Deactived State deactivationDate is required. Deactivation Date must not be before Activation Date or ProtectStopDate.

xts.description: If set to true, then key created will be XTS/CBC-CS1 Key. Defaults to false. Key algorithm must be 'AES.

objectType.description:
This specifies the type of object that needs to be created. Valid values are 'Symmetric Key', 'Public Key', 'Private Key' or 'Certificate'. The object type is inferred for many objects, but must be supplied for the certificate object.
For algorithm RSA or EC  to create a certificate objectType shall be specified as Certificate.
ObjectType Symmetric Key is supported for algorithms
 - AES

 - TDES
 - SEED
 - HMAC

 - RSA
 - EC

 - ML-DSA

 - AES

keyVersion.name: keyVersion

hint.name: hint
hint.description: This string identifies the type of input. It can be one of following printable strings - 'digit', 'alphabet', 'alphanumeric', 'printable' and 'unicode'. This hint needs to be passed.

charset.name: charset

tweakAlg.name: tweakAlg
tweakAlg.description: This string specifies the algorithm used for converting the tweak string into the tweak used by the FPE algorithm. Allowed values are "sha1", "sha256", "sha512" and "none". Defaults to "none".

tweak.name: tweak
tweak.description: This string identifies the tweak to be used along with the cryptographic key for hiding/unhiding the data. If tweakAlg is "none", this should be a 8-byte array encoded in hex. Length of encoded string is 16 bytes. It can be any arbitrary string if the tweakAlg is not "none". If provided, it must be the same for both hide and unhide operations for a given data. Tweak is not allowed if tweakAlg is empty.

iv.name: iv
iv.description: This string identifies the IV to be used along with the cryptographic key for hiding/unhiding data. It is required only if the input data length is larger than the FPE block length. The block length depends on the hint (digit-56, alphabet,alphanumeric-32, printable-28 bytes). The IV should not be supplied if the data length does not exceed the FPE block length. The characters in the IV should lie in the alphabet specified via the hint. The length of the IV should equal the FPE block size.

defaultiv.name: defaultiv
defaultiv.description: This boolean identifies if the user wants to use the default IV along with the cryptographic key for encrypting/decrypting data. False is 0 and True is 1. This field was introduced to support specific legacy integrations and applications. New applications are strongly recommended to use a unique IV for each encryption request.

hash.name: hash
hash.description: This string identifies the hex encoded mac to be verified for the given data.

hashAlgo.name: hashAlgo
hashAlgo.description: This string specifies the hash algorithm used for generating signature. For ECDSA the allowed values are "SHA1", "SHA-256", "SHA-384", "SHA-512", "SHA3-224", "SHA3-256", "SHA3-384", "SHA3-512" and "none". For RSA, the allowed values are "SHA1", "SHA-256", "SHA-384", "SHA-512" and "none". For EdDSA, the allowed value is "". For HashEdDSA, the allowed values are "SHA-512" and ""(defaults to SHA-512). Not applicable to ML-DSA.

signAlgo.name: signAlgo
signAlgo.description: This string specifies the signing algorithm used for generating signature. Allowed values are "ML-DSA" (Tech Preview), "EdDSA", "HashEdDSA", "RSA" and "ECDSA".

signature.description: This string identifies the hex encoded signature to be verified for the given data.

context.name: context
context.description: Optional context string for digital signature operations. Not applicable to RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, HashEdDSA algorithms. For ML-DSA (Tech Preview), this is a hex-encoded context string (FIPS 204, Section 3.2) that binds the signature to a specific application domain. Maximum length is 510 hex characters (255 bytes).

mode.name: mode

pad.name: pad

If an IV is supplied, it should be in hexadecimal format. It should be 16 bytes long (hex string is 32 characters long) for AES-CBC, 8 bytes for TDES-CBC, and between 1 and 16 bytes for AES-GCM.

Users.description:
Users are unique individuals or systems using the API.

Users are authenticated against authentication systems, called
"connections". A "connection" can be an identity provider, such as
an OpenID endpoint, or a directory, such as LDAP or AD.  CipherTrust Manager
has a built-in, internal user directory, whose connection name is
"local_account".

The User's `connection` property refers to the authentication system in
which the user's credentials and identity reside.  When you create a User,
you must specify the `connection`: this tells CipherTrust Manager which
authentication system it should use to authenticate the User.
Some connections may require additional, connection-specific
properties to create the User.

CipherTrust Manager supports external authentication systems.
Once a user is authenticated against an external authentication system, a
user will be created with connection|unique ID. This unique ID will be
taken from an attribute associated with that user on the external authentication
system. For more information, look at Connections.

The `user_id` identifies Users and it is in the form of:

    connection|unique ID in that connection

The internal user database uses UUIDs, so a user in the `local_account`
connection might have a `user_id` of:

    local_account|9cd4196b-b4b3-42d7-837f-d4fdeff36538

Users have two attributes, `user_metadata` and `app_metadata`, which
can be used to store application-specific information.  The system
does not use this information; it just stores it for the convenience
of applications using the API.  These properties are unstructured JSON
documents: the caller can put any JSON-structured information in them.

`user_metadata` is typically used to store application-specific data which
the end user is allowed to see and modify, such as user preferences.

`app_metadata` is typically used to store application-specific data
about the user which the end user is *not* allowed to view or modify,
such as the user's security roles.

`certificate_subject_dn` is used to store Distinguished Name. To enable certificate-based authentication, add "user_certificate" authentication method in `allowed_auth_methods`.
Value of Distinguished Name in the certificate and the value in the user object must match for successful authentication.

`nickname` has been deprecated. It will be removed in a future release.

`allowed_client_types` and `allowed_auth_methods` do not control login behavior for users in admin group.

Connections/Connections.description:
Connections defines how and where to authenticate CipherTrust Manager users.

A "connection" can be an identity provider, such as a OpenID endpoint, or
a directory, such as LDAP or AD. CipherTrust Manager has a built-in,
internal user directory, whose connection name is "local_account".

When you create a connection, you must specify the `name`, `strategy`, and
several options which will be listed below in the POST command (create). `name` is
the friendly name that is associated with the connection that will be used
by a user. `strategy` will be the type of connection. Currently, the allowed
strategies are 'ldap', 'oidc' and 'local_account'.

For an **LDAP** connection:

In order to create a connection, the following parameters must be provided:

- `server_url`
- `root_dn`
- `uid_field`

The following parameters are optional:

- `search_filter`
- `guid_field`
- `bind_dn`
- `bind_pass`
- `user_dn_field`
- `group_base_dn`
- `group_filter`
- `group_id_field`
- `group_member_field`
- `insecure_skip_verify`
- `root_cas`

If the `bind_dn` and `bind_pass` are not provided when the connection is
created, the user's credentials will be used to run the LDAP search. If
the `guid_field` is not provided, it will default to whatever `uid_field`
is.

For an **Active Directory** connection:

- `user_dn_field` should be set to `distingushedName`.
- `search_filter` should be set to `(objectClass=User)`

Default values for other optional parameters should suffice, but can be
configured as required.

Group support:

To enable group support for a connection, `bind_dn`, `bind_password`, `group_base_dn`,
`group_filter`, `group_id_field` and `group_member_field` are mandatory
parameters. If any one of them is not specified, group support is
disabled for the connection.

These parameters are discussed more in-depth in the POST command (create)

Here is an example of a successful creation of an LDAP connection:

    {
      'name' : 'testServer',
      'strategy' : 'ldap',
      'options': {
        'bind_dn': 'cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com',
        'bind_pass' : 'admin',
        'server_url' : 'ldap://ldap.example.com:389',
        'root_dn' : 'dc=example,dc=com',
        'uid_field' : 'uid'
      }
    }

For an **OpenID Connect** (OIDC) connection:

In order to create a connection, the following parameters must be provided:

- `client_id`
- `redirect_uris`
- `discovery_uri`

LDAP Browse.description:
This section is for browsing LDAP users and groups. There are two endpoints which provides us with following capability:

- `LDAP User Listing`
- `LDAP Group Listing`

The LDAP connection needs to be created in **LDAP Connection Manager**.

When browsing LDAP users, the POST parameters are optional and overwrites the values stored in the Connection Manager LDAP connection.

To browse more users and groups, use parameter "server_maximum_page_size". This parameter determines the count of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server.
Use "early_listing_stop" for faster listing, when set to true, the value specified in "server_maximum_page_size" is used to display the users/groups. Total number of records will be equal to the number of records requested based on skip and limit values.
If pagination is disabled, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.

Banners.description:
This service is used to get or set the banners of the CipherTrust Manager Server. There are two kind of banners,
the pre-authentication banner, which is shown to a user before the user is authenticated by the
CipherTrust Manager server, and the post-authentication banner, which is shown to a user after the user is
authenticated by the CipherTrust Manager server.

Banner text supports unicode and markdown.

Groups.description:
Users and Clients can be added to Groups.  Users' and Clients' group
membership is available to the authorization system, so policies can
use users' and clients' group membership to assign permissions.

Groups have an `app_metadata` property, which, like the User and Client property, can be
used by applications to store application-specific data about the group.

Groups are identified by their name, which must be unique.

To get a list of users in a group, use the `/users/` endpoint with
a `groups` query parameter to filter by group.  Use `groups=nil` to
list users that are not in any group.

To get a list of groups a user is in, use the `/groups/` endpoint, with
the `users` query parameter to filter by user member.

To get a list of clients in a group, use the `/clients/` endpoint with
a `groups` query parameter to filter by group.  Use `groups=nil` to
list clients that are not in any group.

To get a list of groups a client is in, use the `/groups/` endpoint, with
the `clients` query parameter to filter by client member.

Groupmaps.description:
The keys created by a CipherTrust Manager system can be configured to allow or disallow
certain operations based on the groups a user belongs to. Groupmaps extend configuration
of key permissions to connection groups. For example, an LDAP group can be mapped to the
system defined `KeyUsers` group; this allows all members of the LDAP group to be key users.
Alternately, an LDAP group can be mapped to a non-system defined CipherTrust Manager group.
The mapped CipherTrust Manager group can then be used to configure group-based key permissions.
Groupmaps also allows mapping a group from parent domain to a child domain group. This allows
members of mapped parent domain group to be member of child domain group when they log-in
to child domain.

A groupmap maps a connection name, and a group associated
with that connection, to a CipherTrust Manager group. The `groupmaps` API
can be used to create, delete, get, list, and modify mappings. A mapping is
created by passing the three parameters to the create API. This returns an
ID along with other information. The ID can be used to get, modify or delete
the mapping.

The list API supports searching for all mappings associated with
(a) a connection, (b) a CipherTrust Manager group, and/or (c) a connection group. Wildcards
can be used in the list API.

Tokens.description:
Access Token: API calls are authenticated with access tokens. An access token
is a string representing an authorization issued to the client. It is referred
as an API authentication token.

Refresh Token: Refresh tokens are issued to the client by the authorization server
and are used to obtain a new access token when the current access token becomes
invalid or expires, or to obtain additional access tokens.

The `/auth/tokens/` endpoint can be used to exchange a username and password for an
access token and long lived refresh token that can be used to get access token without
using the user's credential. You can obtain tokens for LDAP users by entering a username
in the format <connection_name>|<username> or by specifying a connection name in the connection field.

To make API calls against the rest of the API, the token value needs
to be placed in the `Authorization` HTTP header, prepended with
`Bearer `.  For example:

    Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJhdWQiOiJkMzEzYzcwZS01NmYyLTQ5MTUtOGJkNy01ZmMyYmUyNzk2YzEiLCJzdWIiOiJsb2NhbHxiM2ZjOGZlNy1hN2ZlLTQ1YzEtOWU1OS0zYmUxNTRkMTZjYmQiLCJpc3MiOiJreWxvIiwiYWNjIjoia3lsbyIsImN1c3QiOnsiZ3JvdXBzIjpbImFkbWluIl19LCJpYXQiOjE0ODEyMjg1NzgsImV4cCI6MTQ4MTIyODg3OH0.2ZCX8qzzU-a499Ef58tDnDcXqrOv8pw_AXD-z-WeEE0

Access tokens expire and so must be refreshed periodically.  A new
access token can be created with the user's credentials, or with the refresh
token that has not been revoked or expired.

The `/auth/revoke` endpoint can be used to revoke the refresh token.

Client-Management/Tokens.description:
These endpoints perform client registration token operations.

It provides methods for managing client registration tokens for
registering new CipherTrust Manager clients.

Client-Management/Clients.description:
These endpoints perform client management operations.

It provides methods for registering new CipherTrust Manager clients and their
management.

To ensure that the Subject DN of a client certificate is unique, use the `do_not_modify_subject_dn` and `subject_dn_field_to_modify` 
parameters while registering and renewing the client certificate.
If `do_not_modify_subject_dn` is set to true, the client does not allow the server to modify Subject DN in the CSR. 
In this case, the client needs to provide a CSR with Subject DN that should be unique on the CipherTrust Manager.
It is highly recommended to set the value of `do_not_modify_subject_dn` parameter to false unless there are constraints preventing modifications in the CSR.
To maintain the uniqueness of the Subject DN of clients across domains, 
the value provided for the `do_not_modify_subject_dn` and `subject_dn_field_to_modify` parameters should be the same for both client registration and renewal.

In case of renewing a client that is issued by an external CA, you need to provide
the new certificate signed by the external CA in the request.
After the client renewal process, the newly issued certificate will have the client id
set as the UID in the DN of the certificate. This is done to ensure that the DN of a client
certificate is unique to each client.

Client-Management/Profiles.description:
The profile APIs allow for managing client profiles. 

A client profile represents data that can be used to create/renew client certificates.

The following operations can be performed:
- Create, Delete or Update profiles.
- List profiles

Crypto.description:
These endpoints perform cryptographic operations.

It provides methods for format preserving encryption (FPE), symmetric and
asymmetric key encryption, hashing and MAC, and digital signatures.

All crypto operations require a key. The hide/unhide operations (FPE)
use a default if no key is specified as a parameter. The hide operation will
auto-create keys if a key name is specified that does not yet exist.

However, all other operations require an existing key. Any of
the key's identifiers (the name, id, or URI) can be used in the
crypto-operation's parameters.

Keys.description:
Keys are the cryptographic material used in crypto operations.

Keys can be symmetric or asymmetric, in various sizes and algorithms.
The crypto endpoints take key identifiers as parameters to specify
which key to use.  If the key is exportable, the key material can
be exported to the caller and used for local encryption.

Keys have a `meta` attribute, which can be used to store
application-specific information.  This is stored for the convenience of
applications using the API. These properties are unstructured JSON
documents: the caller can put any JSON-structured information in them.

Keys have a `label` attribute which can be used to group keys using
key/value pairs. APIs that list keys can use labels to filter the set of
matching resources.

Keys have three additional identifiers: uuid, muid, and keyId.
These identifiers support legacy DSM behaviours and can be used to filter
keys while listing the keys. The identifiers muid and keyid will be returned in
the response of key APIs only if set.

This is an example of a key resource:

    {
      "id": "d22042eb-b527-48fe-b2d6-65fb0c7c3e04",
      "uri": "kylo:kylo:vault:keys:russ2-v0",
      "account": "kylo:kylo:admin:accounts:kylo",
      "application": "ncryptify:gemalto:admin:apps:kylo",
      "devAccount": "ncryptify:gemalto:admin:accounts:gemalto",
      "createdAt": "2016-12-01T19:57:04.884862Z",
      "name": "mykey",
      "updatedAt": "2016-12-01T19:57:04.884862Z",
      "usage": "any",
      "meta": {
        "ownerId": "local|81f34b79-e3c4-4391-a4c9-4bdd85b13f98",
        "permissions": {
          "UseKey": [
            "stars"
          ],
          "ReadKey": [
            "stars"
          ],
          "DecryptWithKey": [
            "stars"
          ],
          "EncryptWithKey": [
            "stars"
          ],
        "customAttributes": [
              {
                "name": "color",
                "value": "blue"
              }
            ],
        }
      },
      "version": 0,
      "algorithm": "AES",
      "size": 256,
      "format": "raw",
      "unexportable": false,
      "undeletable": false,
      "uuid": "64614b84-fd1e-4126-892b-f2a14f4bc025",
      "muid": "64614b84-fd1e-4126-892b-f2a14f4bc025cba2b073-bf22-43a6-8f52-6ccbe882bbe6",
      "labels": { "region": "noram", "team": "sales" }
    }

This key was created via the
NAE-XML interface (rather than the REST interface).  The NAE-XML
interface has added its own properties to `meta`, to help support
legacy behaviors:

`customAttributes`: This property holds name/value pairs set by NAE-XML
    requests.  They map to the `CustomAttributes` element of NAE-XML
    keys.
`permissions`: This property holds a map of actions to user groups.
    CipherTrust Manager's default Policies use this metadata to grant these
    permissions to members of the listed groups.
    If this property is deleted, it is equivalent to clearing all
    group permissions via the NAE-XML interface.
`ownerId`: This property holds a `user_id`.  CipherTrust Manager's default Policies
    grant that user most permissions to the key.  If it is deleted,
    only admins (members of the "admin" group) will have permissions
    to the key.
`global`: This property can be set to JSON `true` or `false`
    (e.g. `"global":true`).  This property marks the key as a "global" key,
    which will allow unauthenticated NAE-XML users some permissions to
    the key.  "Global Users" is a feature specific to the NAE-XML interface,
    and has no equivalent in the REST interface. In addition, support of "global" 
    keys from the NAE/KMIP interfaces will be deprecated in the future releases.
`versionedKey: This property marks the key as an NAE-XML "Versioned Key".
    This property is only used to emulate the behavior of NAE-XML keys.
    Keys are always versioned, but in NAE-XML, a key can either be
    "versioned" or "non-versioned", and versioned keys produce a
    different format of ciphertext.  NAE-XML crypto commands using a
    versioned key produce ciphertext with a header which contains the key's version.  The same NAE-XML
    crypto commands using a *non-versioned* produce ciphertext without
    the header.  The NAE-XML interface layer uses this "versionedKey" property
    to track whether this key should produce the ciphertext headers.  It is
    not recommended you change this, or you will not be able decrypt
    ciphertext created with the key before changing the field.

The REST interface also allows specification of key aliases. Key aliases are used by
KMIP to specify one or more "Name" attributes associated with the key. A key alias
has an alias, an alias-type, and an index. The alias is an alternative name for the key,
and is unique over an account. The allowed alias-types are "string" and "uri". The
index is generated internally, and is unique for each alias in a key. Key aliases
can be specified while creating a key. They can be added, deleted or modified after
creation using the HTTP patch interface. Key aliases can be used for finding keys.
Here is an example of aliases associated with a key:

    "aliases": [
            {
                "alias": "keyalias1",
                "type": "string",
                "index": 0
            },
            {
                "alias": "keyalias2:monk:gemalto:com",
                "type": "uri",
                "index": 1
            }
        ]

CipherTrust Manager's default authorization policies impose a requirement on newly
created keys.  Users in the "admin" group can create any kind of key, but
other users will be required to include an "ownerId" attribute in the
metadata of the key, which must be set to the creating user's own
`user_id`.  This is because, in order to mimic legacy CipherTrust Manager, keys
must have owners.  The `user_id` of the user is *not* the user's login
name.  It's unique identifier the system assigns to the user.

Use the `/auth/principal` endpoint to fetch information about the
current user.  Here's an example response:

    {
      "sub":"local|95a4d02e-2371-422c-bb17-a218ba0375a5",
      // more attributes, omitted here
    }

The `sub` property holds the current user's `user_id`.  To create a
Key which will pass the default authorization policies, include the
following in the body of the `POST /vault/keys` request:

    {
      "meta": {
        "ownerId":"local|95a4d02e-2371-422c-bb17-a218ba0375a5"
      },
      // other key create params, omitted here
    }

If the key create request doesn't contain that stanza, the request will
be denied by the system's policies.

The `key_format_type` property is server generated and is only applicable when the key format is `opaque`. 
As shown below:

    {
      "meta": {
        "key_format_type":"opaque"
      },
      // other params, omitted here
    }

**CTE Specific Keys**

To use a key in CTE policies, certain CTE-specific attributes should be specified in the key meta at the time of key creation.
Here's an example request to create keys for CTE IDT policies:

    {
      "name": "CTEXTSKey",
      "algorithm": "aes",
      "size": 256,
      "undeletable": true,
      "unexportable": false,
      "meta": {
        "ownerId": "local|59ba6797-e5a6-4427-b11c-a5534b5a975e",
        "permissions": {
          "ExportKey": [
            "CTE Clients"
          ],
          "ReadKey": [
            "CTE Clients"
          ]
        },
        "cte": {
          "persistent_on_client": true,
          "encryption_mode": "XTS",
          "cte_versioned": false
        }
      },
      "xts": true,
      "id": "95cc7868-89bf-492b-b868-bbb884a9b379",            
    }      

CTE-specific parameters that should be supplied in the meta field at the time of key creation are listed below.

parent-parameter | parameter | description
--- | --- | ---
meta | permissions | The "ExportKey" and "ReadKey" permissions are required for the "CTE Clients" group.
cte (inside meta) | persistent_on_client | true or false. Set to `true` if the key is to be stored in persistent memory on the client, otherwise, set to `false`.
cte (inside meta) | encryption_mode | Mode can be CBC, CBC_CS1, or XTS. CBC_CS1 and XTS can be supplied only when the "xts" parameter is set to `true`.
cte (inside meta) | cte_versioned | true or false. Set to `true` for keys to be used in LDT policies. Set to `false` for all other types of policies.
 - | unexportable | false. Always keep it set to `false` for CTE policies.
 - | xts | true or false. For use cases such as IDT and device-level protection using Standard policies and for COS policies, set `xts` to `true`.

**Creating Keys Using Templates**

Keys can be created using templates by providing the template id in request. The key parameters which are present in template will be used to
