CTE/File Activity Monitoring.description:
File Activity Monitoring(FAM) encompasses all the necessary information for managing data sources within the Data Security Framework (DSF) platform. 
This information is crucial for ensuring effective oversight and protection of data access activities.

Scheduler.description:
Used for scheduling CCKM synchronization, key rotation, database backup and AWS XKS credential rotation jobs.

**Time Specification**

The time that a job runs is described in the run_at parameter using the cron expression format : "* * * * *". These five values indicate when the job should be executed. They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.

The following table lists the accepted values:

Field Name   |   Mandatory?   |   Allowed Values    |   Allowed special characters
 ----------- |  ------------  |  -----------------  |  ----------------------------
Minute       |     Yes        |  0-59               | * / , -
Hour         |     Yes        |  0-23               | * / , -
Day of month |     Yes        |  1-31               | * / , - ?
Month        |     Yes        |  1-12 or JAN-DEC    | * / , -
Day of week  |     Yes        |  0-6 or SUN-SAT     | * / , - ?


- Month and Day of week field values are case insensitive. For example, "SUN", "Sun", and "sun" are equally accepted.

- Asterisk ( * ) The asterisk indicates that the cron expression will match for all values of the field; e.g., using an asterisk in the 5th field (month) would indicate every month.

- Slash ( / ) Slashes are used to describe increments of ranges. For example 3-59/15 in the 1st field (minutes) would indicate the 3rd minute of the hour and every 15 minutes thereafter.

- Comma ( , ) Commas are used to separate items of a list. For example, using "MON,WED,FRI" in the 5th field (day of week) would mean Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

- Hyphen ( - ) Hyphens are used to define ranges. For example, 9-17 would indicate every hour between 9am and 5pm inclusive, MON-WED would indicate Monday through Wednesday, JAN-JUN would indicate every month from January through June.

- Question mark ( ? ) Question mark can be used instead of (\*) for leaving either day-of-month or day-of-week blank. ( ? ) means no specific value. For example, to run the job every 10th day of the month and not limit the job to a particular day of the week: '\* \* 10 \* ?'.

Notifications.description:
Notifications are sent whenever an alarm is triggered. For example, if an alarm is triggered because an audit record matches a record based alarm configuration then an email notification is sent to every registered email address.

Limitation: only record based alarms send notifications. Built-in alarms, such as `Disk Full`, will not issue notifications.

Note: notifications via email require configuring an SMTP server.

SMTP Servers.description:
An SMTP server must be configured in order to send notifications via email.
Note: only a single SMTP server is supported.

Logs.description:
These endpoints perform system logs related operations. They provide APIs for downloading logs and changing logs level.
There are two types of logs, debug logs and activity logs (further divided into
NAE activity logs, KMIP activity logs, and web activity logs).

Each type of log file can be downloaded separately, or they can be all downloaded together. Both the current and rotated
logs are included. Download returns a gzipped tar file containing log files, certificate and digital signature. An optional
parameter (ca_id) can be provided for signing the downloaded log files. If ca_id is not provided, the default local CA,
i.e., CipherTrust Manager Root CA, signs the downloaded log files.

Downloaded files are placed in a diretory, and the name of the directory is <system-name>_<version>_logs.

BDT.description: The Batch Data Transformation utility (BDT) provides a policy-based data tranformation and re-key service.

BDT/Protection Profiles.description:
A protection profile is an object that contains all the information needed
to perform a cryptographic operation.

BDT/Character Sets.description:
A character set is used with format preserving algorithms. For example when
encrypting a credit card number a user will want the encrypted data to only
contain numbers. The default character sets are "All Digits" and "Alphanumeric"
but a user can choose to create a custom character set by specifying
the range of the characters used.

BDT/Containers.description:
A container can be either a database or a CSV file. It has all the information
needed to access and connect to it (file path, database credentials).

BDT/Policies.description:
A BDT policy contains all the information required to perform a batch operation.
It is composed of a source, a destination and the protection profiles
assigned to each column.

Data Protection.description:
Data protection is a centralized place for all App and Database encryption
configuration. The configuration contains elements such as the key or algorithm
used for an encryption operation. It can be accessed by multiple products from
the CipherTrust Manager platform. This allows a user to use a one product to encrypt
data and another product to decrypt it using the same configuration.

Data Protection/Character Sets.description:
A character set is used with format preserving algorithms. For example when
encrypting a credit card number a user will want the encrypted data to only
contain numbers. The default character sets are "All Digits" and "Alphanumeric"
but a user can choose to create a custom character set by specifying
the range of the characters used.

Note: The character sets are also used in the BDT API.

Data Protection/Protection Policies.description:
A protection policy is an object that contains all the information needed
to perform a cryptographic operation.

Data Protection/DPG Policies.description:
Data Protection Gateway (DPG) protects sensitive data which is transmitted over REST in a JSON
payload based on the configuration defined in its configuration file.

A DPG policy governs the behavior of DPG execution. It contains a set of URLs tied with encryption parameters.

Connection Manager.description:
The Connection Manager can be used to manage connections with third party servers and services such as AWS, Azure, Salesforce, Google CLoud Platform (GCP) Cloud or Luna SA HSM.
These connections allow CipherTrust Manager connectors to access resources needed for cryptographic, key management, or data discovery and classification tasks.

Note that Connection Manager does not include external services which authenticate CipherTrust Manager users. Those services
are managed through the usermgmt/connections endpoints on the Connections section.

The APIs in this section are common to all types of connections, and can be used to perform the following operations:
- List/Search connections
- Delete connections

The APIs for a specific connection type are not presented here. Check for them in the section associated with that specific connection type.

Connection Manager/Akeyless Connections.description:
**Akeyless Connection Manager**

**Overview**  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage secure connections to Akeyless servers in the cloud. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate and communicate with Akeyless through the Akeyless gateway running on CipherTrust Manager.

**Supported Operations**  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an Akeyless connection
- Get an Akeyless connection
- Update an Akeyless connection
- Delete an Akeyless connection
- List all Akeyless connections
- Test an existing Akeyless connection
- Test an Akeyless connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/akeyless/connections

**Authentication / Connection Methods**  
Akeyless connections use Access Key–based authentication with the following credentials:
- `access_key_id`
- `access_key`

The access key is treated as a secret and is securely protected by CipherTrust Manager.

**Create Connection**  
A new Akeyless connection is created by providing a unique connection name, associated products, and Akeyless authentication credentials.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `access_key_id`
- `access_key`

The `akeyless_url` parameter is optional and is typically required for Single Tenant infrastructures, where it specifies the URL used by the CipherTrust Manager gateway to connect to the Akeyless server.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
 {
  "name": "akeyless-connection",
  "cloud_name": "akeyless",
  "products": ["csm"],
  "access_key_id": "example-access-key-id",
  "access_key": "exampleAccessKeySecret",
  "akeyless_url": "https://akeyless.infra.url"
 }
```

**Update Connection**  
An existing Akeyless connection can be updated to modify authentication credentials, the Akeyless server URL, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

**Delete Connection**  
Deleting an Akeyless connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any configurations or workflows depending on the deleted connection must be updated.

**Test Connection**  
Akeyless connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the Akeyless server and communicate through the configured gateway.

Connection Manager/AWS Connections.description:
**AWS Connection Manager**

**Overview**  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage secure connections to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud. These connections are used by CipherTrust Manager products to authenticate with AWS and perform supported cloud operations.

**Supported Operations**  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an AWS connection
- Get an AWS connection
- Update an AWS connection
- Delete an AWS connection
- List all AWS connections
- Test an existing AWS connection
- Test an AWS connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path:  
`/v1/connectionmgmt/services/aws/connections`

**Authentication / Connection Methods**  
The following AWS authentication methods are supported:

**Access Key Authentication**  
Uses AWS IAM credentials consisting of:
- `access_key_id`
- `secret_access_key`

These credentials must have the permissions required for the intended AWS operations.  
Use this method when static IAM credentials are acceptable.

**Certificate-based Authentication (IAM Roles Anywhere)**  
Uses AWS IAM Roles Anywhere with X.509 certificates to obtain temporary credentials.  
This method avoids long-lived access keys and aligns with AWS recommended security best practices.

**Create Connection**  
A new AWS connection is created by providing a unique connection name, cloud name (`aws`), associated products, and authentication details.  
You must configure **either** Access Key Authentication **or** IAM Roles Anywhere authentication.

**Create Connection – Example (Access Key Authentication)**  
```json
{
"name": "aws-accesskey-connection",
"cloud_name": "aws",
"products": ["cckm"],
"access_key_id": "AKIBEXAMPLEID",
"secret_access_key": "exampleSecretAccessKey"
}
```

**Create Connection – Example (IAM Roles Anywhere)**  
```json
{
"name": "aws-roles-anywhere-connection",
"cloud_name": "aws",
"products": ["cckm"],
"is_role_anywhere": true,
"iam_role_anywhere": {
  "anywhere_role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AnywhereRole",
  "profile_arn": "arn:aws:rolesanywhere:us-east-1:123456789012:profile/example-profile",
  "trust_anchor_arn": "arn:aws:rolesanywhere:us-east-1:123456789012:trust-anchor/example-anchor",
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----...-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
}
}
```


**Update Connection**  
An existing AWS connection can be updated to modify authentication details, role configuration, metadata, labels, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

**Delete Connection**  
Deleting an AWS connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

**Test Connection**  
AWS connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with AWS using the provided configuration.

Connection Manager/Azure Connections.description:
**Azure Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to the Microsoft Azure cloud. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager products to authenticate with Azure and perform supported cloud operations.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an Azure connection
- Get an Azure connection
- Update an Azure connection
- Delete an Azure connection
- List all Azure connections
- Test an existing Azure connection
- Test an Azure connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/azure/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Azure connections support the following authentication methods:

**Client Secret Authentication**  
Uses Azure Active Directory application credentials consisting of:
- `client_id`
- `client_secret`
- `tenant_id`

**Certificate-based Authentication**  
Uses an X.509 certificate associated with an Azure Active Directory application.  
This method avoids long-lived client secrets and aligns with Azure security best practices.

**`is_certificate_used` Parameter Definition**  
The `is_certificate_used` parameter allows the user to select Certificate-based authentication instead of Client Secret authentication for an Azure connection.

- When set to `true`, Certificate-based authentication is used.
- When creating a connection with `is_certificate_used` set to `true`, CipherTrust Manager generates a certificate and returns it in the create API response.
- By default, the generated certificate is valid for **2 years**.
- The certificate can be regenerated for an existing Azure connection by setting `is_certificate_used` to `true` in the Update (PATCH) API call.

Create Connection  
A new Azure connection is created by providing a unique connection name, cloud name, associated products, and authentication details.  

For **Client Secret authentication**, the following parameter is also required:
- `client_secret`

For **Certificate-based authentication**, the following parameter must be set:
- `is_certificate_used` set to `true`

**Create Connection – Example (Client Secret Authentication)**  
```json
{
  "name": "azure-connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "cloud_name": "AzureCloud",
  "client_id": "3bf0dbe6-a2c7-431d-9a6f-4843b74c7e12",
  "tenant_id": "3bf0dbe6-a2c7-431d-9a6f-4843b74c7128",
  "client_secret": "exampleClientSecret"
}
```

**Create Connection – Example (Certificate-based Authentication)**  
```json
{
  "name": "azure-cert-connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "cloud_name": "AzureCloud",
  "client_id": "3bf0dbe6-a2c7-431d-9a6f-4843b74c7e12",
  "tenant_id": "3bf0dbe6-a2c7-431d-9a6f-4843b74c7128",
  "is_certificate_used": true
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Azure connection can be updated to modify authentication parameters, certificate settings, endpoint URLs, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Setting `is_certificate_used` to `true` in the Update (PATCH) API call regenerates the certificate for the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting an Azure connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent cloud key management or Azure-integrated workflows must be updated.

Test Connection  
Azure connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with Azure using the configured authentication method.

Connection Manager/Google Connections.description:
**Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage secure connections to the Google Cloud Platform (GCP). These connections are used by CipherTrust Manager products to authenticate with GCP and perform supported cloud operations.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a GCP connection
- Get a GCP connection
- Update a GCP connection
- Delete a GCP connection
- List all GCP connections
- Test an existing GCP connection
- Test a GCP connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/gcp/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
GCP connections currently support **Service Account–based authentication only**.

Authentication is performed using a Google Cloud service account key file provided in JSON format.

Create Connection  
A new GCP connection is created by providing a unique connection name, cloud name (`gcp`), associated products, and service account credentials.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `key_file` (Service account key file content in JSON string format)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "gcp-connection",
  "cloud_name": "gcp",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "key_file": "{\"type\":\"service_account\",\"private_key_id\":\"exampleKeyId\",\"private_key\":\"-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----...-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\",\"client_email\":\"test@some-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"}"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing GCP connection can be updated to modify the service account key file, metadata, labels, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication credentials may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a GCP connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent configurations or workflows using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
GCP connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with GCP using the provided service account credentials.

Connection Manager/Hadoop Connections.description:
**Hadoop (Knox) Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to Hadoop servers.  
Currently, the supported Hadoop connection type is **Apache Knox**, which acts as a secure gateway for Hadoop services.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a Hadoop connection
- Get a Hadoop connection
- Update a Hadoop connection
- Delete a Hadoop connection
- List all Hadoop connections
- Test an existing Hadoop connection
- Test a Hadoop connection without creating it by passing connection parameters
- List all nodes in an existing Hadoop connection
- Add, get, update, or delete a node in an existing Hadoop connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/hadoop/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Hadoop (Knox) connections use username and password–based authentication and communicate with Knox gateway nodes over HTTP or HTTPS.

Create Connection  
A new Hadoop connection is created by providing a unique connection name, service type, authentication credentials, topology, and one or more Knox gateway nodes.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `service` (Currently supported value: `hadoop-knox`)
- `username` (Username for accessing the Knox gateway)
- `password` (Password for accessing the Knox gateway)
- `nodes`
  - `hostname` (Hostname of the Knox gateway node)
  - `port` (Port on which the Knox gateway is listening)
  - `protocol` (Protocol used to communicate with Knox, for example `http` or `https`)

The following node parameters are **optional**:
- `path` (Custom path for the Knox gateway endpoint)
- `server_certificate` (SSL certificate of the Knox gateway, required for TLS communication when using HTTPS)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "knoxConnection",
  "service": "hadoop-knox",
  "products": ["cte", "data discovery"],
  "description": "a description of the connection",
  "username": "user",
  "password": "password",
  "topology": "default",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "hostname": "node1",
      "port": 1234,
      "protocol": "https",
      "server_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }
  ]
}
```

Node Management  
Hadoop connections support managing individual Knox gateway nodes.  
Nodes can be added, retrieved, updated, or deleted for an existing Hadoop connection.

**Add Node**  
Adds a new node to an existing Hadoop connection.

API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/hadoop/connections/{id}/nodes

The following parameters are **mandatory** when adding a node:
- `hostname` (Hostname of the Knox gateway node)
- `port` (Port on which the Knox gateway is listening)
- `protocol` (Protocol used to communicate with Knox, for example `http` or `https`)

The following parameters are **optional**:
- `path` (Custom path for the Knox gateway endpoint)
- `server_certificate` (SSL certificate of the Knox gateway, required for TLS communication when using HTTPS)

**Add Node – Example**  
```json
{
  "hostname": "node1",
  "port": 1234,
  "protocol": "https",
  "server_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
}
```

Update Node  
An existing node can be updated to modify connection details such as port, protocol, path, or server certificate.  
Updating node parameters may require re-validation of the Hadoop connection.

Delete Node  
Deleting a node removes it from the Hadoop connection.  
If the node is in active use, the operation may be restricted based on system validation rules.

Test Connection  
Hadoop connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the Knox gateway and communicate with all configured nodes.

Connection Manager/Luna Network HSM Serv.description:
The APIs in this section deal with Luna Network HSM Servers. These servers will be used when creating a connection
of a Luna Network HSM type. These APIs, currently, support CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager (CCKM) as a product.
The following operations can be performed:
- Create/Delete/Get a Luna Network HSM Server
- List all Luna Network HSM Servers

Connection Manager/Luna Network HSM Conn.description:
**Luna Network HSM Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to a Luna Network Hardware Security Module (HSM).  
A Luna Network HSM connection can be configured as either **HA (High Availability)** or **non-HA**.

- A **non-HA connection** connects to a single partition on an HSM server.
- An **HA connection** connects to multiple partitions across one or more HSM servers to provide high availability and load balancing.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a Luna Network HSM connection
- Get a Luna Network HSM connection
- Update a Luna Network HSM connection
- Delete a Luna Network HSM connection
- List all Luna Network HSM connections
- Test an existing Luna Network HSM connection
- Test a Luna Network HSM connection without creating it by passing connection parameters
- Add, delete partitions in an existing Luna Network HSM connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/luna-network/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Luna Network HSM connections authenticate using a partition password and connect to one or more HSM partitions defined as part of the connection configuration.

Create Connection  
A new Luna Network HSM connection is created by providing a unique connection name, partition details, authentication credentials, and HA configuration.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `password` (Password for accessing the HSM partition)
- `partitions`
  - `hostname` (Hostname or IP address of the HSM server)
  - `partition_label` (Label of the HSM partition)
  - `serial_number` (Serial number of the HSM partition)

The following parameter is optional:
- `is_ha_enabled` (Set to `true` to enable High Availability across multiple partitions)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "luna-network-connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "password": "Password",
  "is_ha_enabled": false,
  "partitions": [
    {
      "hostname": "sample-hostname",
      "partition_label": "sample-label",
      "serial_number": "serialno"
    }
  ]
}
```

Partition Management  
Luna Network HSM connections support managing individual HSM partitions.  
Partitions can be added to or removed from an existing connection.

**Add Partition**  
Adds a new partition to an existing Luna Network HSM connection.

API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/luna-network/connections/{id}/partitions

The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `hostname` (Hostname or IP address of the HSM server)
- `partition_label` (Label of the HSM partition)
- `serial_number` (Serial number of the HSM partition)

**Add Partition – Example**  
```json
{
  "hostname": "new-partition-host",
  "partition_label": "sample-label",
  "serial_number": "serialno"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Luna Network HSM connection can be updated to modify partition details, HA configuration, password, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication or partition parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a Luna Network HSM connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any cryptographic services or key management operations relying on the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
Luna Network HSM connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the configured HSM partitions and perform cryptographic operations.

Connection Manager/SMB Connections.description:
**SMB Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to file shares using the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol.  
The share path (share name) is not stored as part of the connection and must be provided explicitly when testing the connection.

**Note:** Common Internet File System (CIFS) is a dialect of the SMB protocol.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a SMB connection
- Get a SMB connection
- Update a SMB connection
- Delete a SMB connection
- List all SMB connections
- Test an existing SMB connection
- Test a SMB connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/smb/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
SMB connections use username and password–based authentication to access the remote file share.  
Optional domain information can be provided for domain-based authentication.

Create Connection  
A new SMB connection is created by providing a unique connection name, authentication credentials, and target host details.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `username` (Username for accessing the SMB share)
- `password` (Password for accessing the SMB share)

The following parameters are optional and can be provided based on the SMB environment:
- `domain` (Domain name for domain-based authentication)
- `host` (Hostname or IP address of the SMB server)
- `port` (SMB service port, typically `445`)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "smbConnection",
  "description": "a description of the connection",
  "products": ["cte"],
  "username": "user",
  "password": "password",
  "domain": "domainName",
  "host": "1.2.3.4",
  "port": "445"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing SMB connection can be updated to modify authentication credentials, domain, host, port, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a SMB connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any workflows or services using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
SMB connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
The share path (share name) must be provided as part of the test request, as it is not stored with the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the SMB server and access the specified share.

Connection Manager/DSM Connections.description:
**DSM Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage secure connections to a DSM (Data Security Manager) Key Manager. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate with DSM servers and manage cryptographic operations across DSM nodes.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a DSM connection
- Get a DSM connection
- Update a DSM connection
- Delete a DSM connection
- List all DSM connections
- Test an existing DSM connection
- Test a DSM connection without creating it by passing connection parameters
- List all nodes in an existing DSM connection
- Add, get, update, or delete a node in an existing DSM connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/dsm/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
DSM connections use username and password–based authentication along with TLS-secured communication using DSM server certificates.

Create Connection  
A new DSM connection is created by providing a unique connection name, authentication credentials, and one or more DSM nodes.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `username` (Username for accessing the DSM server)
- `password` (Password for accessing the DSM server)
- `nodes`
  - `hostname` (Hostname of the DSM server)
  - `server_certificate` (SSL certificate of the DSM server used for TLS communication)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "dsm-connection",
  "description": "a description of the connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "username": "user",
  "password": "password",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "hostname": "node1",
      "server_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    },
    {
      "hostname": "node2",
      "server_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }
  ]
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing DSM connection can be updated to modify credentials, node details, server certificates, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication credentials or node configuration may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a DSM connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent configurations or workflows using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
DSM connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the DSM server and establish secure communication with all configured nodes.

Connection Manager/External CM Server.description:
The APIs under this section are used for initial setup of external CM connections.
These APIs provide information about the Nodes and Root CAs needed for external CM connections.
The following operations can be performed:
- Create/Delete/Get external CM 
- List all external CMs
- Add/Delete/Get/Update a node in an existing external CM Server
- Add/Delete a CA in an existing external CM Server

Connection Manager/CM Connections.description:
**CipherTrust Manager (CM) Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage secure connections to an external CipherTrust Manager instance. These connections enable communication and trust establishment between CipherTrust Manager systems.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a CM connection
- Get a CM connection
- Update a CM connection
- Delete a CM connection
- List all CM connections
- Test an existing CM connection
- Test CM connection parameters before establishing the connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/cm/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
CM connections use certificate-based authentication with credentials registered on the external CipherTrust Manager.

Create Connection  
A new CM connection is created by providing a unique connection name, associated products, and authentication details for the external CipherTrust Manager.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `client_certificate` (Certificate of the client registered at the external CipherTrust Manager)
- `client_id` (ID of the client registered at the external CipherTrust Manager)
- `external_cm_id` (ID of the external CipherTrust Manager resource that contains the hostname and root CA information)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "cm-connection",
  "description": "a description of the connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "client_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "client_id": "74bfad7c-2385-487e-95fd-8d0346d655d3",
  "external_cm_id": "adb58b03-ceb7-476d-bdcc-d5a8e19a7521"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing CM connection can be updated to modify the client certificate, client ID, description, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating authentication-related parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a CM connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent configurations or trust relationships using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
CM connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate and communicate with the external CipherTrust Manager.

Connection Manager/SCP Connections.description:
**SCP / SFTP Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections used to copy files, such as system backups, to external servers using Secure Copy Protocol (SCP) or Simple File Transfer Protocol (SFTP).

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an SCP/SFTP connection
- Get an SCP/SFTP connection
- Update an SCP/SFTP connection
- Delete an SCP/SFTP connection
- List all SCP/SFTP connections
- Test an existing SCP/SFTP connection
- Test an SCP/SFTP connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/scp/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
SCP/SFTP connections support the following authentication methods:

**Key-based Authentication**  
Uses an SSH key pair for authentication.
- The public key must be downloaded from the `scp/publickey` API.
- The downloaded public key must be added to the destination host’s `authorized_keys` file.

**Password-based Authentication**  
Uses the password of the destination host user account.

In addition, users must provide the **host public key** for server verification.  
The host public key can be obtained from the destination host machine, typically located under `/etc/ssh/`.

Create Connection  
A new SCP/SFTP connection is created by providing a unique connection name, destination host details, authentication parameters, and file transfer settings.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `host` (Hostname or IP address of the destination server)
- `username` (Username on the destination server)
- `auth_method` (Authentication method: `key` or `password`)
- `path_to` (Destination directory path on the remote server)
- `public_key` (Host public key used for server verification)

For **Password-based authentication**, the following parameter is also required:
- `password`

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "scp-connection",
  "description": "a description of the connection",
  "products": ["backup/restore"],
  "host": "1.2.3.4",
  "port": 22,
  "username": "user",
  "auth_method": "Password",
  "password": "password",
  "path_to": "/home/path/to/directory/",
  "protocol": "sftp",
  "public_key": "ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQDNxnOBfBVU4L3fQBVWK71CdoHXmFNxkD0lFYDagM8etytGxRMQeOSeARUYQA+xC/8ig+LHimQ97L0XPSCvTr/XbXxOYBOdGHFqr1o6QwmSBABoPz0fvfCHaipAdwGlfS50aDbCWYZSd9UX6stOazCPdQ9wiiGD0+wYmagxBtrBlzrXiXKV3q+GNr6iIlejsv2aK"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing SCP/SFTP connection can be updated to modify destination host details, authentication parameters, transfer path, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting an SCP/SFTP connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any backup or file transfer workflows using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
SCP/SFTP connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with the destination server and access the configured path.

Connection Manager/Salesforce Connection.description:
**Salesforce Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to the Salesforce cloud. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate with Salesforce and perform supported cloud operations.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a Salesforce connection
- Get a Salesforce connection
- Update a Salesforce connection
- Delete a Salesforce connection
- List all Salesforce connections
- Test an existing Salesforce connection
- Test a Salesforce connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/salesforce/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Salesforce connections support the following authentication methods:

**Client Credentials Authentication**  
Uses Salesforce connected app credentials consisting of:
- `client_id`
- `client_secret`
- `username`
- `password`

**Certificate-based Authentication**  
Uses a certificate along with:
- `client_id`
- `username` or `domain_name`

When a connection is created using certificate-based authentication:
- CipherTrust Manager generates a certificate and returns it in the response.
- The generated certificate must be uploaded to the Salesforce server for authentication to succeed.

Create Connection  
A new Salesforce connection is created by providing a unique connection name, Salesforce cloud name, associated products, and authentication details.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `cloud_name`
- `client_id`

For **Client Credentials authentication**, the following parameters are also required:
- `client_secret`
- `username`
- `password`

For **Certificate-based authentication**, the following parameters are required:
- `username` or `domain_name`
- `is_certificate_used` set to `true`

**Create Connection – Example (Client Credentials Authentication)**  
```json
{
  "name": "salesforce-connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "cloud_name": "Salesforce Sandbox Cloud",
  "client_id": "3bf0dbe6-a2c7-431d-9a6f-4843b74c7e12",
  "client_secret": "exampleClientSecret",
  "username": "xyz@abc.com",
  "password": "123456",
  "is_certificate_used": false
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Salesforce connection can be updated to modify authentication parameters, certificate settings, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication-related fields may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a Salesforce connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent cloud key management configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
Salesforce connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with Salesforce using the provided configuration.

Connection Manager/SAP Data Custodian Co.description:
**SAP Data Custodian Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to SAP Data Custodian. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate with SAP Data Custodian and perform supported key management operations.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a SAP Data Custodian connection (Standard User or Technical User)
- Get a SAP Data Custodian connection
- Update a SAP Data Custodian connection
- Delete a SAP Data Custodian connection
- List all SAP Data Custodian connections
- Test an existing SAP Data Custodian connection
- Test a SAP Data Custodian connection without creating it by passing connection parameters

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/sap-dc/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
SAP Data Custodian connections support two authentication methods:

**Standard User Authentication**  
Uses standard SAP user credentials consisting of:
- `tenant`
- `user`
- `secret`

**Technical User Authentication**  
Uses technical user credentials consisting of:
- `api_key`
- `secret`

For Technical User authentication:
- Creating the connection activates the technical user and stores the updated secret.
- The stored, activated secret is used for subsequent connection tests.
- When testing a Technical User connection without creating it first, the activated secret must be provided, as activation occurs only during connection creation.

Create Connection  
A new SAP Data Custodian connection is created by providing a unique connection name, API endpoint, associated products, and authentication credentials.  

The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `api_endpoint`

For **Standard User authentication**, the following parameters are required:
- `user_credentials.tenant`
- `user_credentials.user`
- `user_credentials.secret`

For **Technical User authentication**, the following parameters are required:
- `technical_user_credentials.api_key`
- `technical_user_credentials.secret`

**Create Connection – Example (Standard User Authentication)**  
```json
{
  "name": "sap-data-custodian",
  "description": "SAP DC connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "api_endpoint": "https://demo-kms-endpoint/kms/v2",
  "user_credentials": {
    "tenant": "tenant",
    "user": "username",
    "secret": "secret"
  }
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing SAP Data Custodian connection can be updated to modify authentication credentials, API endpoint, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a SAP Data Custodian connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent cloud key management configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
SAP Data Custodian connections can be tested either after creation or by directly passing connection parameters without creating the connection.  
For Technical User authentication, testing without creating the connection requires the activated secret obtained during connection creation.

Connection Manager/Oracle Connections.description:
**Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate with OCI and perform supported cloud key management operations.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an OCI connection
- Get an OCI connection
- Update an OCI connection
- Delete an OCI connection
- List all OCI connections
- Test an existing OCI connection
- Test OCI connection parameters before establishing the connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/oci/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
OCI connections use API signing–based authentication with OCI user credentials.  
Authentication is performed using an OCI user OCID, tenancy OCID, region, API key fingerprint, and a private key.

Create Connection  
A new OCI connection is created by providing a unique connection name, associated products, and OCI authentication details.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `user_ocid` (OCID of the OCI user)
- `tenancy_ocid` (OCID of the OCI tenancy)
- `fingerprint` (Fingerprint of the OCI API signing key)
- `region` (OCI region identifier)
- `credentials.key_file` (Private key used for OCI API signing)

The following parameter is **optional**:
- `credentials.pass_phrase` (Passphrase for the private key, if applicable)

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "oci-connection",
  "description": "OCI Connection",
  "products": ["cckm"],
  "user_ocid": "ocid1.user.oc1..exampleuserocid",
  "tenancy_ocid": "ocid1.tenancy.oc1..exampletenancyocid",
  "fingerprint": "c4:a9:89:47:21:11:11:ac:c4:a9:89:47:21:31:9e",
  "region": "ap-sydney-1",
  "credentials": {
    "key_file": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----...-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----",
    "pass_phrase": "password"
  }
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing OCI connection can be updated to modify authentication credentials, region, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting an OCI connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any dependent cloud key management configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
OCI connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can authenticate with OCI using the provided credentials and region.

Connection Manager/OIDC Connections.description:
**OIDC Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to an Identity Provider (IdP) that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) specifications. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate users using an external OIDC-compliant identity provider.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an OIDC connection
- Get an OIDC connection
- Update an OIDC connection
- List all OIDC connections
- Delete an OIDC connection

Deletion of an in-use OIDC connection is restricted.  
To delete an in-use connection, the delete operation must be performed with the `force` flag explicitly set.

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/oidc/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
OIDC connections use client-based authentication with credentials issued by the OIDC Identity Provider.

Create Connection  
A new OIDC connection is created by providing a unique connection name, OIDC provider endpoint details, and client credentials.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `url` (OIDC provider base URL)
- `client_id` (Client identifier registered with the OIDC provider)
- `client_secret` (Client secret issued by the OIDC provider)

During create and update operations, a SHA256 checksum value is generated using the `client_secret` and `url`, and is returned in the API response.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "oidc-connection",
  "description": "OIDC Connection",
  "products": ["cte"],
  "client_id": "js7sjn-4jas98-fo2rm13-94ne5t",
  "url": "https://www.oidc-test-connection.com",
  "client_secret": "exampleClientSecret"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing OIDC connection can be updated to modify client credentials, provider URL, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating authentication parameters results in regeneration of the SHA256 checksum returned in the response.

Delete Connection  
An OIDC connection that is currently in use cannot be deleted by default.  
To delete an in-use connection, the delete operation must be executed with the `force` flag set to true.

Connection Manager/LDAP Connections.description:
**LDAP Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to an Identity Provider (IdP) that supports LDAP specifications. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to authenticate users and groups using an external LDAP directory.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an LDAP connection
- Get an LDAP connection
- Update an LDAP connection
- Delete an LDAP connection
- List all LDAP connections
- Test an existing LDAP connection
- Test LDAP connection parameters before establishing the connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/ldap/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
LDAP connections use bind-based authentication to communicate with the LDAP server.  
Communication can be secured using TLS, and additional LDAP query parameters can be configured to control user and group resolution.

Create Connection  
A new LDAP connection is created by providing a unique connection name, LDAP server details, bind credentials, and directory configuration.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `server_url` (LDAP server URL, for example `ldap://host:389` or `ldaps://host:636`)
- `bind_dn` (Distinguished Name used to bind to the LDAP server)
- `bind_password` (Password for the bind DN)

Additional parameters can be configured to define search behavior, user and group attributes, paging behavior, and TLS settings.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "ldap-connection",
  "description": "LDAP Connection",
  "products": ["cte"],
  "server_url": "ldap://172.27.0.6:389",
  "bind_dn": "cn=admin,dc=planetexpress,dc=com",
  "bind_password": "GoodNewsEveryone",
  "base_dn": "dc=planetexpress,dc=com",
  "search_filter": "(objectclass=User)",
  "user_login_attribute": "uid",
  "group_base_dn": "ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com",
  "group_filter": "(objectclass=Group)",
  "group_name_attribute": "groupFriendlyName",
  "user_dn_attribute": "dn",
  "group_id_attribute": "cn",
  "group_member_field": "member"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing LDAP connection can be updated to modify bind credentials, server configuration, search filters, directory attributes, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating authentication or directory parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting an LDAP connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any authentication or authorization configurations depending on the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
LDAP connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can bind to the LDAP server and resolve users and groups using the configured settings.

Connection Manager/Elasticsearch Connect.description:
**Elasticsearch Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to an Elasticsearch log forwarder. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to forward logs securely to an Elasticsearch endpoint.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create an Elasticsearch connection
- Get an Elasticsearch connection
- Update an Elasticsearch connection
- Delete an Elasticsearch connection
- List all Elasticsearch connections
- Test an existing Elasticsearch connection
- Test Elasticsearch connection parameters before establishing the connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/log-forwarders/elasticsearch/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Elasticsearch connections are configured using network and transport parameters.  
Optional authentication and TLS parameters can be provided through Elasticsearch connection settings.

Create Connection  
A new Elasticsearch connection is created by providing a unique connection name, target host and port, and optional transport and security parameters.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `host`
- `port`

Optional parameters can be provided under `elasticsearch_params` to configure transport protocol, authentication, and TLS behavior.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "elasticsearch-connection",
  "description": "Elasticsearch Connection",
  "products": ["logger"],
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 5321,
  "elasticsearch_params": {
    "transport": "tcp"
  }
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Elasticsearch connection can be updated to modify the host, port, transport configuration, authentication parameters, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating connection parameters may require re-validation.

Delete Connection  
Deleting an Elasticsearch connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any log forwarding configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
Elasticsearch connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can connect to the Elasticsearch endpoint using the configured settings.

Connection Manager/Loki Connections.description:
**Loki Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to a Loki log forwarder. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to forward logs to a Loki endpoint for centralized log aggregation and analysis.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a Loki connection
- Get a Loki connection
- Update a Loki connection
- Delete a Loki connection
- List all Loki connections
- Test an existing Loki connection
- Test Loki connection parameters before establishing the connection

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/log-forwarders/loki/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Loki connections are configured using network and transport parameters.  
Optional HTTP authentication and TLS-related settings can be provided through Loki connection parameters.

Create Connection  
A new Loki connection is created by providing a unique connection name, target endpoint details, and optional transport and security parameters.  
The following parameter is **mandatory**:
- `host`
- `port`

Other parameters such as host, transport protocol, and authentication settings can be configured based on the Loki deployment.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "loki-connection",
  "description": "Loki Connection",
  "products": ["logger"],
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 5321,
  "loki_params": {
    "transport": "tcp"
  }
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Loki connection can be updated to modify endpoint details, transport configuration, authentication parameters, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating connection parameters may require re-validation.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a Loki connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any log forwarding configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
Loki connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can connect to the Loki endpoint using the configured settings.

Connection Manager/Syslog Connections.description:
**Syslog Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage Syslog log forwarder connections. These connections enable CipherTrust Manager to forward logs to an external Syslog server for centralized logging and monitoring.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a Syslog connection
- Get a Syslog connection
- Update a Syslog connection
- Delete a Syslog connection
- List all Syslog connections
- Test an existing Syslog connection
- Test Syslog connection parameters before establishing the connection.

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/log-forwarders/syslog/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
Syslog connections are configured using network and transport parameters.  
Secure communication can be enabled using TLS by providing a trusted CA certificate.

Create Connection  
A new Syslog connection is created by providing a unique connection name, destination host details, and Syslog transport configuration.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `host` (Hostname or IP address of the Syslog server)
- `port` (Port on which the Syslog server is listening)
- `syslog_params.transport` (Transport protocol, for example `TCP`, `UDP`, or `TLS`)

Additional parameters such as message format and CA certificate can be configured based on the Syslog server setup.

**Note**  
Testing a Syslog connection using the `UDP` transport protocol is **not supported**.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "syslog-connection",
  "description": "Syslog Connection",
  "products": ["logger"],
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 514,
  "syslog_params": {
    "transport": "TLS",
    "message_format": "rfc3164",
    "ca_cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIID...example...CERTIFICATE\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
  }
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing Syslog connection can be updated to modify destination host details, transport configuration, TLS settings, message format, metadata, description, or associated products.  
Updating transport or security parameters may require re-validation of the connection.

Delete Connection  
Deleting a Syslog connection permanently removes it from CipherTrust Manager.  
Any log forwarding configurations using the deleted connection must be updated.

Test Connection  
Syslog connections can be tested either after creation or by validating the connection parameters before establishing the connection.  
A successful test confirms that CipherTrust Manager can connect to the Syslog server using the configured transport and settings.

Connection Manager/CSR Creation.description:
The API in this section creates a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) that can be used in a connection (eg: Azure, Salesforce) in CipherTrust Manager.

The corresponding private key is stored securely on the CipherTrust Manager. The user can get the CSR signed using the external PKI.            
If the private key remains unused by a connection after 24 hours of creation, it gets deleted automatically.

Connection Manager/CC Connections.description:
**Confidential Computing (CC) Connection Manager**

Overview  
The APIs in this section allow CipherTrust Manager to create and manage connections to an attestation authority that supports Confidential Computing (CC) specifications. These connections are used to validate and interact with CC-enabled environments.

Supported Operations  
The following operations can be performed:
- Create a CC connection
- Get a CC connection
- Update a CC connection
- Delete a CC connection
- List all CC connections

Base API Path  
/v1/connectionmgmt/services/confidential-computing/connections

Authentication / Connection Methods  
CC connections use secret-based authentication with the following mandatory parameters:
- `client_secret`
- `url`

An optional `base_url` can be provided to define a base endpoint for the attestation authority.

Create Connection  
A new CC connection is created by providing a unique connection name, associated products, and connection details.  
The following parameters are **mandatory**:
- `name`
- `client_secret`
- `url`

During create and update operations, a SHA256 checksum value is generated using the `client_secret` along with the URL (or base URL, if provided) and returned in the API response.

**Create Connection – Example**  
```json
{
  "name": "cc-connection",
  "description": "CC Connection",
  "products": ["cte"],
  "url": "https://www.cc-test-connection.com",
  "base_url": "https://www.cc-test-base-connection.com",
  "client_secret": "exampleClientSecret"
}
```

Update Connection  
An existing CC connection can be updated to modify the client secret, URLs, description, metadata, or associated products.  
Updating connection parameters results in regeneration of the SHA256 checksum returned in the response.

Delete Connection  
A CC connection that is currently in use cannot be deleted by default.  
To delete an in-use connection, the delete operation must be performed with the `force` flag explicitly set.

Test Connection  
CC connections can be validated by creating or updating the connection and verifying successful communication with the configured attestation authority.

CCKM.description:
CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager (CCKM) centralizes the management of key life cycle for various cloud services providers.

CCKM complies with data security mandates in cloud storage environments while retaining the custodianship of the encryption keys.
Enterprises can back up keys on-premise, destroy keys when no longer needed, and manage the entire life cycle of the cloud keys.

CCKM/AWS Custom Key Stores.description:
CCKM provides APIs for integrating Custom Key Stores proxy service for Amazon Web Services. 
Custom Key Stores include External Key Store (XKS) and CloudHSM Key Store.

Custom Key Store of type `AWS_CLOUDHSM` would have keys backed by CloudHSM cluster in AWS.
Custom Key Store of type `EXTERNAL_KEY_STORE` could have keys from Luna HSM or CipherTrust Manager.

Use the APIs in this section to perform following operations:
1. Operations common to both key store types: 
  - Create, list, get, update and delete custom key stores.
  - Connect and disconnect to a custom key stores.
  - Synchronizes AWS custom key stores, get status of synchronization job, cancel a synchronization job.

2. Operations exclusive to external key store: 
  - Block and unblock access.
  - Rotate credential.
  - List and get credentials.
  - Link local external key store with AWS.

3. Operations exclusive to CloudhSM key store: 
  - Get list of unused CloudHSM clusters (that are not already associated with a CloudHSM key store).

4. Operations exclusive to HYOK keys:
  - Create an AWS HYOK key in a external key store.
  - Create, list, and get virtual keys and their versions.
  - Link an unlinked HYOK key.
  - List versions of an AWS HYOK key.
  - Block and unblock HYOK key access.

5. Operations exclusive to CloudHSM keys:
  - Create key in a CloudHSM key store.

CCKM/AWSKeys.description:
CCKM provides the key management and storage for Amazon Web Services.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Perform tasks such as creating, deleting, and uploading keys on AWS.
- Synchronize AWS keys.
- Update key parameters such as add-alias, add-tags, and description.
- Schedule key rotation.

CCKM/AzureKeys.description:
CCKM provides the key management and storage for Microsoft Azure.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Perform tasks such as creating, deleting, uploading, and restoring keys on Azure.
- Synchronize Azure keys.
- Update key parameters such as attributes and key_ops.
- Schedule key rotation.

CCKM/AWSKms.description:
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is used to create and manage keys.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- List and add the AWS accounts and regions based on the connections.
- Get, delete, and update the AWS KMS account.
- Grant permissions to CCKM users to perform specific actions on the AWS KMS.

CCKM/AzureVaults.description:
Azure Key Vault is a tool for securely storing and accessing keys.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Get the list of Azure vaults based on Azure subscriptions.
- Add, delete, and update Azure vaults from the CCKM.
- Create a vault on Azure.
- Grant permissions to CCKM users to perform specific actions on the Azure vaults.

CCKM/AzureSubscriptions.description:
A Microsoft Azure subscription grants you access to the Azure services.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Fetch Azure subscriptions based on the connection.
- Get, list, and delete subscriptions from the CCKM.

CCKM/AWSReports.description:
AWS reports deal with creating various types of reports based on:
- The key activities in AWS
- Which applications are using which keys in AWS
- Reconcile Key activities between Cloud Key Manager and AWS

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Get, delete Report Jobs.
- Generate Reports based on report_type.
- Get, list, and check the status of the report.

CCKM/AzureReports.description:
Azure reports deal with creating various types of reports based on:
- The key activities in Azure
- Which applications are using which keys in Azure
- Reconcile Key activities between Cloud Key Manager and Azure

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Get, delete Report Jobs.
- Generate Reports based on report_type.
- Get, list, and check the status of the report.

CCKM/Google Cloud EKM.description: For managing EKM endpoints that do not reside in a cryptospace, a user must belong to CCKM Admin group and Key User group to perform any operation (create ekm, list ekm, get ekm, update ekm, delete ekm, get policy, update policy, rotate ekm, enable ekm, and disable ekm).

CCKM/Google Cloud EKM CryptoSpaces.description: For managing EKM endpoints that reside in a cryptospace, ensure to configure appropriate ACLs within the Google Cloud project in CCKM after giving appropriate permissions to a user or custom group. Refer admin guide for permission details.

CCKM/HSMLunaPartitions.description:
This section manages the Luna HSM partitions which has its own data, access controls, security policies, and separate administration access for at least some roles, independent of other HSM Luna partitions (if your HSM supports more than one). It could be single partition or group of partition which form a HA group.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Add, list, and update Luna HSM partitions
- View details of Luna HSM partitions
- Grant permissions to users or groups to perform specific actions on the Luna HSM partitions
- Delete Luna HSM partitions

CCKM/HSMLunaKeys.description:
CCKM provides the key management and storage for Luna HSM Keys.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Create Luna HSM keys based on different cryptographic algorithms
- List, update, replicate, and delete Luna HSM keys on CCKM
- View details of Luna HSM keys
- Delete keys from Luna HSM
- Refresh keys from Luna HSM partitions, view the status of key refresh from partitions, view the details of a key refresh process, and cancel a key refresh process
- Synchronize Luna HSM keys from partitions in CCKM, view the status of key synchronizations, view the details of a synchronization process, and cancel a synchronization process

CCKM/SFDC Cache Only Key Endpoints.description:
CCKM provides keys on demand for Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption's Cache-Only Key Service.

Use the APIs in this section to:
- Create and list SFDC Cache-Only Key endpoints for Salesforce to fetch Cache-Only keys.
- Return details for an SFDC Cache-Only Key endpoint
- Update base hostname and password authentication details for an SFDC Cache-Only Key endpoint
- Delete an SFDC Cache-Only Key endpoint

DNS Hosts.description:
The DNS Hosts API is used to add DNS entries to CipherTrust Manager. DNS names are unique.
Multiple IP addresses can be assigned to a single hostname and vice versa. While specifying a hostname, it is required to define the 
corresponding IP address(es). The CipherTrust Manager directly connects to this IP address whenever its hostname is specified for any outbound 
connection such as SMTP and Syslog Server.
The **type** field has been added. Possible values are:
- **address** (default):
    Supports domain redirection. For example, if a DNS entry for the domain `example.com` exists with an IP address, the subdomain `abc.example.com` 
    will also be redirected to the same IP as defined for the `example.com`. For entries with multiple IPs, round-robin is not supported. 
    For example, if a DNS record is created with multiple IPs and type address, only a specific IP will be returned every time at the domain 
    name resolution process.

- **host-record**:
    Supports round-robin over multiple IPs, but doesn't support domain redirection. 
    Therefore, the resolution only takes place when there's an exact match for the specified hostname.

Either of the values can be used at a time. Currently, local DNS-Host entries are not resolved while configuring SNMP and NTP server.

Migration Split Keys.description:
The DSM (Data Security Management) product uses these type of keys for protecting its exported backups.
The CipherTrust Manager uses these keys for decrypting backups uploaded from the DSM.

These keys are split keys. That is, a single key is split into many shares.
A minimum number of shares is required to reassemble the key.
The APIs in this section can be used for CRUD operations on these keys.
The APIs also provide methods for adding, modifying and deleting shares associated with these keys.

Proxy.description:
The proxy API is used to set the proxy in the system. The API also provides an option to input a CA certificate to trust by the system.
A system restart is required after adding new or changing proxy settings.The following operations can be performed:
- Set Proxy(http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy, certificate)
- Update Proxy
- Get proxy
- Delete proxy

Quorum.description:
Quorum is a functionality where an administrator can configure a system that requires a number of
approvers to approve an operation before it can be successfully executed.

A quorum or a quorum request can have one of these six states: pre-active, active, approved, denied, executed, expired.

When user initiates an operation, which is configured by the administrator to require a quorum, it is denied
and leads to a creation of a quorum request. In case a quorum already exists for the same operation, the status
of the existing quorum is used to determine the outcome of the operation.

A new quorum created is in a 'pre-active' state. The user or requester of this quorum must activate the quorum
before any of the approvers can review the quorum request. The requestor can optionally add a reason or
motivation for initiating the request while activating it. Once activated, the quorum is set to an 'active'
state and is now available for other approvers to review it. A quorum in 'pre-active' state is prone to an
expedited expiry.

Any approver can vote to approve or deny a quorum request. A note can be added for additional information.

  - When the required amount of approvals are met, the quorum is set to an 'approved' state
  and any user requesting the operation again would succeed.
  - A deny vote forces the quorum into a 'denied' state suggesting that the operation should not be performed
and the quorum is terminated.

A quorum request is set to an 'executed' state if the operation has been successfully completed with an approved quorum.

Every quorum after a defined time limit is expired and this leads to the termination of that quorum.

The APIs listed in this section can be used to perform the following operations:

1. List/Search Quorums

2. Activate Quorum

3. Delete Quorum

4. Approve Quorum

5. Deny Quorum

6. Revoke vote

7. List Resources of the Quorum 

Quorum Configuration:

A quorum configuration consists of two parts: a quorum profile and a quorum policy.

A quorum profile consists of the following configurations:

1. User groups that can vote

2. Number of approvals required

3. Expiration period of a quorum

A quorum policy consists of actions/operations and a quorum profile.
The quorum created as a result of this quorum policy uses the configuration parameters mentioned
in the profile attached to it.

Note:

1. Quorum profiles and quorum policies cannot be created. A predefined set of profiles are provided and
consequently a set of policies can be activated associated with the profiles.
2. Default operations supported for quorum policies:

   1. DeleteKey
   2. AddUserToGroup
   3. ManagePolicyAttachment
   4. DeletePolicy
   5. DeleteDomain
   6. DownloadBackupKeyDomain
   7. RestoreBackupDomain
   8. DownloadBackupkey (Only Root Domain)
   9. RestoreBackup (Only Root Domain)
   10. DeleteEKMEndpoint for deleting EKM Endpoints
   11. DeleteClientCTE for deleting CTE Client
   12. DeleteClientGroupCTE for deleting CTE Client-Group
   13. DeleteGuardPointCTE for deleting CTE Guard-Point
   14. UpdatePolicyCTE for updating CTE Policies Operations including (key, LDT, IDT, DataTx and Security Rules)
   15. UpdateClientGroupCTE for updating CTE Client-Group
   16. DeleteGoogleWorkspaceCSEEndpoint for deleting Google Workspace CSE endpoint.
   17. UpdateQuorumProfile for updating the quorom policies.

If a Quorum is enabled for DeletePolicy and ManagePolicyAttachment(together), the activation and deactivation of 
Quorum for any supported operation has to go through the Quorum's approval process. This also applies to any other 
user policy in the CipherTrust Manager i.e. If a Quorum is enabled for DeletePolicy and ManagePolicyAttachment, no 
access control policy can be activated without going through Quorum's approval process.

Identity Providers.description:
The CipherTrust Manager allows configuration of external identity
providers with the use of "connections" of certain strategy.

Available external identity providers:

- OpenID Connect (oidc)

Other external identity providers may be added in the future.

Log Forwarders.description:
Audit records and activity logs can optionally be sent to one or more
external log forwarder. By default these logs are stored in the local
database and/or local disk and will continue to do so even if log
forwarders are configured. Each log record will be sent to each
configured log forwarder.

In a multi-node clustered environment the log forwarders configuration
will be automatically synchronized and each node will be aware of all log
forwarders. The log forwarder message will be sent from the currently
active node. This means that if an event that results in a log record is
performed on node 1 the log record will originate from node 1, in a
similar manner if a log record is performed on node 2 the log record will
in this case originate from node 2.

Prometheus Metrics.description:
The CipherTrust Manager (CM) exports metrics that can be collected and viewed by a
Prometheus monitoring system (see https://prometheus.io/).
The CM provides API tokens for Prometheus metrics monitoring clients.
The API tokens can be created by an administrator and passed on to the
Prometheus monitoring clients. The API tokens don't expire.
An API token is returned when Prometheus metrics are enabled, or when the status is obtained.
The API token can be renewed.

Root of Trust Keys.description:
Root of Trust (RoT) key is the root key for encrypting/decrypting secrets or Master Key Encryption Keys (MKEKs) which are then used to
encrypt/decrypt secrets. These set of APIs can manage the life cycle and rotate root of trust keys.

The following operations can be performed on root of trust keys:
- List RoT keys: Lists root of trust keys.
- Get RoT key: Gets root of trust key (with given ID/name)
- Rotate RoT key: Rotates the root of trust key to a new one (optionally with a given ID/name).
- Delete RoT Key: Deletes the root of trust key (with given ID/name).

Loki Configuration.description: CipherTrust Manager uses Loki (see https://grafana.com/oss/loki/) to aggregate information for records.

Akeyless Configuration.description:
The CipherTrust Manager (CM) uses the Akeyless cloud server for secrets management.
The CM communicates with the Akeyless cloud server via the Akeyless gateway.
The Akeyless configuration specifies an existing Akeyless connection whose access key-id and access key
are used by the Akeyless gateway. 
CM also provides the option to use any other akeyless infrastructure apart from the default SAAS server. This functionality can be leveraged in cases where a dedicated akeyless single-tenant environment is in place.

**Single Sign On (SSO)**

The CipherTrust Manager also allows its users to configure a single sign on (SSO) flow, 
which creates a session for a CM user on Akeyless console. The CM's JWT can be exchanged for an akeyless token and 
after some basic configurations, a CM user can make use of the Secrets Management tile on UI and perform operations on CSM console. 

**Customer Fragment**

The CipherTrust Manager allows for the use of a customer fragment to encrypt Akeyless Vault Platform secrets. This fragment is a secret object
which can be used to create a protection key which is used to encrypt and decrypt akeyless secrets. As Akeyless Vault Platform cannot access 
the CM's customer fragment or construct the full encryption key, Akeyless has no access to any secrets material. The CipherTrust Manager 
customer fragment is protected by the same root of trust key hierarchy that protects all keys originating from CipherTrust Manager.
The CM also allows a user to create multiple customer fragments, all being protected by the same ROT. These fragments can be used on akeyless console to create protection keys. Creating or Deleting a fragment automatically adds/removes it from the configs. This operation also restarts the akeyless gateway across all nodes.

Trusted CA Certificates.description:
The trusted CA Certificate API can be used to configure trusted CA certificates for a service. The following operations can be performed:
- Add a trusted CA certificate
- List trusted CA certificates
- Delete a trusted CA certificate

Products.description:
The APIs provided in this section are meant to be used to enable or disable a product's functionality in CipherTrust manager.
- Disabling a product stops the services ( except core services ) that support functionality of a product.
- Enabling a product starts the services required to support the functionality of product.
- NOTE : As of now we support this feature for CSM (CipherTrust Secrets Management) only.
